### E005-F001-S001-T001-A001 — A001-MODEL Data Model Enhancements

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** Multi-CLI Engine Support
> **Feature:** Data Model Enhancements for Multi-Provider Support
> **Story:** Define Core Provider and Model Types
> **Task:** Implement AIProvider, AIModel, ModelTier, and DirectorySource Types

#### Problem Statement
The Session model currently lacks provider and model association fields needed for multi-CLI support. Without these, the harness cannot determine which CLI adapter to use, which model-specific CLI flags to pass, or which provider branding to display. This atom creates the type-safe foundation for the entire multi-engine architecture.

#### Description
Add AIProvider enum (anthropic, openai, google, community), AIModel struct with full metadata (context window, costs, capabilities), ModelTier enum (flagship, balanced, fast), DirectorySource enum (browse, clone, create), and AIModelRegistry static lookup. Extend Session model with provider and modelId fields. Add database migration v7 for new columns.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Define AIProvider enum with cases: anthropic, openai, google, community
- Define AIProvider computed properties: displayName, brandColor, logoAssetName, fallbackSymbol, engineType, cliBinary, supportsHooks, hookEventCount
- Define ModelTier enum with cases: flagship, balanced, fast
- Define ModelTier computed properties: displayName, icon, badgeColor, costMultiplier
- Define AIModel struct with fields: id, name, provider, tier, contextWindow, isDefault, releaseDate, deprecationDate, inputCostPerMillion, outputCostPerMillion, maxOutputTokens, supportsVision, supportsToolUse, cliFlags
- Define AIModel computed properties: contextWindowFormatted, isDeprecated, fullDisplayName
- Define AIModelRegistry enum with static model arrays and lookup methods
- Define DirectorySource enum with cases: browse, clone, create
- Extend Session struct with provider and modelId stored properties
- Extend Session struct with model and modelCliFlags computed properties
- Create database migration v7 adding provider and model_id columns to sessions table
- Create idx_sessions_provider index for filtering by provider
- Backfill existing sessions based on engine_type column

**Out of Scope:**
- Runtime model switching during active session (deferred to F009)
- Model cost estimation and billing integration
- Dynamic model registry fetching from provider APIs (deferred to F006)
- Model capability detection at runtime
- Provider authentication and credential management

#### Functional Requirements
1. AIProvider.engineType returns the correct EngineType for adapter routing
1. AIProvider.cliBinary returns the correct CLI binary name for each provider
1. AIModelRegistry.defaultModel(for:) returns the provider default model
1. AIModelRegistry.model(byId:) performs O(1) lookup on model ID string
1. Session.model resolves to AIModel from registry using session.modelId
1. Session.modelCliFlags returns empty array if model not found
1. Migration v7 adds provider column with NOT NULL DEFAULT anthropic
1. Migration v7 adds model_id column with NOT NULL DEFAULT claude-sonnet-4-5-20251101
1. Migration v7 creates idx_sessions_provider index
1. Migration v7 backfills provider from engine_type for existing sessions

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- All enum rawValues must be lowercase for JSON serialization consistency
- All types must conform to Sendable for Swift 6 concurrency safety
- Registry lookup must be O(n) or better where n is total model count
- Memory footprint of static registry must not exceed 10KB

| E005-F001-S001-T002-A001 | Git Clone Backend Implementation | planned | must | medium |

### E005-F001-S001-T002-A001 — Git Clone Backend Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 2.0 days

> **Epic:** Session Creation and Project Onboarding
> **Feature:** Git Repository Integration
> **Story:** Clone Repository from URL
> **Task:** Implement Git Clone Core Logic

#### Problem Statement
Users currently can only browse existing local directories when creating sessions. There is no way to clone a remote Git repository directly from within the app, forcing users to switch to Terminal, clone manually, then return to Blaze to browse the cloned directory. This breaks workflow continuity and adds friction to the onboarding experience for new projects.

#### Description
Implement the core GitWorktreeManager.cloneRepository(url:destination:shallow:progress:) method that spawns git clone as a child process, parses stderr for progress updates, handles authentication failures gracefully, and supports shallow cloning for faster setup.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Add cloneRepository(url:destination:shallow:progress:) async method to GitWorktreeManager
- Support HTTPS URLs in format https://github.com/owner/repo or https://github.com/owner/repo.git
- Support SSH URLs in format git@github.com:owner/repo.git
- Implement shallow clone option via --depth=1 flag for faster cloning of large repos
- Parse git clone stderr output to extract progress phases: counting, compressing, receiving, resolving
- Report progress percentage and phase via callback closure
- Handle git clone exit codes and translate to typed GitError cases
- Support cancellation via Task.checkCancellation() between progress updates

**Out of Scope:**
- Git LFS support - large file storage cloning deferred to future atom
- Submodule handling - recursive submodule clone deferred to future atom
- Custom authentication UI - rely on system git credential helpers and ssh-agent
- Branch selection during clone - clone default branch only, branch switching is separate feature
- Mirror or bare clone modes - not needed for user workflow
- Clone to custom worktree - always clone to standard directory structure

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: cloneRepository shall accept a url parameter as String and validate it matches HTTPS or SSH URL patterns before proceeding
1. FR2: cloneRepository shall accept a destination parameter as String specifying the absolute path where the repository will be cloned
1. FR3: cloneRepository shall accept a shallow parameter as Bool defaulting to false that when true adds --depth=1 to the git clone command
1. FR4: cloneRepository shall accept a progress callback closure that receives CloneProgress struct updates during the clone operation
1. FR5: cloneRepository shall spawn git clone with --progress flag to ensure progress output is sent to stderr
1. FR6: cloneRepository shall parse stderr lines matching pattern 'Receiving objects: N%' and extract percentage as Int
1. FR7: cloneRepository shall parse stderr lines matching pattern 'Resolving deltas: N%' and extract percentage as Int
1. FR8: cloneRepository shall detect clone completion when git process exits with code 0 and .git directory exists at destination
1. FR9: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.invalidURL when url parameter does not match https:// or git@ patterns
1. FR10: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.authenticationFailed when git exits with code 128 and stderr contains 'Authentication failed'
1. FR11: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.repositoryNotFound when git exits with code 128 and stderr contains 'not found'
1. FR12: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.networkError when git exits with code 128 and stderr contains 'Could not resolve host'
1. FR13: cloneRepository shall clean up partial clone directory on failure before throwing error
1. FR14: cloneRepository shall respect Task cancellation and terminate git process when cancelled

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Clone operation must not block main thread - all Process spawning and I/O must be on background queue
- NFR2: Progress callbacks must be delivered on MainActor for safe UI updates
- NFR3: Memory usage during clone must remain constant regardless of repository size - stream stderr line by line
- NFR4: Clone of 100MB repository over 100Mbps connection should complete within 30 seconds
- NFR5: Error messages must be user-friendly and not expose raw git stderr when possible

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Define CloneProgress struct with phase enum (counting, compressing, receiving, resolving, done), percent Int, and message String
1. Step 2: Define ClonePhase enum with cases counting, compressing, receiving, resolving, done
1. Step 3: Add GitError cases: invalidURL(String), authenticationFailed(String), repositoryNotFound(String), networkError(String), cloneFailed(Int, String), cloneCancelled
1. Step 4: Create private helper parseCloneProgress(_ line: String) -> CloneProgress? that uses regex to extract phase and percentage from git stderr lines
1. Step 5: Create private helper validateCloneURL(_ url: String) throws that validates URL matches https:// or git@ patterns
1. Step 6: Add cloneRepository(url:destination:shallow:progress:) async throws -> String method signature to GitWorktreeManager
1. Step 7: In cloneRepository, first call validateCloneURL to check URL format
1. Step 8: Build git command arguments array: clone, --progress, optionally --depth=1, url, destination
1. Step 9: Create Process instance with executableURL pointing to git binary
1. Step 10: Configure Process with arguments array and empty environment to inherit system environment
1. Step 11: Create Pipe for stderr and assign to Process.standardError
1. Step 12: Create Task to read stderr pipe data in chunks and split into lines
1. Step 13: For each stderr line, call parseCloneProgress and if non-nil, dispatch progress callback on MainActor
1. Step 14: Check Task.isCancelled periodically and if true, call Process.terminate() and throw GitError.cloneCancelled
1. Step 15: Call Process.run() and Process.waitUntilExit() wrapped in withCheckedThrowingContinuation
1. Step 16: After process exits, check terminationStatus - if non-zero, parse stderr to determine specific error type and throw appropriate GitError
1. Step 17: If terminationStatus is 0, verify .git directory exists at destination, return destination path
1. Step 18: Add cleanup logic in catch block to remove partial clone directory via FileManager.default.removeItem

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/GitWorktreeManager.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/GitError.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
git clone --progress https://github.com/owner/repo destination
git clone --progress --depth=1 https://github.com/owner/repo destination
git clone --progress git@github.com:owner/repo.git destination
swift build
swift test --filter GitWorktreeManagerTests
```

#### Data Model Changes
- Add CloneProgress struct to GitWorktreeManager with fields: phase (ClonePhase), percent (Int), message (String)
- Add ClonePhase enum to GitWorktreeManager with cases: counting, compressing, receiving, resolving, done
- Extend GitError enum with cases: invalidURL(String), authenticationFailed(String), repositoryNotFound(String), networkError(String), cloneFailed(exitCode: Int, stderr: String), cloneCancelled

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- GitWorktreeManager.cloneRepository(url: String, destination: String, shallow: Bool, progress: @escaping @Sendable (CloneProgress) -> Void) async throws -> String
- GitWorktreeManager.CloneProgress: Sendable struct with phase, percent, message properties
- GitWorktreeManager.ClonePhase: Sendable enum with counting, compressing, receiving, resolving, done cases
- GitError.invalidURL(String): Thrown when URL does not match https:// or git@ patterns
- GitError.authenticationFailed(String): Thrown when git returns 128 with auth failure message
- GitError.repositoryNotFound(String): Thrown when remote repository does not exist
- GitError.networkError(String): Thrown when DNS resolution or network connection fails
- GitError.cloneFailed(Int, String): Thrown for other non-zero exit codes with stderr content
- GitError.cloneCancelled: Thrown when Task is cancelled during clone operation

**Event Contracts:**
- Progress callback invoked with CloneProgress(phase: .counting, percent: 0-100, message: 'Counting objects') during counting phase
- Progress callback invoked with CloneProgress(phase: .compressing, percent: 0-100, message: 'Compressing objects') during compression phase
- Progress callback invoked with CloneProgress(phase: .receiving, percent: 0-100, message: 'Receiving objects') during receiving phase
- Progress callback invoked with CloneProgress(phase: .resolving, percent: 0-100, message: 'Resolving deltas') during resolving phase
- Progress callback invoked with CloneProgress(phase: .done, percent: 100, message: 'Clone complete') on successful completion

#### UI States
- N/A - This atom is backend-only; UI states covered in separate UI atom

#### UI Interactions
- N/A - This atom is backend-only; UI interactions covered in separate UI atom

#### Edge Cases
- Empty URL string passed - throw GitError.invalidURL with message 'URL cannot be empty'
- URL with trailing whitespace - trim whitespace before validation
- URL with embedded spaces - throw GitError.invalidURL with message 'URL cannot contain spaces'
- Destination directory already exists and is non-empty - git will fail, translate to GitError.cloneFailed with clear message
- Destination directory already exists and is empty - git clone should succeed
- Destination parent directory does not exist - throw GitError.cloneFailed before spawning git
- Destination path is not absolute - throw GitError.cloneFailed with message 'Destination must be absolute path'
- Repository requires authentication but credentials not available - throw GitError.authenticationFailed
- Repository URL valid but repository deleted or private - throw GitError.repositoryNotFound
- Network disconnected mid-clone - throw GitError.networkError after timeout
- Clone cancelled while receiving objects - terminate git process, clean up partial directory
- Very large repository (multiple GB) - shallow clone recommended, progress updates keep UI responsive
- Repository with non-ASCII characters in name - URL encode properly
- SSH URL with non-standard port - parse git@host:port:path format correctly
- HTTPS URL with username embedded - support https://user@github.com/repo format
- Git binary not found at expected path - throw GitError.cloneFailed with message 'Git not installed'

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: Git process spawn fails - FileManager cannot execute git binary. Handle by checking git exists before spawn, throw descriptive error.
- FM2: Network timeout during clone - git hangs waiting for data. Handle by implementing 5-minute timeout that terminates process and cleans up.
- FM3: Disk full during clone - git fails mid-write. Handle by catching clone failure, cleaning up partial directory, throwing GitError.cloneFailed with disk space hint.
- FM4: Permission denied on destination - cannot create directory or files. Handle by pre-checking write permission before clone, throwing early with clear message.
- FM5: SSH key passphrase required - blocking stdin prompt. Handle by setting GIT_SSH_COMMAND to use batch mode, detect passphrase errors in stderr.
- FM6: Progress parsing fails - unexpected stderr format. Handle by continuing clone operation, deliver indeterminate progress updates.
- FM7: Process terminated by system - SIGKILL or memory pressure. Handle by detecting non-zero exit without our cancellation flag, throw GitError.cloneFailed.

#### Rollback Plan
To rollback this change: 1) Revert changes to GitWorktreeManager.swift and GitError.swift. 2) Remove any new test files. 3) Run swift build to verify compilation. 4) No data migration needed as this is additive functionality with no persistence changes.

- Test cloneRepository rejects file:// protocol URLs to prevent local file access abuse
- Test cloneRepository does not log or expose authentication credentials from URL
- Test cloneRepository destination path cannot escape intended directory via path traversal
- Test cloneRepository handles git URL injection attempts in url parameter

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| clone_duration_seconds | histogram | seconds | <30 for repos under 100MB | Track end-to-end clone time from method entry to successful return |
| clone_bytes_received | counter | bytes | N/A - varies by repo | Track total bytes transferred during clone for bandwidth estimation |
| clone_success_rate | gauge | percent | >95% | Track ratio of successful clones to total clone attempts |
| clone_error_count | counter | count | <5% of attempts | Count of clone failures by error type for debugging |

#### Telemetry Events
- `clone_started: Emitted when cloneRepository method begins with url (sanitized), shallow flag, timestamp`
- `clone_progress: Emitted at 25%, 50%, 75% progress milestones with phase and elapsed time`
- `clone_completed: Emitted when clone succeeds with total duration, repo size estimate, shallow flag`
- `clone_failed: Emitted when clone fails with error type, duration before failure, partial size if available`
- `clone_cancelled: Emitted when user cancels clone with duration before cancellation, phase at cancellation`

#### Acceptance Tests
- Given a valid HTTPS URL and empty destination, when cloneRepository is called, then the repository is cloned and destination contains .git directory
- Given a valid SSH URL and configured ssh-agent, when cloneRepository is called, then the repository is cloned successfully
- Given shallow=true flag, when cloneRepository is called, then the cloned repo has only one commit in history
- Given a progress callback, when cloneRepository is running, then callback receives at least one progress update with percentage
- Given an invalid URL format, when cloneRepository is called, then GitError.invalidURL is thrown with descriptive message
- Given a nonexistent repository URL, when cloneRepository is called, then GitError.repositoryNotFound is thrown
- Given network disconnection mid-clone, when timeout expires, then partial clone directory is removed and GitError.networkError is thrown

#### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: cloneRepository method exists on GitWorktreeManager with documented signature
- [ ] AC2: Valid HTTPS URLs (github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org patterns) are accepted
- [ ] AC3: Valid SSH URLs (git@host:path patterns) are accepted
- [ ] AC4: Invalid URLs throw GitError.invalidURL with the rejected URL in error message
- [ ] AC5: Progress callback receives CloneProgress updates during clone operation
- [ ] AC6: Shallow clone with depth=1 produces valid git repository with single commit
- [ ] AC7: Failed clone operations clean up any partial directory before throwing
- [ ] AC8: Cancelled clone operations terminate git process and clean up partial directory
- [ ] AC9: All GitError cases have user-friendly localizedDescription
- [ ] AC10: Clone operation does not block main thread

#### Definition of Done
- [ ] cloneRepository method implemented with full signature including progress callback
- [ ] All 14 functional requirements implemented and verified
- [ ] All 5 non-functional requirements verified
- [ ] Unit tests written and passing for URL validation and progress parsing
- [ ] Integration tests written and passing for successful clone scenarios
- [ ] Integration tests written and passing for error scenarios
- [ ] Code reviewed and approved by at least one reviewer
- [ ] No compiler warnings in changed files
- [ ] Documentation comments added for public API
- [ ] Telemetry events instrumented

**Requires:** Tests, Telemetry, Error Handling, Rollback Plan

#### Completion
**Completed When:** The cloneRepository method is fully implemented, all unit and integration tests pass, code is reviewed and merged, and manual verification confirms cloning works for both HTTPS and SSH URLs with proper progress reporting.

**Evidence:** 1) swift test --filter GitWorktreeManagerTests shows all tests passing. 2) Manual test cloning https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-cookbook succeeds with progress updates visible in debug console. 3) Manual test with invalid URL shows appropriate error. 4) Code coverage report shows >80% coverage of new code.

#### Source References
- docs/new-features-v2.md section A002-CLONE
- Apple Process documentation
- Git clone command documentation

#### Open Questions
- Should we support git:// protocol URLs or restrict to https:// and git@ only for security?
- What is the appropriate timeout value - 5 minutes may be too short for very large repos over slow connections?
- Should we expose environment variable configuration for GIT_SSH_COMMAND customization?

#### Notes
This atom focuses on the backend logic only. The UI components (URL input field, progress bar, error display) are covered in a separate UI atom (A003-DIRSRC). The shallow clone option is important for large repos but users should be warned that shallow clones have limitations for some git operations.

## Phase 1: MVP Session Creation

### E005-F001-S001-T003-A001 — Directory Source Segmented Picker and Conditional Views

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** Remote Registry and CLI Integration
> **Feature:** New Session Creation Flow
> **Story:** Directory Source Selection for Session Creation
> **Task:** Implement Directory Source UI Components

#### Problem Statement
The current New Session modal only supports browsing for an existing directory. Users who want to clone a repository or create a new project folder must do so outside the app, then browse to that location. This friction discourages starting new projects directly from Blaze and creates extra steps in the workflow.

#### Description
Implement a segmented control with Browse, Clone, and Create segments. Each segment displays a distinct view: Browse shows a path display with NSOpenPanel trigger, Clone shows repository URL and destination inputs with progress indicator, Create shows project name input with parent folder selection and git init toggle. State persists across segment switches.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Implement DirectorySourcePicker as a SwiftUI Picker with segmented style containing three cases: browse, clone, create
- Implement BrowseDirectoryView with path display TextField (read-only) and Browse button that opens NSOpenPanel for directory selection
- Implement CloneRepositoryView with TextField for repository URL, TextField for destination folder path, Toggle for shallow clone option, and ProgressView that appears during clone operations
- Implement CreateProjectView with TextField for project name, read-only path display showing computed full path, Change button to select parent folder via NSOpenPanel, and Toggle for git init option
- Define DirectorySource enum with associated values: browse(URL), clone(repositoryURL: String, destination: URL, shallow: Bool), create(name: String, parent: URL, initGit: Bool)
- Preserve user input state when switching between segments so no data is lost
- Validate Clone URL format using regex pattern for common Git URL formats (https, ssh, git protocol)
- Show inline validation indicator (checkmark or X icon) next to Clone URL field based on format validity

**Out of Scope:**
- Template selection dropdown for Create mode (future enhancement)
- Organization or team directory presets (future enhancement)
- Actual git clone execution (handled by separate atom)
- Actual directory creation execution (handled by separate atom)
- SSH key management for clone authentication
- Submodule handling during clone
- Branch selection for clone operations

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-01: DirectorySourcePicker displays three labeled segments: Browse, Clone, Create
1. FR-02: Selecting a segment immediately shows the corresponding child view below the picker
1. FR-03: BrowseDirectoryView displays the selected directory path or placeholder text when none selected
1. FR-04: BrowseDirectoryView Browse button opens NSOpenPanel configured for directory selection only
1. FR-05: NSOpenPanel allows selecting exactly one directory and updates the bound selectedPath on confirmation
1. FR-06: CloneRepositoryView URL field accepts text input and triggers validation on each character change
1. FR-07: Clone URL validation shows green checkmark icon for valid URLs and red X icon for invalid URLs
1. FR-08: CloneRepositoryView destination field shows default path based on URL (last path component without .git)
1. FR-09: CloneRepositoryView shallow clone toggle defaults to off
1. FR-10: CreateProjectView name field accepts text input and updates computed path in real-time
1. FR-11: CreateProjectView computed path combines parent folder path with sanitized project name
1. FR-12: CreateProjectView parent folder defaults to user Documents directory
1. FR-13: CreateProjectView Change button opens NSOpenPanel to select different parent folder
1. FR-14: CreateProjectView git init toggle defaults to on
1. FR-15: Switching segments preserves all entered data in each view independently

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-01: Segment switch animation completes within 150ms
- NFR-02: URL validation regex evaluation completes within 5ms for URLs up to 2000 characters
- NFR-03: All interactive elements have minimum 44pt touch targets for accessibility
- NFR-04: VoiceOver announces segment changes and field labels correctly
- NFR-05: All text fields support standard keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+A, Cmd+C, Cmd+V)

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Define DirectorySource enum in Blaze/Sources/Models/DirectorySource.swift with cases browse, clone, create and associated values
1. Step 2: Create DirectorySourcePicker.swift view with Picker using segmented style and DirectorySource binding
1. Step 3: Add @State properties in DirectorySourcePicker for each segment independent state: browsePath, cloneURL, cloneDestination, cloneShallow, createName, createParent, createInitGit
1. Step 4: Implement switch statement in DirectorySourcePicker body that renders BrowseDirectoryView, CloneRepositoryView, or CreateProjectView based on selected segment
1. Step 5: Create BrowseDirectoryView.swift with HStack containing path Text and Browse Button
1. Step 6: Implement openDirectoryPanel() function using NSOpenPanel with canChooseDirectories=true, canChooseFiles=false, allowsMultipleSelection=false
1. Step 7: Create CloneRepositoryView.swift with VStack containing URL TextField, destination TextField, shallow Toggle, and conditional ProgressView
1. Step 8: Implement validateGitURL(_ url: String) -> Bool function with regex for https://, git@, and git:// patterns
1. Step 9: Add inline validation indicator Image(systemName:) that changes based on validation result
1. Step 10: Create CreateProjectView.swift with VStack containing name TextField, computed path Text, Change Button, and git init Toggle
1. Step 11: Implement sanitizeProjectName(_ name: String) -> String to remove invalid filesystem characters
1. Step 12: Compute destination path by joining createParent with sanitized createName
1. Step 13: Set default createParent to FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first
1. Step 14: Wire all views into DirectorySourcePicker with appropriate Bindings
1. Step 15: Add DirectorySourcePicker to NewSessionModal.swift in the directory selection section
1. Step 16: Ensure selectedSource binding in NewSessionModal updates when user completes input in any mode

#### Files

#### Data Model Changes
- Add DirectorySource enum with three cases: browse(selectedPath: URL?), clone(repositoryURL: String, destination: URL?, shallow: Bool), create(name: String, parent: URL, initGit: Bool)
- DirectorySource conforms to Equatable and Hashable for state comparison
- DirectorySource provides computed property isComplete: Bool indicating whether required fields are filled

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- DirectorySourcePicker.init(selection: Binding<DirectorySource>) - main picker component
- BrowseDirectoryView.init(selectedPath: Binding<URL?>) - browse mode view
- CloneRepositoryView.init(repositoryURL: Binding<String>, destination: Binding<URL?>, shallow: Binding<Bool>, isCloning: Binding<Bool>) - clone mode view
- CreateProjectView.init(name: Binding<String>, parent: Binding<URL>, initGit: Binding<Bool>) - create mode view
- validateGitURL(_ url: String) -> Bool - URL format validation function
- sanitizeProjectName(_ name: String) -> String - filesystem-safe name conversion

**Event Contracts:**
- No runtime events emitted - this is pure UI state management
- Parent view observes DirectorySource binding changes to enable/disable Create Session button

#### UI States
- Initial state: Browse segment selected, no path selected, placeholder text shown
- Browse selected with path: Shows full path in text field, Browse button enabled
- Browse NSOpenPanel open: Modal sheet showing directory picker
- Clone selected empty: URL field empty, destination empty, shallow off, no validation indicator
- Clone selected with valid URL: Green checkmark visible, auto-computed destination path shown
- Clone selected with invalid URL: Red X visible, destination may be empty
- Clone in progress: ProgressView spinning, fields disabled (handled by parent)
- Create selected empty: Name field empty, default parent shown, computed path shows parent only, git init on
- Create selected with name: Computed full path updates in real-time as user types
- Create parent selection open: NSOpenPanel showing directory picker for parent folder

#### UI Interactions
- Tap Browse segment -> BrowseDirectoryView appears with current browsePath state
- Tap Clone segment -> CloneRepositoryView appears with current clone field states
- Tap Create segment -> CreateProjectView appears with current create field states
- Click Browse button in BrowseDirectoryView -> NSOpenPanel opens, selection updates browsePath
- Type in Clone URL field -> Each keystroke triggers validation, indicator updates
- Type in Clone destination field -> Manual override of auto-computed destination
- Toggle Shallow clone -> Updates cloneShallow state
- Type in Create name field -> Computed path updates immediately with sanitized name
- Click Change button in CreateProjectView -> NSOpenPanel opens for parent folder selection
- Toggle Git init -> Updates createInitGit state
- Press Tab key -> Focus moves to next interactive element in logical order
- Press Escape -> Closes any open NSOpenPanel without selection

#### Edge Cases
- User pastes extremely long URL (2000+ chars) into Clone field - validation must not freeze UI
- User enters project name with special characters (slashes, colons, null bytes) - must sanitize to valid filename
- User selects parent folder that requires admin permissions - must handle gracefully when creation attempted
- User rapidly switches segments while typing - state must not be corrupted or lost
- User has no Documents folder (edge case on new/restricted accounts) - fallback to home directory
- User pastes URL with trailing whitespace - trim before validation
- Clone destination folder already exists - show warning indicator (yellow)
- Project name results in empty string after sanitization - disable Create Session button
- NSOpenPanel cancelled - do not modify current path binding
- User selects symlink as browse directory - resolve to actual path

#### Failure Modes
- NSOpenPanel fails to open (sandbox restriction) - log error and show alert explaining permission needed
- FileManager cannot access Documents directory - fallback to temporary directory with warning
- URL validation regex has catastrophic backtracking on malformed input - use timeout/limit on regex
- Memory pressure during rapid segment switching - ensure no retain cycles in view bindings
- VoiceOver not announcing segment changes - verify accessibility labels are set correctly

#### Rollback Plan
Revert changes to NewSessionModal.swift to remove DirectorySourcePicker integration. Delete the five new files (DirectorySourcePicker.swift, BrowseDirectoryView.swift, CloneRepositoryView.swift, CreateProjectView.swift, DirectorySource.swift). The modal will return to its previous browse-only behavior. Git revert of the commit containing these changes is sufficient.

- Test sanitizeProjectName replaces spaces with hyphens

### E005-F001-S001-T004-A001 — Provider Model Selector Component

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

#### Problem Statement
Users currently have no way to select which AI provider or model to use when creating a session. The app defaults to a single provider without giving users control over which CLI backend or model tier they want, limiting flexibility and user choice.

#### Description
Create the ProviderModelSection SwiftUI component containing a segmented provider picker and a filterable model list with tier badges, CLI status indicators, and appropriate state management for the New Session Modal.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Provider segmented picker with three options: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google
- Model list filtered by selected provider with radio button selection
- Tier badges on each model: flagship, balanced, fast
- CLI availability indicator checking PATH for installed binaries
- Default model auto-selection when provider changes
- State binding to parent NewSessionModal for provider and modelId

**Out of Scope:**

- API key entry or management UI (handled by system keychain)
- Model download or installation flow (defer to F005)

### E005-F001-S001-T006-A001 — Engine Adapter Routing Implementation

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.25 days

> **Epic:** Multi-Engine Architecture
> **Feature:** Engine Adapter Wiring
> **Story:** Session-to-Adapter Routing
> **Task:** Implement Engine Adapter Wiring Logic

#### Problem Statement
EngineManager currently has a dictionary of adapters keyed by EngineType, but there is no method to get an adapter for a given Session. The orchestrator and UI need a single entry point that accepts a Session and returns the properly configured adapter for that session's provider.

#### Description
Implement the core routing logic in EngineManager that takes a Session and returns the appropriate EngineAdapter based on session.engineType, ensuring adapters are lazily registered and available before use.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Add getAdapter(for session: Session) -> EngineAdapter? method to EngineManager
- Validate adapter is registered before returning
- Log warning if requested adapter type is not registered
- Return nil with error context if adapter unavailable
- Add convenience method getAdapter(for type: EngineType) -> EngineAdapter? for direct type lookup

**Out of Scope:**
- CLI flag mapping for specific models (deferred to per-adapter configuration)
- Provider authentication flow (handled by each adapter's validateInstallation)
- Session persistence changes (session already has engineType field)
- UI for adapter selection (already exists in NewSessionModal)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: EngineManager.getAdapter(for:) accepts Session and returns matching EngineAdapter or nil
1. FR2: If adapter for session.engineType is not registered, method returns nil
1. FR3: Debug logging emits warning when adapter is not found for requested type
1. FR4: Method is synchronous since adapter lookup is dictionary-based O(1) operation
1. FR5: Existing adapter(for type:) method is preserved for backward compatibility

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Adapter lookup must complete in under 1 microsecond (simple dictionary access)
- NFR2: No memory allocation on hot path (return existing adapter reference)

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Open Blaze/Sources/Engine/EngineAdapter.swift and locate EngineManager class
1. Step 2: Add getAdapter(for session: Session) -> (any EngineAdapter)? method after existing adapter(for type:) method
1. Step 3: Implement method body: lookup adapters[session.engineType] and return result
1. Step 4: Add os.Logger instance to EngineManager for warning logs
1. Step 5: Add warning log if adapters[session.engineType] returns nil
1. Step 6: Write unit test in Tests/Engine/EngineManagerTests.swift for getAdapter routing
1. Step 7: Verify existing tests still pass with swift test

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Engine/EngineAdapter.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Tests/Engine/EngineManagerTests.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test
swift test --filter EngineManagerTests
```

#### Data Model Changes
- No schema changes required - Session.engineType already exists

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- EngineManager.getAdapter(for session: Session) -> (any EngineAdapter)? - returns adapter for session's engine type
- EngineManager.adapter(for type: EngineType) -> (any EngineAdapter)? - existing method preserved

**Event Contracts:**
- No new events - adapter lookup is synchronous and does not emit events

#### UI States
- No UI changes - this is backend routing logic

#### UI Interactions
- No UI changes - this is backend routing logic

#### Edge Cases
- EC1: Session has engineType but no adapter registered - return nil with warning log
- EC2: Session is created before adapters are registered at startup - return nil (caller must handle)
- EC3: Multiple rapid calls with same session - return same adapter instance (stateless lookup)
- EC4: Adapter previously registered but later removed - return nil (dictionary key removed)

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: Adapter not registered - return nil, log warning, caller shows user-facing error about missing CLI
- FM2: EngineType enum gains new case not in adapters dict - return nil, log warning with unknown type

#### Rollback Plan
Remove the getAdapter(for session:) method from EngineManager. The existing adapter(for type:) method provides equivalent functionality. No data migration needed.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test getAdapter returns ClaudeCodeAdapter when session.engineType is .claude
- Test getAdapter returns GeminiCliAdapter when session.engineType is .gemini
- Test getAdapter returns CodexCliAdapter when session.engineType is .codex
- Test getAdapter returns nil when adapter is not registered
- Test getAdapter returns same instance on repeated calls (identity check)

**Integration:**
- Test SessionOrchestrator uses getAdapter to obtain correct adapter for session
- Test full flow: create session with .gemini type, verify Gemini adapter returned

**Ui:**
- N/A - no UI changes in this atom

**Perf:**
- Verify adapter lookup completes in under 1ms for 1000 sequential calls

**Security:**
- N/A - no security implications for in-memory dictionary lookup

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| engine_adapter_lookup_time_ns | histogram | nanoseconds | <1000 | Time to look up adapter by session engine type |
| engine_adapter_miss_count | counter | count | 0 | Count of adapter lookups that returned nil due to unregistered type |

#### Telemetry Events
- `engine_adapter_lookup - emitted when getAdapter is called with session id and engine type`

#### Acceptance Tests
- AT1: Given a session with engineType=.claude, when getAdapter is called, then ClaudeCodeAdapter is returned
- AT2: Given a session with engineType=.gemini and GeminiCliAdapter registered, when getAdapter is called, then GeminiCliAdapter is returned
- AT3: Given a session with engineType=.codex and no adapter registered, when getAdapter is called, then nil is returned

- [ ] AC2: Method returns correct adapter type based on session.engineType

## Phase 1: MVP

_1 atoms in this phase_

| E005-F001-S001-T007-A001 | CLI Availability Checker Implementation | planned | must | low |

### E005-F001-S001-T007-A001 — CLI Availability Checker Implementation

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** Multi-CLI Provider Support
> **Feature:** Provider Selection Modal
> **Story:** Provider Selection and Validation
> **Task:** CLI Validation Pre-Check

#### Problem Statement
Users may attempt to create a session with a provider whose CLI is not installed on their system. Without pre-validation, the app would fail at session spawn time with a confusing Process.run error. This atom implements proactive CLI detection to show availability status upfront, disable unavailable providers, and provide a clear path to installation.

#### Description
Create CLIAvailabilityChecker service that detects installed CLIs via which/where commands, caches availability state, and integrates with NewSessionModal to disable unavailable providers and show install prompts.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Implement CLIAvailabilityChecker actor that runs which/where commands to detect CLI binaries
- Check for claude, gemini, and codex CLI binaries on system PATH
- Cache availability results with configurable TTL to avoid repeated shell calls
- Integrate checker with NewSessionModal to query availability on modal open
- Disable ProviderCard selection for unavailable CLIs with visual indicator
- Show Install button on unavailable provider cards that navigates to onboarding flow
- Extract CLI version string when available for display in provider card
- Handle edge cases: CLI exists but not executable, CLI exists but returns error on version check

**Out of Scope:**
- Automatic CLI installation - deferred to F005 onboarding flow
- Homebrew or package manager integration for installation
- Custom CLI path configuration - users must have CLI on standard PATH
- Provider-specific authentication validation - separate from CLI availability
- Background re-checking while modal is open - single check on open is sufficient

#### Functional Requirements
1. CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAvailability(provider: EngineType) returns CLIStatus enum with cases: available(version: String), notInstalled, notExecutable, versionCheckFailed
1. CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAllProviders() returns dictionary mapping EngineType to CLIStatus
1. NewSessionModal calls checkAllProviders() in onAppear and stores results in local state
1. ProviderCard receives isAvailable binding and renders disabled state with opacity 0.5 when false
1. ProviderCard shows Install button overlay when CLI not available, button triggers navigation to onboarding
1. Selected provider validation prevents Continue button action if selected provider CLI is unavailable
1. CLI check results are cached in actor-isolated dictionary with timestamp for TTL expiration
1. Version string displayed in ProviderCard subtitle when CLI is available (e.g. Claude Code v1.2.3)

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- All CLI checks complete within 3 seconds total for all three providers running in parallel
- No UI jank or blocking during availability check - modal opens immediately with loading state
- Cache reduces shell command overhead for repeated modal opens within TTL window
- Graceful degradation if shell commands fail - treat as notInstalled rather than crashing

#### Implementation Steps
1. Create Blaze/Sources/Services/CLIAvailabilityChecker.swift with actor declaration and CLIStatus enum
1. Implement private shellCommand helper that runs Process with timeout and captures stdout/stderr
1. Implement cliPath(for:) method that returns expected binary name for each EngineType
1. Implement checkAvailability(provider:) that runs which command and parses result
1. Implement version extraction by running cli --version and parsing first line of output
1. Add cache dictionary with timestamps and TTL constant, implement cache lookup in checkAvailability
1. Implement checkAllProviders() that runs all three checks concurrently using TaskGroup
1. Add @Published availabilityStatus dictionary to NewSessionViewModel or create dedicated state
1. Wire onAppear in NewSessionModal to call checker and update state
1. Modify ProviderCard to accept isAvailable and version bindings, implement disabled visual state
1. Add Install button overlay to ProviderCard that appears when not available
1. Wire Install button to navigation coordinator to show onboarding CLI installation screen
1. Add guard in Continue button action to prevent proceeding with unavailable provider
1. Write unit tests for CLIAvailabilityChecker with mocked Process execution
1. Write UI test that verifies disabled state renders correctly for unavailable provider

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/NewSessionModal.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Components/ProviderCard.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/ViewModels/NewSessionViewModel.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Services/CLIAvailabilityChecker.swift`
- `Tests/BlazeTests/Services/CLIAvailabilityCheckerTests.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test --filter CLIAvailabilityCheckerTests
which claude
which gemini
which codex
claude --version
gemini --version
codex --version
```

#### Data Model Changes
- Add CLIStatus enum: available(version: String), notInstalled, notExecutable, versionCheckFailed
- Add CLIAvailabilityCache struct with status: CLIStatus, checkedAt: Date fields
- No SQLite schema changes - availability is ephemeral state not persisted to database

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAvailability(provider: EngineType) async -> CLIStatus
- CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAllProviders() async -> [EngineType: CLIStatus]
- CLIAvailabilityChecker.invalidateCache() to force re-check on next call
- CLIAvailabilityChecker.shared singleton access pattern for app-wide usage

**Event Contracts:**
- No new NormalizedEvent types - CLI availability is pre-session validation
- Existing navigation events used for Install button to onboarding flow transition

#### UI States
- ProviderCard loading state: subtle pulse animation while availability check in progress
- ProviderCard available state: full opacity, version subtitle visible, selectable
- ProviderCard unavailable state: 0.5 opacity, Install button overlay, not selectable
- ProviderCard error state: same as unavailable with generic not available message
- Continue button disabled state when selected provider is unavailable

#### UI Interactions
- User opens New Session modal - triggers availability check for all providers
- User sees loading indicators on provider cards during check (brief, sub-second typical)
- User sees Install button appear on unavailable provider card
- User taps Install button - navigates to onboarding flow for that provider
- User taps unavailable provider card - selection prevented, visual feedback via shake or no-op
- User selects available provider - normal selection behavior, version shown
- User taps Continue with available provider selected - proceeds to session creation

#### Edge Cases
- CLI binary exists but is not executable (chmod issue) - detect via access check and report notExecutable
- CLI binary exists but version command fails (corrupted install) - report versionCheckFailed status
- PATH environment variable is empty or malformed - handle gracefully, report notInstalled
- Multiple CLI versions installed (homebrew and npm global) - which returns first in PATH, use that
- CLI installed during app session after initial check - cache TTL allows re-detection on modal reopen
- Network-dependent CLI that requires auth before version works (some CLIs) - timeout and report versionCheckFailed
- User has alias but not actual binary (alias claude=xyz) - which resolves aliases on macOS, should work
- Symlink to CLI that points to missing target - which succeeds but execution fails, detect via test execution

#### Failure Modes
- Process.run throws on which command - catch exception, log warning, return notInstalled
- Process.run times out (CLI hangs) - terminate process after timeout, return versionCheckFailed
- Actor isolation violation - ensure all Process calls happen within actor context
- Memory pressure during concurrent checks - TaskGroup handles cancellation gracefully
- Modal dismissed during check - Task cancellation propagates, no orphan processes

#### Rollback Plan
Revert CLIAvailabilityChecker.swift and related NewSessionModal changes. ProviderCard returns to always-enabled state. Remove availability check from modal onAppear. Feature gracefully degrades to original behavior where CLI errors surface at session spawn time.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAvailability returns available with version when which succeeds and version parses
- Test CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAvailability returns notInstalled when which returns non-zero exit
- Test CLIAvailabilityChecker.checkAvailability returns versionCheckFailed when version command times out
- Test cache TTL expiration triggers re-check on subsequent call
- Test checkAllProviders runs checks concurrently and returns complete dictionary
- Test version string parsing extracts version from various CLI output formats

**Integration:**
- Test NewSessionModal loads availability state on appear and updates ProviderCard states
- Test Install button navigation triggers correct onboarding flow for provider
- Test selecting unavailable provider does not update selection state
- Test Continue button remains disabled when unavailable provider somehow selected

**Ui:**
- Verify ProviderCard renders with reduced opacity when unavailable
- Verify Install button overlay appears and is tappable on unavailable card
- Verify version subtitle displays correctly for available providers
- Verify loading state animation appears during availability check
- Verify Continue button shows disabled styling when appropriate

**Perf:**
- Verify all three provider checks complete within 3 second budget
- Verify modal open to interactive latency under 500ms with cached results
- Verify no main thread blocking during availability checks via Instruments
- Verify memory usage stable across repeated modal open/close cycles

**Security:**
- Verify shell commands use absolute paths or validated binary names only
- Verify no user input is passed to shell commands (injection prevention)
- Verify Process environment is sanitized, no sensitive env vars leaked
- Verify timeout prevents denial of service from hanging CLI

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| cli_check_duration_ms | histogram | milliseconds | p99 < 2000 | Track time for individual CLI availability checks |
| cli_check_cache_hit_rate | gauge | percentage | > 80% | Measure effectiveness of availability cache |
| cli_unavailable_rate | gauge | percentage | < 20% | Track how often users encounter unavailable CLIs |
| install_button_click_rate | counter | clicks | N/A informational | Measure user engagement with install prompts |

#### Telemetry Events
- `cli_availability_check_started with provider: EngineType`
- `cli_availability_check_completed with provider: EngineType, status: CLIStatus, duration_ms: Int`
- `cli_install_button_tapped with provider: EngineType`
- `session_creation_blocked_unavailable_cli with provider: EngineType`

#### Acceptance Tests
- Given Claude CLI is installed, when user opens New Session modal, then Claude provider card shows available with version
- Given Gemini CLI is not installed, when user opens New Session modal, then Google provider card shows Install button and is not selectable
- Given user taps Install on unavailable provider, then app navigates to onboarding installation screen for that provider
- Given all CLIs unavailable, when user opens modal, then all cards show Install and Continue button is disabled
- Given user closes and reopens modal within 30 seconds, then cached availability is used without re-running checks

#### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLI availability checked automatically on New Session modal open without user action
- [ ] Unavailable providers visually distinct with Install button overlay
- [ ] Available providers show version string extracted from CLI
- [ ] Install button navigates to onboarding flow for correct provider
- [ ] Continue button disabled when no available provider is selected
- [ ] All checks complete within 3 seconds for responsive UX
- [ ] Cache prevents redundant shell commands on rapid modal reopens

#### Definition of Done
- [ ] CLIAvailabilityChecker actor implemented with all specified methods
- [ ] Unit tests achieve 90% coverage of checker logic
- [ ] Integration tests verify modal state updates correctly
- [ ] UI renders all specified states (loading, available, unavailable)
- [ ] Telemetry events fire correctly for all check outcomes
- [ ] No memory leaks observed in repeated modal open/close
- [ ] Code review approved by designated reviewer

**Requires:** Tests, Telemetry, Error Handling, Rollback Plan

#### Completion
**Completed When:** NewSessionModal correctly shows availability status for all providers, Install buttons work, and unavailable providers cannot be selected for session creation.

**Evidence:** Screenshot showing modal with one available provider (version visible) and one unavailable provider (Install button visible). Test run output showing all CLIAvailabilityCheckerTests passing. Instruments trace showing no main thread blocking during checks.

#### Source References

- docs/atoms/atom.schema.v2.json

#### Open Questions
- Should we support custom CLI paths via preferences for users with non-standard installations?
- What is the correct binary name for OpenAI Codex CLI - codex or openai-codex?
- Should version check failure prevent selection or just hide version string?

#### Notes
CLI detection is critical path for multi-provider UX. If check is too slow, consider optimistic UI that allows selection while check runs in background, with validation on Continue tap instead.

## Phase 1: Core Data Layer

| E005-F002-S001-T001-A001 | ReadStateStore Core Implementation | planned | must | low |

### E005-F002-S001-T001-A001 — ReadStateStore Core Implementation

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** Session Management
> **Feature:** Unread Notifications
> **Story:** Unread Badge State Management
> **Task:** Implement ReadStateStore Actor

#### Problem Statement
Users cannot tell if background worktrees or inactive sessions have received new events. Without unread tracking, users must manually check each session to discover new activity, which wastes time and creates cognitive load.

#### Description
Implement the ReadStateStore Swift actor with methods for tracking read positions, calculating unread counts, marking sessions as read, and persisting to the session_read_states SQLite table.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Create ReadStateStore actor in Blaze/Sources/Data/ReadStateStore.swift
- Create session_read_states SQLite table schema
- Implement getLastReadSequence(sessionId:) method returning Int64
- Implement markAsRead(sessionId:sequence:) method to update read position
- Implement getUnreadCount(sessionId:totalEvents:) method returning Int
- Implement loadAllReadStates() method for app startup
- Implement persistReadState(sessionId:sequence:) method for SQLite writes
- Add ReadState model struct with sessionId, lastReadSequence, and lastReadAt fields

**Out of Scope:**
- UI badge rendering (covered in S002-BADGE)
- Real-time event subscription and count updates (covered in T002)
- Notification sounds or system notifications
- Cross-device sync of read states
- Read state export or backup functionality

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: ReadStateStore.getLastReadSequence(sessionId:) returns the last read event sequence for a session, or 0 if never read
1. FR2: ReadStateStore.markAsRead(sessionId:sequence:) updates the read position and lastReadAt timestamp
1. FR3: ReadStateStore.getUnreadCount(sessionId:totalEvents:) returns max(0, totalEvents - lastReadSequence)
1. FR4: ReadStateStore.loadAllReadStates() loads all persisted states into memory on app startup
1. FR5: Read state changes persist to SQLite within 1 second of the markAsRead call
1. FR6: ReadStateStore handles concurrent read and write operations safely via actor isolation

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Actor methods complete within 50ms for single-session operations
- NFR2: loadAllReadStates completes within 200ms for up to 1000 sessions
- NFR3: SQLite writes are batched if multiple updates occur within 100ms window
- NFR4: Memory usage for cached read states stays under 1MB for 10000 sessions

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create Blaze/Sources/Data/ReadStateStore.swift with actor declaration and ReadState struct
1. Step 2: Add private dictionary readStates: [String: ReadState] for in-memory cache
1. Step 3: Implement init(database:) that takes Database actor dependency
1. Step 4: Implement loadAllReadStates() that queries session_read_states table and populates cache
1. Step 5: Implement getLastReadSequence(sessionId:) that returns cached value or 0
1. Step 6: Implement markAsRead(sessionId:sequence:) that updates cache and schedules persistence
1. Step 7: Implement getUnreadCount(sessionId:totalEvents:) with max(0, totalEvents - lastRead) calculation
1. Step 8: Implement persistReadState(sessionId:sequence:) with INSERT OR REPLACE SQL
1. Step 9: Add Migration.v7_addSessionReadStates to Blaze/Sources/Data/Migrations.swift
1. Step 10: Register ReadStateStore in BlazeApp.swift dependency injection

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Data/Migrations.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/App/BlazeApp.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Models.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Data/ReadStateStore.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test --filter ReadStateStoreTests
sqlite3 ~/Library/Application Support/Blaze/blaze.db '.schema session_read_states'
```

#### Data Model Changes
- Add ReadState struct with fields: sessionId (String), lastReadSequence (Int64), lastReadAt (Date)
- Add session_read_states table: session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_read_sequence INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_read_at DATETIME NOT NULL

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- ReadStateStore.getLastReadSequence(sessionId: String) async -> Int64
- ReadStateStore.markAsRead(sessionId: String, sequence: Int64) async throws
- ReadStateStore.getUnreadCount(sessionId: String, totalEvents: Int64) async -> Int
- ReadStateStore.loadAllReadStates() async throws
- ReadStateStore.persistReadState(sessionId: String, sequence: Int64) async throws

**Event Contracts:**
- Internal: readStateUpdated(sessionId: String, newSequence: Int64) posted to NotificationCenter after markAsRead
- No external event emission - UI observes via Combine publisher on ReadStateStore

#### UI States
- N/A - this atom is data layer only

#### UI Interactions
- N/A - this atom is data layer only

#### Edge Cases
- EC1: markAsRead called for non-existent session - create new ReadState entry
- EC2: markAsRead called with sequence lower than current - ignore (keep higher value)
- EC3: getUnreadCount called before loadAllReadStates completes - return 0 as safe default
- EC4: Database locked during write - retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff
- EC5: Session deleted while read state exists - orphan cleanup on next loadAllReadStates
- EC6: App crash during persistence - incomplete write handled by SQLite transaction rollback

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: SQLite database corruption - log error, reset read states to empty, continue with in-memory only until restart
- FM2: Out of memory loading states - implement pagination for loadAllReadStates if more than 10000 sessions
- FM3: Actor deadlock - use nonisolated methods for read-only operations where safe

#### Rollback Plan
Revert ReadStateStore.swift creation and Migration.v7 changes. Run migration rollback SQL: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS session_read_states. Remove ReadStateStore registration from BlazeApp.swift.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- test_getLastReadSequence_returnsZeroForNewSession
- test_getLastReadSequence_returnsCachedValueAfterMarkAsRead
- test_markAsRead_updatesInMemoryCache
- test_markAsRead_ignoresLowerSequenceValue
- test_getUnreadCount_calculatesCorrectDifference
- test_getUnreadCount_returnsZeroWhenFullyRead
- test_getUnreadCount_returnsZeroWhenOverread
- test_loadAllReadStates_populatesCacheFromDatabase

**Integration:**
- test_readStateStore_persistsAcrossActorRecreation
- test_readStateStore_handlesMultipleConcurrentWrites
- test_readStateStore_survivesAppRelaunch via XCTest with app lifecycle
- test_migration_v7_createsTableWithCorrectSchema

**Ui:**
- N/A - data layer atom has no UI

**Perf:**
- test_markAsRead_completesWithin50ms
- test_loadAllReadStates_completesWithin200msFor1000Sessions
- test_getUnreadCount_completesWithin1ms

**Security:**
- test_sessionIdValidation_rejectsEmptyStrings
- test_sessionIdValidation_rejectsSqlInjectionAttempts
- test_readStateStore_isolatesDataBetweenSessions

#### Acceptance Tests

### E005-F003-S001-T004-A001 — CLI Detection Screen with Installation Flow

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 2.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Multi-CLI Hooks Architecture
> **Feature:** E005-F003: Onboarding Flow
> **Story:** E005-F003-S001: First-Run Setup Experience
> **Task:** E005-F003-S001-T004: CLI Detection Screen Implementation

#### Problem Statement
Users may not have all AI CLIs installed when they first launch Blaze, and manually installing command-line tools requires terminal knowledge, dependency management, and PATH configuration. This creates friction in the onboarding experience and may prevent users from using all supported engines.

#### Description
A SwiftUI view that presents a list of supported AI CLIs with their installation status, version numbers when installed, recommended badges, and one-click install buttons that orchestrate dependency checking, package installation, PATH configuration, and verification.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Detect installed CLIs by executing 'which' and version commands for each supported CLI
- Display CLI cards showing name, icon, installed/not-installed status, and version when available
- Show 'Recommended' badges for Claude Code and Aider based on capabilities
- Provide 'Install' button for each missing CLI that triggers installation flow
- Implement 'Install All Missing' bulk action button
- Check runtime dependencies (Node.js, Python, Rust) before CLI installation
- Install missing dependencies via Homebrew automatically
- Execute appropriate package manager command (npm, pip, brew) per CLI
- Update PATH in shell config file (.zshrc) after installation
- Verify installation succeeded by re-running detection
- Handle skip action to proceed without installing missing CLIs

**Out of Scope:**
- Authentication or login flows for any CLI - deferred to later screens
- CLI configuration beyond PATH setup - handled in subsequent onboarding steps
- Updating already-installed CLIs to newer versions - deferred to settings
- Custom CLI path configuration - advanced users can configure manually
- Windows or Linux support - macOS only for MVP

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: On view appear, execute parallel detection for all six supported CLIs using Process spawn with 5-second timeout
1. FR2: Display each CLI as a card with icon, name, status badge (Installed/Not Installed), version string when installed, and Recommended badge where applicable
1. FR3: Show Install button for each not-installed CLI that transitions to installing state with progress indicator
1. FR4: Install button tap triggers dependency check, then runs appropriate install command, then verifies installation
1. FR5: Provide Install All Missing button that queues all missing CLI installations in sequence with aggregate progress
1. FR6: Skip button navigates to next onboarding screen without blocking on missing CLIs
1. FR7: Next button navigates forward and is enabled only when at least one CLI is installed
1. FR8: Re-detect CLI status after each successful installation and update UI accordingly
1. FR9: Display error state with retry option if installation fails, including error message from stderr

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Detection phase completes within 3 seconds for all CLIs running in parallel
- NFR2: UI remains responsive during detection and installation with no main thread blocking
- NFR3: Installation progress updates at least every 500ms for user feedback
- NFR4: Memory footprint for Process spawns stays under 50MB
- NFR5: Support VoiceOver accessibility with proper labels for all interactive elements

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create CLIDetectionOnboardingView.swift with @StateObject for CLIDetectionViewModel
1. Step 2: Define SupportedCLI enum with cases for claudeCode, geminiCLI, codexCLI, aider, openCode, amp including detection commands and install commands
1. Step 3: Create CLIDetectionResult model with properties: cli enum, isInstalled bool, version optional string, error optional string
1. Step 4: Implement CLIDetectionViewModel with Published array of detection results and detection/installation methods
1. Step 5: Create detectCLI async method that spawns Process with which command followed by version command, with 5-second timeout
1. Step 6: Implement detectAllCLIs using TaskGroup for parallel detection of all supported CLIs
1. Step 7: Create installCLI async method that checks dependencies, installs if missing, then installs target CLI
1. Step 8: Implement checkDependencies method that verifies node/python/rust based on CLI requirements
1. Step 9: Create installDependency method using brew install with progress parsing from stdout
1. Step 10: Implement runInstallCommand for each CLI type (npm install -g, pip install, brew install)
1. Step 11: Create updatePathIfNeeded method that appends to ~/.zshrc if path not already present
1. Step 12: Implement verifyInstallation by re-running detection and comparing results
1. Step 13: Build CLICardView subview with icon, name, status badge, version, recommended badge, and install button
1. Step 14: Create InstallProgressView showing current step, progress bar, and cancel button
1. Step 15: Implement error state UI with error message display and retry button
1. Step 16: Add Install All Missing button with aggregate progress tracking
1. Step 17: Wire up Skip and Next navigation buttons with proper enabled states
1. Step 18: Add telemetry calls for detection results, install attempts, and outcomes
1. Step 19: Write unit tests for detection logic with mock Process outputs
1. Step 20: Write UI tests for card interactions and navigation flow

#### Files
**Files Touched:**

- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/ViewModels/CLIDetectionViewModel.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/CLI/SupportedCLI.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/CLI/CLIDetector.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/CLI/CLIInstaller.swift`


#### Data Model Changes
- Add SupportedCLI enum with rawValue strings: claudeCode, geminiCLI, codexCLI, aider, openCode, amp
- Add CLIDetectionResult struct with fields: cli (SupportedCLI), isInstalled (Bool), version (String?), error (String?), isRecommended (Bool)
- Add CLIInstallState enum: idle, checkingDependencies, installingDependency(String), installingCLI, configuringPath, verifying, completed, failed(Error)
- Add DetectionState enum: notStarted, detecting, completed, error(String)

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CLIDetector.detectCLI(cli: SupportedCLI) async throws -> CLIDetectionResult
- CLIDetector.detectAll() async -> [CLIDetectionResult]
- CLIInstaller.install(cli: SupportedCLI, progressHandler: (CLIInstallState) -> Void) async throws -> Void
- CLIInstaller.installAll(clis: [SupportedCLI], progressHandler: (SupportedCLI, CLIInstallState) -> Void) async throws -> Void
- ShellExecutor.run(command: String, arguments: [String], timeout: TimeInterval) async throws -> (stdout: String, stderr: String, exitCode: Int32)

**Event Contracts:**
- OnboardingEvent.cliDetectionStarted - emitted when detection phase begins
- OnboardingEvent.cliDetectionCompleted(results: [CLIDetectionResult]) - emitted with all detection results
- OnboardingEvent.cliInstallStarted(cli: SupportedCLI) - emitted when install begins for a CLI
- OnboardingEvent.cliInstallProgress(cli: SupportedCLI, state: CLIInstallState) - emitted on state changes during install
- OnboardingEvent.cliInstallCompleted(cli: SupportedCLI, success: Bool, error: String?) - emitted when install finishes
- OnboardingEvent.cliDetectionScreenSkipped - emitted when user clicks Skip
- OnboardingEvent.cliDetectionScreenCompleted(installedCLIs: [SupportedCLI]) - emitted when user proceeds with Next

#### UI States
- Loading state: Spinner with 'Scanning for AI CLIs' text while detection runs
- Results state: List of CLI cards showing detection outcomes
- Installing state: Progress view overlay showing current installation step and progress bar
- Error state: Card shows red status with error message and Retry button
- Completed state: All cards show final status with Next button enabled

#### UI Interactions
- Tap Install button on CLI card to trigger single CLI installation flow
- Tap Retry button on failed installation to re-attempt installation
- Tap Cancel button during installation to abort current install with cleanup
- Tap Install All Missing button to queue bulk installation of all missing CLIs
- Tap Skip button to proceed to next screen without installing anything
- Tap Next button to proceed after at least one CLI is confirmed installed
- Pull to refresh triggers re-detection of all CLIs

#### Edge Cases
- User has CLI installed but not in PATH - detect via common install locations as fallback
- CLI command exists but returns non-zero exit code on version check - treat as corrupt installation
- Homebrew not installed - prompt user to install Homebrew first with one-click install option
- Network timeout during package download - show error with retry option
- Disk full during installation - detect error and show actionable message
- Another process has lock on package manager - wait with timeout then error
- CLI version command returns multi-line output - parse first line only
- User .zshrc has syntax errors - append PATH without breaking existing config

#### Failure Modes
- Process spawn fails due to sandbox restrictions - show error explaining need for Full Disk Access permission
- Installation completes but verification fails - show partial success state with manual instructions
- User cancels during dependency install - clean up partial dependency installation
- npm/pip not available after node/python install - source shell config before continuing
- Multiple simultaneous install attempts - queue installations to run sequentially
- Memory pressure during bulk install - pause and retry after GC

#### Rollback Plan
If installation fails mid-process, remove any partially installed packages using brew uninstall, npm uninstall -g, or pip uninstall. Restore original PATH entries in .zshrc by removing only the lines added by Blaze (marked with comment). Track all modifications in OnboardingState for reliable cleanup.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test CLIDetector.detectCLI returns correct isInstalled for mocked which output
- Test CLIDetector.detectCLI extracts version correctly from version command output
- Test CLIDetector.detectCLI handles timeout gracefully with error result
- Test CLIInstaller.checkDependencies identifies missing dependencies correctly
- Test CLIInstaller.install transitions through all states in correct order
- Test SupportedCLI.installCommand returns correct command for each CLI type
- Test PATH update logic does not duplicate existing entries

**Integration:**
- Test full detection flow spawns real processes and parses output (integration environment)
- Test full install flow for a test CLI in sandboxed environment
- Test bulk install correctly sequences multiple installations
- Test cancellation properly terminates spawned processes

**Ui:**
- Test CLI card renders correct state based on detection result
- Test Install button disabled during ongoing installation
- Test progress overlay appears and updates during installation
- Test error state shows correct message and enables Retry button
- Test Next button disabled when no CLIs installed
- Test VoiceOver announces correct status for each CLI card

**Perf:**
- Test parallel detection completes within 3 seconds for all 6 CLIs
- Test UI thread not blocked during Process spawn operations
- Test memory usage stays under 50MB during bulk installation

**Security:**
- Test shell command arguments are properly escaped to prevent injection
- Test PATH modifications are limited to appending safe paths
- Test no sensitive data logged during installation process

- Given Claude Code is installed at /usr/local/bin/claude, when detection runs, then Claude Code card shows Installed with correct version
