### E005-F003-S001-T005-A001 — Skills Recommendations Screen with Remote Registry Integration

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 2 days

> **Epic:** E005: Multi-CLI Hooks Architecture
> **Feature:** E005-F003: Onboarding Flow
> **Story:** E005-F003-S001: First-Run Setup Experience
> **Task:** E005-F003-S001-T005: Skills Recommendations Screen Implementation

#### Problem Statement
Users new to AI CLI tools may not know which skills (pre-built prompts, workflows, and configurations) are available or would benefit their workflow. Without curated recommendations filtered to their installed CLIs, users must manually discover and configure skills, reducing time-to-value and increasing onboarding friction.

#### Description
A SwiftUI view presenting a searchable, filterable grid of skill cards populated from a remote JSON registry, dynamically filtered to show only skills compatible with the user's detected CLIs, supporting multi-select checkbox behavior, category filtering, popularity sorting, and navigation via Skip and Next buttons.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Fetch skill metadata from remote registry endpoint (JSON over HTTPS)
- Parse skill registry response into local SkillCard models with id, name, description, category, for_cli array, stars count, downloads count, and recommended flag
- Display skills in a responsive grid layout with 2-3 columns based on window width
- Filter displayed skills to only those matching at least one installed CLI from previous detection screen
- Implement text search filtering across skill name and description fields
- Implement category filter dropdown with All plus unique categories from registry
- Sort skills by popularity using weighted score of stars and downloads
- Display Recommended badge on skills flagged as recommended in registry
- Implement checkbox selection state for each skill card with visual feedback
- Track selected skills in view model for later installation
- Provide Skip button that navigates forward without selecting any skills
- Provide Next button that navigates forward and queues selected skills for installation
- Show loading state while fetching registry data
- Show error state with retry option if registry fetch fails
- Cache registry response locally to avoid refetch on back navigation

**Out of Scope:**
- Actual skill installation logic - deferred to completion screen batch install
- Skill preview or detailed view modal - users see name, description, and badges only
- User-uploaded or custom skills - only registry-hosted skills shown
- Skill version management or updates - initial install only
- Offline skill bundle fallback - requires network for registry fetch
- Skill dependency resolution - skills are independent units
- Rating or review submission - read-only popularity metrics

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: On view appear, fetch skills registry from configured HTTPS endpoint using URLSession
1. FR2: Parse registry JSON response into array of SkillCard models with validation for required fields
1. FR3: Filter skills array to include only skills where for_cli array intersects with OnboardingState.detectedCLIs
1. FR4: Display filtered skills in a LazyVGrid with adaptive column sizing (minimum 280pt per card)
1. FR5: Each skill card shows name, truncated description (2 lines), category badge, star count, download count, Recommended badge if flagged, and selection checkbox
1. FR6: Implement search TextField that filters displayed skills by case-insensitive substring match on name or description
1. FR7: Implement category Picker that filters displayed skills by exact category match, with All option to show all
1. FR8: Sort displayed skills by popularity score calculated as (stars * 2) + downloads, descending
1. FR9: Checkbox tap toggles selection state for that skill and updates selectedSkills set in view model
1. FR10: Display count of selected skills in header area (e.g., 3 skills selected)
1. FR11: Skip button is always enabled and navigates to next onboarding screen without queuing any skills
1. FR12: Next button is always enabled (unlike CLI screen), navigates forward, and persists selectedSkills to OnboardingState
1. FR13: Show loading skeleton grid while registry fetch is in progress
1. FR14: Show error view with message and Retry button if registry fetch fails
1. FR15: Cache successful registry response in memory for session duration to handle back navigation

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Registry fetch completes within 5 seconds or times out with error state
- NFR2: JSON parsing and filtering complete within 100ms for up to 500 skills
- NFR3: Grid renders at 60fps during scroll with no frame drops
- NFR4: Memory usage for skill cards stays under 30MB for 500 skills
- NFR5: VoiceOver announces skill name, category, selection state, and badge status correctly
- NFR6: Search and filter operations complete within 50ms with no perceived lag

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create SkillsRecommendationsView.swift with @StateObject for SkillsRecommendationsViewModel
1. Step 2: Define SkillCard model struct conforming to Identifiable, Codable with fields: id (String), name (String), description (String), category (String), forCLIs ([String]), stars (Int), downloads (Int), isRecommended (Bool)
1. Step 3: Define SkillsRegistryResponse struct conforming to Codable wrapping array of SkillCard
1. Step 4: Create SkillsRecommendationsViewModel with Published properties: allSkills, filteredSkills, selectedSkillIDs, searchText, selectedCategory, loadingState
1. Step 5: Define LoadingState enum: idle, loading, loaded, error(String)
1. Step 6: Implement fetchRegistry async method using URLSession.shared.data(from:) with 5-second timeout configuration
1. Step 7: Implement parseRegistry method that decodes JSON and validates required fields
1. Step 8: Implement filterSkillsByCLI method that filters allSkills based on OnboardingState.detectedCLIs intersection
1. Step 9: Implement applyFilters method that chains CLI filter, search filter, category filter, and popularity sort
1. Step 10: Add Combine pipeline using Publishers.CombineLatest3 for searchText, selectedCategory, allSkills to trigger applyFilters
1. Step 11: Implement popularityScore computed property on SkillCard returning (stars * 2) + downloads
1. Step 12: Create SkillCardView subview with card background, name label, description text (lineLimit 2), category badge, stats row, recommended badge, and checkbox
1. Step 13: Implement checkbox toggle binding that adds/removes skill ID from selectedSkillIDs set
1. Step 14: Build header section with search TextField, category Picker, and selection count label
1. Step 15: Build main content with LazyVGrid using adaptive GridItem with minimum 280pt
1. Step 16: Create LoadingSkeletonGrid view showing 6 placeholder cards with shimmer animation
1. Step 17: Create ErrorStateView with error message and Retry button that calls fetchRegistry
1. Step 18: Create EmptyStateView for case when no skills match filters or no CLIs detected
1. Step 19: Wire Skip button to OnboardingCoordinator.advance() without modifying state
1. Step 20: Wire Next button to persist selectedSkillIDs to OnboardingState.selectedSkills then OnboardingCoordinator.advance()
1. Step 21: Add onAppear modifier to trigger fetchRegistry if loadingState is idle
1. Step 22: Implement registry response caching in view model to preserve data on back navigation
1. Step 23: Add telemetry calls for screen viewed, search performed, category changed, skills selected, skip pressed, next pressed
1. Step 24: Write unit tests for filtering logic, sorting logic, and selection state management
1. Step 25: Write UI tests for search interaction, category filtering, card selection, and navigation

**Files Touched:**

#### Commands

```bash
swift build
```

#### Data Model Changes
- Add SkillCard struct: id (String), name (String), description (String), category (String), forCLIs ([String]), stars (Int), downloads (Int), isRecommended (Bool), conforming to Identifiable, Codable, Hashable
- Add SkillsRegistryResponse struct: skills ([SkillCard]), version (String), updatedAt (String), conforming to Codable
- Add LoadingState enum: idle, loading, loaded, error(String)
- Extend OnboardingState with selectedSkills: Set<String> for persisting selected skill IDs across navigation

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- GET https://registry.blaze.app/v1/skills -> SkillsRegistryResponse JSON with 200 OK or error status
- SkillsRegistryService.fetchSkills() async throws -> [SkillCard] encapsulating network call and parsing
- SkillsRecommendationsViewModel.selectSkill(id: String) mutates selectedSkillIDs set
- SkillsRecommendationsViewModel.deselectSkill(id: String) mutates selectedSkillIDs set
- SkillsRecommendationsViewModel.commitSelection() persists selectedSkillIDs to OnboardingState.selectedSkills

**Event Contracts:**
- OnboardingEvent.skillsScreenViewed - emitted when view appears with detected CLI count
- OnboardingEvent.skillsRegistryFetchStarted - emitted when fetch begins
- OnboardingEvent.skillsRegistryFetchCompleted(count: Int) - emitted with number of skills loaded
- OnboardingEvent.skillsRegistryFetchFailed(error: String) - emitted on fetch failure
- OnboardingEvent.skillsSearchPerformed(query: String, resultCount: Int) - emitted on search with results
- OnboardingEvent.skillsCategoryChanged(category: String, resultCount: Int) - emitted on category filter change
- OnboardingEvent.skillSelected(skillId: String) - emitted when skill checkbox checked
- OnboardingEvent.skillDeselected(skillId: String) - emitted when skill checkbox unchecked
- OnboardingEvent.skillsScreenSkipped - emitted when Skip button pressed
- OnboardingEvent.skillsScreenCompleted(selectedCount: Int) - emitted when Next button pressed with selection count

#### UI States
- Loading state: Skeleton grid with 6 shimmer placeholder cards while fetching registry
- Loaded state: Grid of skill cards with search bar, category picker, and selection count header
- Empty state (no matches): Message explaining no skills match current filters with suggestion to clear filters
- Empty state (no CLIs): Message explaining skills require CLI detection first with Back button
- Error state: Error message with Retry button centered in content area
- Selected state: Skill cards show filled checkbox and highlighted border when selected

#### UI Interactions
- Type in search TextField to filter skills by name or description substring match
- Select category from Picker dropdown to filter skills by category
- Tap skill card checkbox to toggle selection state
- Tap skill card anywhere (not checkbox) to toggle selection state (convenience)
- Tap Skip button to proceed without selecting skills
- Tap Next button to proceed with selected skills queued for installation
- Tap Retry button in error state to re-attempt registry fetch
- Scroll grid vertically to view all filtered skills

#### Edge Cases
- Registry returns empty skills array - show empty state with message that no skills are available yet
- All skills are for CLIs user does not have installed - show empty state with guidance to install more CLIs
- User has zero detected CLIs - show specialized empty state with back navigation suggestion
- Registry returns malformed JSON - parse error handled as fetch error with retry option
- Network request times out - show timeout-specific error message
- User rapidly toggles same checkbox - debounce or ensure state consistency
- Search query matches no skills - show no matches state with clear suggestion
- User types very long search query - truncate display but use full query for filtering
- Registry returns skill with missing required field - skip that skill with warning log rather than failing entire parse
- User navigates back then forward - preserve cached registry data and selection state

#### Failure Modes
- Network unreachable during fetch - show error state with offline-specific messaging if detectable
- Registry endpoint returns 500 - show server error message with retry option
- Registry endpoint returns 404 - show configuration error message and log for investigation
- JSON decode fails - show parse error message and log raw response for debugging
- Memory pressure during large registry parse - handle gracefully with reduced parsing or pagination
- View model deallocated during async fetch - use weak self capture to prevent crashes
- Combine pipeline memory leak - ensure proper cancellable storage and cleanup

#### Rollback Plan
If Skills screen proves problematic, it can be bypassed by setting OnboardingState.skipSkillsScreen = true which causes OnboardingCoordinator to skip this step. Selected skills are only persisted to OnboardingState and not installed until completion screen, so no system changes occur from this screen. Registry caching is in-memory only with no persistent side effects.

### E005-F003-S001-T006-A001 — Plugins Recommendations Screen with Dynamic CLI-Based Filtering

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Multi-CLI Hooks Architecture
> **Feature:** E005-F003: Onboarding Flow
> **Story:** E005-F003-S001: First-Run Setup Experience
> **Task:** E005-F003-S001-T006: Plugins Recommendations Screen Implementation

#### Problem Statement
Users who have just installed AI CLIs may not know about useful plugins and extensions that enhance their workflow. Without guidance, they miss productivity improvements from tools like Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, Braintrust for Claude Code, or official extension catalogs for Gemini CLI. The onboarding flow should surface these recommendations contextually based on which CLIs the user has installed.

#### Description
A SwiftUI view that presents plugin recommendations organized by CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Aider), dynamically showing only sections for CLIs the user has installed. Each plugin is displayed as a card with name, description, install button, and status indicator. Installation triggers the appropriate package manager or opens external links for manual setup.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Display plugin recommendations grouped by installed CLI only
- Show Claude Code plugins section when Claude Code is installed: Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, Braintrust
- Show Gemini CLI section when Gemini CLI is installed: link to official extensions catalog
- Show Codex CLI section when Codex CLI is installed: MCP servers info, AGENTS.md guide link
- Show Aider section when Aider is installed: Git integration tips card
- Render each plugin as a card with icon, name, description, and install/view action button
- Track installation status per plugin (not installed, installing, installed)
- Handle plugin installation via npm, pip, brew, or external URL opening
- Persist plugin installation choices for session continuity
- Provide Skip button to bypass plugin installation entirely
- Provide Next button to proceed after reviewing recommendations

**Out of Scope:**
- Plugin configuration or settings after installation - deferred to CLI-specific settings
- Auto-updating plugins to newer versions - manual process
- Custom plugin discovery from registries - only curated recommendations shown
- Plugin uninstallation from this screen - handled elsewhere if needed
- Plugin compatibility validation - assume latest versions work
- Cross-CLI plugin sharing or dependencies - each CLI section is independent

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: On view appear, read installed CLIs from OnboardingState and filter plugin sections to only show relevant ones
1. FR2: Display Claude Code Plugins section with Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, and Braintrust cards when Claude Code is installed
1. FR3: Display Gemini CLI Extensions section with official catalog link card when Gemini CLI is installed
1. FR4: Display Codex CLI section with MCP servers card and AGENTS.md guide card when Codex CLI is installed
1. FR5: Display Aider section with Git integration tips card when Aider is installed
1. FR6: Each plugin card shows icon, name, brief description, and contextual action button
1. FR7: Action button for npm/pip installable plugins triggers installation with progress indicator
1. FR8: Action button for external links opens URL in default browser via NSWorkspace
1. FR9: Track installation status per plugin and update card UI to show Installed checkmark on success
1. FR10: Skip button navigates to next onboarding screen without installing any plugins
1. FR11: Next button navigates to next screen after user has reviewed recommendations
1. FR12: Show empty state with encouraging message if no CLIs are installed (edge case fallback)

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Initial render completes within 500ms with smooth animations for section reveals
- NFR2: Plugin installation feedback updates UI within 200ms of state change
- NFR3: Support VoiceOver with meaningful labels for all interactive elements
- NFR4: Respect system Reduce Motion preference for section reveal animations
- NFR5: Memory footprint stays under 20MB for plugin recommendation data structures

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create PluginsRecommendationsView.swift with @StateObject for PluginsRecommendationsViewModel
1. Step 2: Define PluginRecommendation struct with id, name, description, iconName, cliType, installType enum (npm, pip, brew, externalUrl), installCommand or url, and isInstalled
1. Step 3: Define PluginInstallType enum with cases: npmGlobal, pipInstall, brewInstall, externalUrl
1. Step 4: Define SupportedCLI extension or use existing enum to associate plugins with each CLI
1. Step 5: Create PluginsRecommendationsViewModel with Published properties: installedCLIs, pluginsBySection, installationStates
1. Step 6: Implement loadRecommendations method that reads OnboardingState.installedCLIs and builds filtered plugin list
1. Step 7: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Claude Code: Gastown (npm), Continuous-Claude-v2 (npm), Braintrust (npm)
1. Step 8: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Gemini CLI: Official Extensions Catalog (externalUrl)
1. Step 9: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Codex CLI: MCP Servers Guide (externalUrl), AGENTS.md Guide (externalUrl)
1. Step 10: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Aider: Git Integration Tips (externalUrl)
1. Step 11: Implement installPlugin async method that dispatches to appropriate installer based on PluginInstallType
1. Step 12: Create npmInstall helper that runs npm install -g packageName with progress tracking
1. Step 13: Create openExternalUrl helper that uses NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)
1. Step 14: Build PluginSectionView subview that renders section header and list of PluginCardView items
1. Step 15: Build PluginCardView subview with icon, name, description, and action button (Install or Open)
1. Step 16: Implement action button states: default (Install/Open), installing (spinner), installed (checkmark), error (retry)
1. Step 17: Add section reveal animation using withAnimation and staggered delays when motion is enabled
1. Step 18: Build empty state view shown when installedCLIs is empty with message to go back and install a CLI
1. Step 19: Wire up Skip button to call coordinator.navigateNext without installing anything
1. Step 20: Wire up Next button to call coordinator.navigateNext after logging selected plugins
1. Step 21: Add telemetry events for screen view, plugin install attempts, and navigation actions
1. Step 22: Write unit tests for PluginsRecommendationsViewModel filtering logic
1. Step 23: Write unit tests for plugin install method dispatch based on install type
1. Step 24: Write UI tests for section visibility based on mocked installedCLIs state

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Screens/PluginsRecommendationsView.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/ViewModels/PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Models/PluginRecommendation.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test --filter PluginsRecommendations
npm install -g gastown
npm install -g continuous-claude-v2
npm install -g braintrust
open https://gemini.google.com/extensions
```

#### Data Model Changes
- Add PluginRecommendation struct with fields: id (String), name (String), description (String), iconSystemName (String), cliType (SupportedCLI), installType (PluginInstallType), installCommand (String?), externalUrl (URL?), isRecommended (Bool)
- Add PluginInstallType enum with cases: npmGlobal, pipInstall, brewInstall, externalUrl
- Add PluginInstallState enum with cases: notInstalled, installing, installed, failed(Error)
- Add OnboardingState.selectedPlugins: [String] to persist user choices across sessions

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.loadRecommendations(installedCLIs: [SupportedCLI]) -> Void
- PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.installPlugin(plugin: PluginRecommendation) async throws -> Void
- PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.openExternalLink(url: URL) -> Void
- PluginInstaller.npmInstall(package: String, progressHandler: (Double) -> Void) async throws -> Void
- PluginInstaller.openUrl(url: URL) -> Bool

**Event Contracts:**
- OnboardingEvent.pluginsScreenViewed(installedCLIs: [SupportedCLI], sectionsShown: [String]) - emitted when screen appears with context
- OnboardingEvent.pluginInstallStarted(pluginId: String, pluginName: String, installType: PluginInstallType) - emitted when install begins
- OnboardingEvent.pluginInstallCompleted(pluginId: String, pluginName: String, success: Bool, error: String?) - emitted when install finishes
- OnboardingEvent.pluginExternalLinkOpened(pluginId: String, url: String) - emitted when external link is opened
- OnboardingEvent.pluginsScreenSkipped - emitted when user clicks Skip
- OnboardingEvent.pluginsScreenCompleted(installedPlugins: [String], viewedPlugins: [String]) - emitted when user clicks Next

#### UI States
- Loading state: Brief skeleton placeholders while filtering plugin sections (under 200ms)
- Populated state: Sections for each installed CLI with plugin cards rendered
- Empty state: Message indicating no CLIs installed with Back button to return to CLI detection
- Installing state: Individual plugin card shows spinner during installation
- Installed state: Plugin card shows green checkmark and Installed label
- Error state: Plugin card shows red indicator with error message and Retry button

#### UI Interactions
- Tap Install button on plugin card to trigger npm/pip/brew installation flow
- Tap Open button on external link plugin card to open URL in browser
- Tap Retry button on failed installation to re-attempt installation
- Tap Skip button to proceed without installing any plugins
- Tap Next button to proceed after reviewing and optionally installing plugins
- Tap Back button to return to previous onboarding screen
- Scroll vertically to view all plugin sections when content exceeds viewport

#### Edge Cases
- User has no CLIs installed - show empty state with Back button instead of empty sections
- All plugin installs fail - allow proceeding with warning toast about partial setup
- Network unavailable during npm install - detect offline and show offline-specific error message
- Plugin already globally installed from previous session - detect via npm list -g and show as Installed
- External URL returns 404 - cannot pre-validate, user sees browser error (acceptable)
- User rapidly taps Install on multiple plugins - queue installations to run sequentially
- Plugin npm package name changed - installation fails, show error with link to manual instructions

#### Failure Modes
- npm install fails due to permission denied - prompt user to fix npm permissions or use sudo (with warning)
- External URL open fails silently - log error but show success since browser opened
- Plugin version incompatible with installed CLI version - defer to plugin maintainer docs, not our problem
- Memory pressure during multiple installs - let system handle, our footprint is minimal
- Onboarding state corrupt and installedCLIs empty - treat as no CLIs, show empty state

#### Rollback Plan
Plugin installations can be rolled back via npm uninstall -g packageName or pip uninstall packageName. External link opens have no rollback needed. If this screen causes issues, it can be temporarily disabled in OnboardingCoordinator by skipping directly to next screen. User selections stored in OnboardingState can be cleared via UserDefaults.removeObject.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.loadRecommendations filters sections correctly for single installed CLI
- Test PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.loadRecommendations filters sections correctly for multiple installed CLIs
- Test PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.loadRecommendations returns empty sections array when no CLIs installed
- Test PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.installPlugin dispatches to npm for npmGlobal type
- Test PluginsRecommendationsViewModel.installPlugin dispatches to openUrl for externalUrl type
- Test PluginRecommendation model encodes and decodes correctly
- Test PluginInstallState transitions are valid (notInstalled -> installing -> installed)

**Integration:**
- Test full plugin install flow for Gastown npm package in sandboxed environment
- Test external URL opening triggers NSWorkspace.shared.open correctly
- Test section visibility updates when OnboardingState.installedCLIs changes
- Test Skip navigation triggers coordinator.navigateNext without modifications

**Ui:**
- Test Claude Code section appears when claudeCode is in installedCLIs
- Test Gemini CLI section hidden when geminiCLI not in installedCLIs
- Test plugin card Install button shows spinner during installing state
- Test plugin card shows checkmark after successful installation
- Test empty state view appears when installedCLIs is empty
- Test VoiceOver announces plugin name and install status correctly
- Test Skip and Next buttons are always enabled

**Perf:**
- Test initial render completes within 500ms with 4 sections visible
- Test UI thread not blocked during npm install process
- Test memory usage stays under 20MB with all sections expanded

**Security:**
- Test npm install commands are sanitized to prevent injection
- Test external URLs are validated before opening to block non-https schemes
- Test no sensitive data (npm tokens, paths) logged during installation

|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| plugins_screen_render_ms | histogram | milliseconds | <500 | Time from view appear to all sections rendered |
| plugin_install_duration_ms | histogram | milliseconds | <30000 | Time to complete single plugin installation |
| plugins_installed_count | gauge | count | >=1 | Number of plugins installed during onboarding |
| plugins_screen_skip_rate | gauge | percentage | <50 | Percentage of users who skip without installing any plugins |

- `onboarding.plugins_screen.section_shown`

- `onboarding.plugin.install_failed`

- Given user has only Aider installed, when plugins screen loads, then only Aider section is visible

### E005-F003-S001-T007-A001 — Agents Recommendations Screen with Filterable Grid

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Multi-CLI Hooks Architecture
> **Feature:** E005-F003: Onboarding Flow
> **Story:** E005-F003-S001: First-Run Setup Experience
> **Task:** E005-F003-S001-T007: Agents Recommendations Screen Implementation

#### Problem Statement
Users need to discover and select from available agent configurations during onboarding. Without a curated recommendations screen, users would need to manually configure agents after setup, creating friction and potentially missing valuable automation capabilities. A filterable grid enables quick discovery and selection based on intended use cases.

#### Description
A SwiftUI view presenting agent recommendations in a responsive grid layout with category filters (Planning, Debugging, Security, Performance, Documentation, Testing), checkbox selection for each agent, bulk select/deselect actions, and storage of user selections for post-onboarding configuration.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Display grid of agent cards with name, icon, description, and use case category
- Implement category filter bar to show agents by use case (All, Planning, Debugging, Security, Performance, Documentation, Testing)
- Enable checkbox selection on each agent card for multi-select behavior
- Provide Select All and Deselect All buttons for bulk actions
- Show selected count badge in header
- Store user selections in OnboardingState for later installation
- Support keyboard navigation between cards and filters
- Implement search field to filter agents by name or description
- Display agent capability tags on each card
- Navigate to next screen with Continue button

**Out of Scope:**
- Agent installation or configuration during this screen - deferred to completion screen
- Custom agent creation or editing - advanced feature for settings
- Agent preview or dry-run functionality - future enhancement
- Importing agents from external sources - deferred to settings
- Dependency checking between agents - all agents are independent for MVP
- Per-agent settings customization - handled in dedicated agent settings screen

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: On view appear, load agent catalog from bundled JSON and display all agents in responsive grid layout
1. FR2: Display category filter bar with All, Planning, Debugging, Security, Performance, Documentation, Testing options
1. FR3: Tapping a category filter animates grid to show only matching agents with smooth transition
1. FR4: Each agent card displays icon, name, description, category badge, capability tags, and selection checkbox
1. FR5: Tapping anywhere on agent card toggles its selection checkbox state
1. FR6: Header shows 'N agents selected' count that updates in real-time as selections change
1. FR7: Select All button selects all visible agents based on current filter
1. FR8: Deselect All button clears all selections regardless of current filter
1. FR9: Search field filters agents by name or description text with debounced 300ms delay
1. FR10: Continue button navigates to next onboarding screen and saves selections to OnboardingState
1. FR11: Back button preserves current selections when returning to previous screen
1. FR12: Keyboard arrow keys navigate between cards with visible focus ring

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Grid renders 20 agent cards within 100ms with no dropped frames
- NFR2: Filter animation completes within 300ms using matched geometry effect
- NFR3: Checkbox state change reflects in UI within 16ms (single frame)
- NFR4: Memory footprint stays under 30MB including all agent icon assets
- NFR5: VoiceOver reads card content in order: name, category, description, selection state
- NFR6: Search results update within 350ms of keystroke (300ms debounce + 50ms render)

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create AgentsRecommendationsView.swift with @StateObject for AgentsRecommendationsViewModel
1. Step 2: Define AgentCategory enum with cases: all, planning, debugging, security, performance, documentation, testing

#### Data Model Changes

- Add AgentRecommendation struct with fields: id (String), name (String), iconName (String), description (String), category (AgentCategory), tags ([String]), isRecommended (Bool)
- Add AgentCatalog class with agents array and filter methods
- Extend OnboardingState with selectedAgentIds: Set<String> property

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- AgentCatalog.shared.loadAgents() -> [AgentRecommendation]
- AgentCatalog.shared.agents(for category: AgentCategory) -> [AgentRecommendation]
- AgentCatalog.shared.search(query: String) -> [AgentRecommendation]

- AgentsRecommendationsViewModel.deselectAll() -> Void

**Event Contracts:**

#### UI States
- Loading state: Skeleton grid while agents.json loads (typically under 50ms so may not be visible)
- Default state: Grid showing all agents with All filter selected and no search text
- Filtered state: Grid showing only agents matching selected category with filter pill highlighted
- Search state: Grid showing only agents matching search query with search field active
- Empty state: Message shown if filter or search yields no results
- Selection state: Cards show checked state with header badge showing count

#### UI Interactions
- Tap category filter pill to filter grid to that category with animated transition
- Tap agent card anywhere to toggle its selection checkbox
- Tap checkbox directly on card to toggle selection (same as card tap)
- Type in search field to filter agents by name or description text
- Tap clear button in search field to reset search and show all
- Tap Select All to select all currently visible agents
- Tap Deselect All to clear all selections
- Press arrow keys to navigate between cards with keyboard
- Press Space or Enter on focused card to toggle selection
- Tap Continue to save selections and proceed to next screen
- Tap Back to return to previous screen preserving selections

#### Edge Cases
- User navigates back and forward - selections must persist across navigation
- User searches with no results then clears - grid restores to previous filter state
- User selects all then changes filter - only newly visible agents should be selected, not hidden ones
- User types very fast in search - debounce prevents excessive filtering calls
- User has no agents selected and taps Continue - allow proceeding with warning or confirmation
- agents.json missing or corrupt - show error state with retry option
- Category has zero agents defined - hide that filter option from bar
- Screen rotates during filter animation - animation should complete smoothly

#### Failure Modes
- agents.json fails to parse - show error state with message explaining bundled data issue and contact support
- Memory pressure during grid render - implement cell recycling via LazyVGrid
- VoiceOver skips cards - ensure all cards have proper accessibility identifiers and traits
- Keyboard focus lost after filter - restore focus to first visible card
- Selection state desyncs from UI - use single source of truth in ViewModel with Binding

#### Rollback Plan
Agent selections are stored only in OnboardingState which persists to UserDefaults. If issues occur, clear the selectedAgentIds key from UserDefaults to reset to default state. The agents.json catalog is bundled and immutable. No system changes occur on this screen - all actions are app-local.

**Perf:**

- Test filter animation completes in under 300ms
- Test search does not block main thread during debounce
- Test memory stays under 30MB with all agent icons loaded

**Security:**
- Test agents.json cannot be overwritten by user at runtime
- Test no user input is executed as code from search field
- Test agent IDs are sanitized before storage in UserDefaults

### E005-F003-S001-T008-A001 — Completion Screen with Summary and Tutorial Launch

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Multi-CLI Hooks Architecture
> **Feature:** E005-F003: Onboarding Flow
> **Story:** E005-F003-S001: First-Run Setup Experience
> **Task:** E005-F003-S001-T008: Completion Screen Implementation

#### Problem Statement
After completing all onboarding steps, users need clear confirmation that setup succeeded, a summary of what was configured, and a smooth transition to using the app. Without a proper completion screen, users may be uncertain whether onboarding finished correctly or feel abruptly dumped into the main app without context on what to do next.

#### Description
A SwiftUI view that celebrates successful onboarding completion with an animated success state, displays a summary of all installed CLIs and configured settings from previous screens, persists hasCompletedOnboarding to UserDefaults, triggers installation of any queued items, and provides two exit paths: Close to dismiss and start using Blaze, or Start Tutorial to launch the guided tour overlay.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Display animated success indicator when screen appears (checkmark with spring animation)
- Show summary section listing all installed CLIs from OnboardingState with version numbers
- Show summary section listing configured settings (theme choice, permissions granted)
- Show summary section listing installed starter packs or prompt libraries if any
- Display personalized welcome message using userName from OnboardingState
- Persist hasCompletedOnboarding = true to UserDefaults/@AppStorage on view appear
- Trigger background installation of any queued items (starter packs, prompt libraries)
- Provide Close button that dismisses onboarding and reveals main app ContentView
- Provide Start Tutorial button that dismisses onboarding and activates TutorialOverlayView
- Add confetti or celebratory animation that respects accessibilityReduceMotion
- Track screen view and button taps via telemetry events

**Out of Scope:**
- Actual implementation of TutorialOverlayView - separate atom handles tutorial infrastructure
- Deep configuration of installed CLIs - handled in subsequent first-run flows
- Account creation or cloud sync setup - future feature not in MVP
- Walkthrough of specific Blaze features - deferred to tutorial overlay
- Recovery flow if onboarding was incomplete - handled by OnboardingCoordinator guard

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: On view appear, immediately set hasCompletedOnboarding = true in @AppStorage
1. FR2: Display animated checkmark success indicator with spring animation scale 0.5 to 1.0 over 0.6 seconds
1. FR3: Show optional confetti animation that auto-dismisses after 3 seconds, respecting accessibilityReduceMotion
1. FR4: Display summary card titled 'Ready to Code' with list of installed CLIs showing name and version
1. FR5: Display summary card titled 'Your Settings' with configured theme, permissions, and preferences
1. FR6: Display summary card titled 'Installed Packs' with any starter packs or prompt libraries selected (or hide if none)
1. FR7: Show personalized greeting 'Welcome, {userName}!' using OnboardingState.userName
1. FR8: Trigger OnboardingCoordinator.installQueuedItems() async on appear to process any pending installations
1. FR9: Close button dismisses onboarding full screen cover and transitions to main ContentView
1. FR10: Start Tutorial button dismisses onboarding and sets showTutorial = true to activate tutorial overlay
1. FR11: If queued installations fail, show non-blocking toast with retry option
1. FR12: Emit telemetry events for screen view, close tap, and tutorial tap with timing data

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Screen renders within 100ms of navigation to avoid perceived lag
- NFR2: Success animation completes within 600ms with smooth 60fps rendering
- NFR3: Background installations do not cause UI jank or dropped frames
- NFR4: Summary cards render correctly with 1 to 10 items without scrolling issues
- NFR5: VoiceOver reads summary items in logical order with proper grouping
- NFR6: Memory footprint stays under 30MB including animation assets

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create CompletionOnboardingView.swift file with struct conforming to View protocol
1. Step 2: Add @AppStorage property wrapper for hasCompletedOnboarding Bool flag
1. Step 3: Add @EnvironmentObject for OnboardingState to access detection results and settings
1. Step 4: Add @Binding properties for isPresented (dismiss onboarding) and showTutorial (activate tutorial)
1. Step 5: Create CompletionViewModel class with @Published properties for installationProgress and installationError
1. Step 6: Implement success checkmark view using SF Symbol checkmark.circle.fill with scale animation modifier
1. Step 7: Create ConfettiView using Canvas and TimelineView for particle animation respecting reduceMotion
1. Step 8: Build SummaryCard reusable view with title String and items array of SummaryItem (icon, text)
1. Step 9: Create CLISummaryCard that maps OnboardingState.detectedCLIs to SummaryItems with version text
1. Step 10: Create SettingsSummaryCard that extracts theme choice and permissions from OnboardingState
1. Step 11: Create PacksSummaryCard that shows installed starter packs or returns EmptyView if none
1. Step 12: Implement personalized greeting text view with userName interpolation and fallback
1. Step 13: Add onAppear modifier that sets hasCompletedOnboarding = true
1. Step 14: Add task modifier that calls viewModel.installQueuedItems() for background installation
1. Step 15: Create CloseButton view with 'Get Started' label and action dismissing isPresented
1. Step 16: Create TutorialButton view with 'Start Tutorial' label and action setting showTutorial true then dismissing
1. Step 17: Implement toast overlay for installation errors with retry button
1. Step 18: Add telemetry calls in onAppear, CloseButton action, and TutorialButton action
1. Step 19: Compose all views in body with VStack layout, proper spacing, and scroll view wrapper
1. Step 20: Add accessibility modifiers including accessibilityLabel for summary cards and button hints
1. Step 21: Wire CompletionOnboardingView into OnboardingRootView navigation flow as final step
1. Step 22: Write unit tests for CompletionViewModel installation logic
1. Step 23: Write UI tests for summary rendering and button actions

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Screens/CompletionOnboardingView.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/ViewModels/CompletionViewModel.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Views/SummaryCard.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Views/ConfettiView.swift`

#### Commands

```bash
swift build
swift test --filter Completion
xcodebuild test -scheme Blaze -destination 'platform=macOS'
xcrun simctl boot 'Mac'
```

#### Data Model Changes
- Add SummaryItem struct with fields: icon (String SF Symbol name), title (String), subtitle (String optional) for summary card rows
- Add CompletionState enum: loading, ready, installingQueued, completed, error(String) for view state management
- Extend OnboardingState with computed property summaryItems: [SummaryItem] aggregating all configured items
- Add InstallationResult struct with fields: itemName (String), success (Bool), error (String optional)

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CompletionViewModel.installQueuedItems() async -> [InstallationResult] - processes pending installations
- CompletionViewModel.retryFailedInstallations() async -> [InstallationResult] - retries failed items
- OnboardingCoordinator.completeOnboarding() -> Void - finalizes onboarding state and transitions out
- OnboardingCoordinator.launchTutorial() -> Void - dismisses onboarding and activates tutorial overlay
- OnboardingState.summaryItems: [SummaryItem] - computed property returning all summary data

**Event Contracts:**
- OnboardingEvent.completionScreenViewed - emitted when completion screen appears
- OnboardingEvent.onboardingCompleted(duration: TimeInterval, cliCount: Int, packsCount: Int) - emitted after hasCompletedOnboarding set
- OnboardingEvent.completionClosePressed - emitted when user taps Close/Get Started button
- OnboardingEvent.completionTutorialPressed - emitted when user taps Start Tutorial button
- OnboardingEvent.queuedInstallationStarted(itemCount: Int) - emitted when background install begins
- OnboardingEvent.queuedInstallationCompleted(successCount: Int, failureCount: Int) - emitted when install finishes
- OnboardingEvent.queuedInstallationRetried - emitted when user retries failed installations

#### UI States
- Initial state: Success animation playing, summary cards loading
- Ready state: Animation complete, summary cards displayed with data, buttons enabled
- Installing state: Background installation in progress, subtle progress indicator in corner
- Completed state: All installations done, full summary visible, ready to dismiss
- Error state: Toast overlay showing installation failures with retry option

#### UI Interactions
- View appear triggers success animation and hasCompletedOnboarding persistence
- Confetti animation plays automatically and dismisses after 3 seconds (skipped if reduceMotion)
- Tap Close/Get Started button dismisses onboarding and shows main app
- Tap Start Tutorial button dismisses onboarding and activates tutorial overlay
- Tap Retry in error toast retries failed background installations
- Scroll vertically if summary content exceeds visible height

#### Edge Cases
- User skipped all optional screens - show minimal summary with just detected CLIs
- No CLIs were detected or installed - show message suggesting to install one from settings
- userName is empty or nil - use generic greeting 'Welcome!' without name
- All queued installations fail - show error toast but do not block Close action
- OnboardingState is nil or corrupted - show error state with option to restart onboarding
- Device in low power mode - skip confetti animation to conserve resources
- Screen appears via deep link or restoration - re-check hasCompletedOnboarding before showing

#### Failure Modes
- UserDefaults write fails - retry with exponential backoff, alert if persistent failure
- Background installation task cancelled on dismiss - allow pending items to complete
- Animation assets fail to load - fall back to static checkmark image
- OnboardingCoordinator reference is nil - log error and allow manual dismiss
- Memory pressure during confetti animation - gracefully degrade to no animation
- Tutorial view not available - disable Start Tutorial button and show tooltip explaining

#### Rollback Plan
If completion screen causes crashes or data corruption, revert to previous onboarding flow version. hasCompletedOnboarding flag can be reset via Settings > Developer > Reset Onboarding for users who experienced issues. Queued installations that failed can be retried from Settings > Installed Packs.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test hasCompletedOnboarding is set to true on view appear
- Test summaryItems correctly aggregates CLIs from OnboardingState
- Test summaryItems correctly aggregates settings from OnboardingState
- Test summaryItems handles empty OnboardingState gracefully
- Test CompletionViewModel.installQueuedItems processes items correctly
- Test CompletionViewModel handles installation failures without crashing
- Test personalized greeting falls back when userName is nil
- Test confetti animation respects accessibilityReduceMotion setting

**Integration:**
- Test full onboarding flow ends at completion screen with correct state
- Test Close button dismisses onboarding and shows ContentView
- Test Start Tutorial button activates TutorialOverlayView after dismiss
- Test background installations complete successfully for real packages
- Test telemetry events fire with correct parameters

**Ui:**
- Test success animation renders at 60fps without dropped frames
- Test summary cards display correct content from OnboardingState
- Test both buttons are visible and tappable without overlap
- Test error toast appears and Retry button functions correctly
- Test VoiceOver reads summary items in correct order
- Test scroll behavior when summary content is long

**Perf:**
- Test screen renders within 100ms of navigation
- Test animation completes within 600ms
- Test background installation does not block UI thread
- Test memory stays under 30MB including animations

**Security:**
- Test hasCompletedOnboarding cannot be spoofed by external apps
- Test queued installation items are validated before execution
- Test no sensitive data exposed in telemetry events

### E005-F002-S001-T002-A001 — Unread Badge UI Rendering

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** Multi-CLI Hooks Architecture
> **Feature:** Session Activity and Unread Tracking
> **Story:** Unread Badge System
> **Task:** Implement Unread Badge UI Component

#### Problem Statement
Users managing multiple concurrent CLI sessions have no visual indicator of which sessions have accumulated new events since they last viewed them. This forces users to manually click through each session to discover activity, wasting time and causing missed important events in background sessions.

#### Description
Implement the visual badge component that displays unread event counts on session rows in the sidebar. This includes the CountBadge view component, conditional visibility logic, and proper integration with the existing SessionRow layout structure.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- CountBadge SwiftUI view component implementation with configurable count display
- Conditional badge visibility logic based on unread count and active session state
- Integration of CountBadge into existing SessionRow component layout
- Badge styling following design system color tokens and typography
- Accessibility labels for screen reader support on badge element

**Out of Scope:**
- Unread count calculation logic from event stream (handled by T001)
- Badge animation or transitions when count changes (future enhancement)
- Badge click interactions or navigation behavior
- Notification system integration for OS-level alerts
- Badge persistence across app restarts

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: CountBadge displays integer count value when initialized with count > 0
1. FR2: CountBadge renders as empty view when count equals 0
1. FR3: SessionRow shows CountBadge only when session has unread events AND is not the current session
1. FR4: Badge displays 99+ for counts exceeding 99 to prevent layout overflow
1. FR5: Badge background uses accent color from design system theme
1. FR6: Badge text uses contrasting foreground color for readability

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Badge render time must not exceed 1ms to maintain 60fps scroll performance
- NFR2: Badge accessibility label must include exact count for screen readers
- NFR3: Badge must maintain visual consistency across light and dark themes

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create CountBadge.swift in Blaze/Sources/DesignSystem/Components with View protocol conformance
1. Step 2: Implement CountBadge body with Text view displaying formatted count string
1. Step 3: Add capsule background shape with design system accent color fill
1. Step 4: Implement count formatting logic to show 99+ for large values
1. Step 5: Add conditional @ViewBuilder logic to return EmptyView when count is 0
1. Step 6: Add accessibilityLabel modifier with descriptive count text
1. Step 7: Modify SessionRow.swift to inject UnreadTracker dependency
1. Step 8: Add computed property to SessionRow for shouldShowBadge based on unread count and active state
1. Step 9: Insert CountBadge in SessionRow HStack after Spacer and before HoverButtons
1. Step 10: Verify badge visibility toggles correctly when switching sessions

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Sidebar/SessionsSidebarView.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Sidebar/SessionRow.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/DesignSystem/Components/CountBadge.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test --filter CountBadgeTests
swift test --filter SessionRowTests
```

#### Data Model Changes
- No persistent data model changes - badge reads from in-memory UnreadTracker state

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CountBadge.init(count: Int) - Initializes badge with display count
- UnreadTracker.currentUnreadCount(for sessionId: UUID) -> Int - Returns unread count for session

**Event Contracts:**
- No new events emitted - badge is purely reactive to existing UnreadTracker state changes

#### UI States
- BadgeVisible: Count > 0 and session is not active - shows filled capsule with white count text
- BadgeHidden: Count = 0 OR session is active - renders EmptyView with zero frame
- BadgeOverflow: Count > 99 - displays 99+ text to prevent layout expansion

#### UI Interactions
- Badge appears when background session receives events while user views different session
- Badge disappears when user switches to that session (becomes active)
- Badge updates count in real-time as new events arrive in background session

#### Edge Cases
- EC1: Count exactly 99 displays 99 not 99+
- EC2: Count of 100 or higher displays 99+
- EC3: Session becomes active while badge visible - badge immediately hides
- EC4: Rapid count updates do not cause flickering or layout thrashing
- EC5: Empty session list renders without errors when no badges to display

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: UnreadTracker unavailable - badge renders as hidden with warning log
- FM2: Invalid session ID - badge renders as hidden gracefully without crash

#### Rollback Plan
Remove CountBadge.swift file and revert SessionRow.swift changes. Badge feature disabled with no user-facing errors. Sessions sidebar returns to previous appearance without unread indicators.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- test_CountBadge_displaysCount_whenPositive: Verify badge shows 5 when initialized with 5
- test_CountBadge_displaysOverflow_whenAbove99: Verify badge shows 99+ when initialized with 150
- test_CountBadge_hidesCompletely_whenZero: Verify badge returns EmptyView when count is 0
- test_CountBadge_accessibilityLabel_includesExactCount: Verify label reads 5 unread events for count 5

**Integration:**
- test_SessionRow_showsBadge_whenUnreadAndNotActive: Full row renders badge when conditions met
- test_SessionRow_hidesBadge_whenActive: Active session row never shows badge regardless of count
- test_SessionsSidebar_badgesUpdateOnTrackerChange: Published unread changes propagate to UI

**Ui:**
- UI_Badge_Visible: Screenshot test showing badge on inactive session with unread events
- UI_Badge_Hidden: Screenshot test showing active session without badge
- UI_Badge_Theme: Visual comparison of badge in light vs dark theme

**Perf:**
- test_CountBadge_renderTime_under1ms: Benchmark badge instantiation and body computation
- test_SessionsSidebar_scrollPerformance_withManyBadges: 60fps maintained with 50 sessions showing badges

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| badge_render_count | counter | renders | No specific target - observational | Track how often badges are rendered to detect unnecessary re-renders |
| badge_max_count_displayed | gauge | count | <100 typical | Track highest unread count shown to validate 99+ overflow logic |

#### Telemetry Events
- `badge_displayed: Fires when badge becomes visible with session_id and count properties`
- `badge_hidden: Fires when badge hides due to session becoming active`

#### Acceptance Tests
- AT1: Given a background session with 5 new events, when viewing the sessions sidebar, then a badge showing 5 appears on that session row
- AT2: Given viewing a session with unread events, when that session becomes active, then the badge immediately disappears
- AT3: Given a session with 150 unread events, when viewing the sidebar, then the badge displays 99+ not 150

#### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: CountBadge component exists and compiles without errors
- [ ] AC2: Badge displays correct count for values 1-99
- [ ] AC3: Badge displays 99+ for values 100 and above
- [ ] AC4: Badge is hidden when count is 0
- [ ] AC5: Badge is hidden for the currently active session
- [ ] AC6: All unit and integration tests pass
- [ ] AC7: VoiceOver reads badge count correctly

#### Definition of Done
- [ ] CountBadge.swift created with full implementation
- [ ] SessionRow.swift modified to include badge conditionally
- [ ] All CountBadgeTests pass
- [ ] All SessionRowTests pass
- [ ] Manual verification shows badge appearing and hiding correctly
- [ ] Code review approved

**Requires:** Tests, Telemetry, Error Handling, Rollback Plan

#### Completion
**Completed When:** CountBadge component renders unread counts in SessionRow, hides appropriately for active sessions and zero counts, and all automated tests pass.

**Evidence:** swift test output showing CountBadgeTests and SessionRowTests green. Screenshot of sidebar showing badge on one session row with count visible.

## Phase 2: Core Features

_1 atoms in this phase_

| ID | Atom | Status | Priority | Risk |

| E005-F002-S001-T004-A001 | Badge Animation | planned | should | low |

### E005-F002-S001-T004-A001 — Badge Animation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** Remote Registry and CLI Onboarding
> **Feature:** Sidebar Navigation Badges
> **Story:** Unread Badge Indicators
> **Task:** Badge Animation Implementation

#### Problem Statement
When new events arrive in background sessions, users need visual attention cues to notice the badge count change. Static badges are easy to miss, especially in peripheral vision. Animation provides a non-intrusive way to draw attention, but must be disabled for users with motion sensitivity preferences.

#### Description
Add CSS-style pulse animation to unread badges when count increases, with automatic detection and respect for macOS accessibilityReduceMotion system preference.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Implement subtle pulse animation on badge when unread count increases
- Implement fade-in animation for badge appearance when count goes from 0 to 1
- Detect and respect macOS accessibilityReduceMotion system preference
- Use SwiftUI animation modifiers with appropriate duration and easing
- Animation triggers only on count increase, not on count decrease or reset

**Out of Scope:**
- Badge count calculation logic (handled by T001-A001)
- Badge styling and theming (handled by T002-A001)
- Continuous or looping animations
- Sound or haptic feedback
- Animation preferences beyond system reduce motion setting

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: Badge pulses with scale animation (1.0 to 1.15 to 1.0) when unread count increases
1. FR2: Badge fades in with opacity animation (0.0 to 1.0) when transitioning from 0 to non-zero count
1. FR3: Animation is completely disabled when accessibilityReduceMotion is enabled
1. FR4: Animation triggers only on count increase, not on decrease or manual reset
1. FR5: Multiple rapid count increases coalesce into single animation cycle

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Animation completes within 300ms total duration
- NFR2: Animation uses easeOut timing curve for natural deceleration feel
- NFR3: Animation does not impact scroll performance in sidebar list
- NFR4: Zero CPU usage when animation is not active

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create BadgeAnimationModifier ViewModifier that encapsulates pulse and fade animations
1. Step 2: Add @State property to track previous unread count for change detection
1. Step 3: Implement onChange handler to detect count increases and trigger animation
1. Step 4: Query NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion at animation trigger time
1. Step 5: Apply scaleEffect and opacity modifiers with withAnimation block
1. Step 6: Add animation completion callback to reset animation state
1. Step 7: Integrate BadgeAnimationModifier into UnreadBadgeView
1. Step 8: Test animation behavior with Accessibility Inspector reduce motion toggle

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Components/UnreadBadgeView.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Sidebar/SessionRowView.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Components/BadgeAnimationModifier.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test --filter BadgeAnimationTests
open -a 'Accessibility Inspector'
```

#### Data Model Changes
- N/A - Animation is purely presentational with no data model impact

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- BadgeAnimationModifier.init(triggerCount: Int, reduceMotion: Bool)
- BadgeAnimationModifier.body(content: Content) -> some View

**Event Contracts:**
- N/A - Animation does not emit events, only responds to count changes

#### UI States
- Idle state: Badge displayed at normal scale (1.0) and full opacity (1.0)
- Pulse animating state: Badge scales from 1.0 to 1.15 over 150ms then back to 1.0 over 150ms
- Fade-in animating state: Badge opacity transitions from 0.0 to 1.0 over 200ms
- Reduce motion state: All animations disabled, immediate state changes only

#### UI Interactions
- System receives new event in background session, badge count increases, pulse animation triggers
- User enables Reduce Motion in System Preferences, animation stops immediately
- User switches to session, count resets to 0, no animation on decrease
- Multiple events arrive rapidly, single coalesced pulse animation plays

#### Edge Cases
- Count increases by more than 1 in single update: single pulse animation, not multiple
- Count increases while animation already playing: queue next animation after current completes
- View disappears mid-animation: animation completes in background without crash
- Reduce motion toggled mid-animation: current animation completes, future animations disabled
- Badge removed from view hierarchy during animation: no crash or leak

#### Failure Modes
- Animation fails to trigger: Badge still displays correct count, user sees static badge (graceful degradation)
- Reduce motion check fails: Default to showing animation (safer than hiding important feedback)
- Animation duration exceeds 300ms: Use transaction timeout to force completion

#### Rollback Plan
Remove BadgeAnimationModifier import and usage from UnreadBadgeView.swift, delete BadgeAnimationModifier.swift file, badge reverts to static display without animation.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test BadgeAnimationModifier triggers animation when count increases from 0 to 1
- Test BadgeAnimationModifier triggers animation when count increases from 5 to 8
- Test BadgeAnimationModifier does not trigger animation when count decreases from 3 to 0
- Test BadgeAnimationModifier does not trigger animation when count stays same
- Test BadgeAnimationModifier respects reduceMotion parameter when true
- Test animation coalescing when multiple count updates arrive within 100ms

**Integration:**
- Test full flow: SessionStore count update triggers badge animation in SessionRowView
- Test reduce motion integration: Toggle system preference and verify animation behavior changes

**Ui:**
- Visual verification: Badge pulse animation is visible and smooth
- Visual verification: Badge fade-in animation appears natural
- Visual verification: No animation plays when Reduce Motion enabled in System Preferences

**Perf:**
- Verify animation does not cause dropped frames during sidebar scroll
- Verify zero CPU usage when badge is idle with no count changes
- Measure animation duration stays within 300ms budget

**Security:**
- N/A - Animation modifier has no security surface

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| badge_animation_duration_ms | timer | ms | <300 | Track actual animation duration to ensure it stays within budget |
| badge_animation_skipped_count | counter | count | monitoring only | Track how often animations are skipped due to reduce motion preference |

#### Telemetry Events
- `badge_animation_triggered`
- `badge_animation_skipped_reduce_motion`

#### Acceptance Tests
- Given a session with 0 unread events, when 1 event arrives, then badge fades in with opacity animation
- Given a session with 3 unread events, when 2 more events arrive, then badge pulses once with scale animation
- Given Reduce Motion is enabled in System Preferences, when events arrive, then badge updates without any animation
- Given animation is in progress, when additional events arrive, then only one animation cycle plays

#### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pulse animation scales badge to 1.15x and back within 300ms total duration
- [ ] Fade-in animation transitions opacity from 0 to 1 within 200ms
- [ ] Animation is completely disabled when accessibilityReduceMotion is enabled
- [ ] No animation triggers on count decrease or reset to zero
- [ ] All unit tests pass with animation timing verified

#### Definition of Done
- [ ] BadgeAnimationModifier.swift compiles without warnings
- [ ] All unit tests pass including animation trigger conditions
- [ ] Integration test verifies SessionStore to animation flow
- [ ] Manual QA confirms animation is visually smooth and non-intrusive
- [ ] Manual QA confirms Reduce Motion preference is respected

**Requires:** Tests, Telemetry, Error Handling, Rollback Plan

#### Completion
**Completed When:** Badge animation triggers on count increase, respects reduce motion preference, and all tests pass.

**Evidence:** Unit test BadgeAnimationTests passes, visual demo video shows pulse animation, Accessibility Inspector confirms reduce motion respected.

#### Source References
- docs/new-features-v2.md section F002 S004-ANIMATION

#### Open Questions
- Should animation trigger on app becoming active if count changed while in background?
- Should there be a user preference to disable animation independent of system reduce motion?

#### Notes
Animation is intentionally subtle to avoid being annoying. Pulse scale of 1.15x was chosen based on Apple HIG recommendations for attention-drawing without alarm. Duration of 300ms matches system alert animations.

## Phase 2: Multi-Provider Hooks

_1 atoms in this phase_

| ID | Atom | Status | Priority | Risk |
|----|------|--------|----------|------|
| E005-F004-S001-T002-A001 | Per-Provider Event Definitions | planned | must | low |

### E005-F004-S001-T002-A001 — Per-Provider Event Definitions

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1 days

> **Epic:** Remote Repository and CLI Onboarding
> **Feature:** Multi-Provider Hook System
> **Story:** Per-Provider Hook Schema Definitions
> **Task:** Hook Schema Type Definitions

#### Problem Statement
The hook system currently has no type-safe representation of which hook events exist for each CLI provider. Without per-provider event definitions, the hook builder cannot validate event names, cannot filter matchers appropriately, cannot indicate which events support blocking responses, and cannot support cross-provider hook migration with correct event name mapping.

#### Description
Create comprehensive Swift type definitions in HookSchema.swift encoding all hook event types for Claude Code (12 events), Gemini CLI (11 events), and Codex CLI (2 notify events), including which events support blocking, which matchers are valid per event, and tool name mappings between providers.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- HookProvider enum with cases claude, gemini, codex representing supported CLI providers
- ClaudeHookEventType enum with 12 events: SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, Notification, PermissionRequest, ErrorOccurred, ContextCompacted
- GeminiHookEventType enum with 11 events: BeforeTool, AfterTool, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, BeforeModel, AfterModel, BeforeToolSelection, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreCompress, Notification
- CodexHookEventType enum with 2 events: AgentTurnComplete, ApprovalRequested
- HookEventCapability struct defining canBlock, availableMatchers, description per event
- HookToolNameMapping struct for cross-provider tool name translation
- Static dictionaries mapping event types to their capabilities per provider

**Out of Scope:**
- Hook execution logic - handled by HookRunner in separate atom
- Hook configuration persistence - handled by MultiProviderHooksService
- Hook builder UI - handled by HooksBuilderView atoms
- Hook migration utilities - handled by H007-MIGRATE atom
- Runtime event dispatching - handled by engine adapters

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-01: HookProvider enum distinguishes between claude, gemini, and codex CLI backends
1. FR-02: Each provider has dedicated event type enum with all supported events
1. FR-03: HookEventCapability struct indicates if event can block execution flow
1. FR-04: HookEventCapability includes array of valid matcher patterns per event
1. FR-05: HookEventCapability includes human-readable description for UI display
1. FR-06: HookToolNameMapping provides bidirectional mapping between provider tool names
1. FR-07: Static factory methods return capabilities for any event on any provider
1. FR-08: Events that take matchers define valid matcher patterns as enum or string array
1. FR-09: SessionStart events include startup, resume, clear, compact matcher options
1. FR-10: Tool events include tool name patterns as matchers

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-01: All types must be Sendable for safe concurrent access
- NFR-02: All types must be Codable for JSON serialization
- NFR-03: Enum raw values must match CLI config file expectations exactly
- NFR-04: Type definitions compile to zero runtime overhead via static dispatch
- NFR-05: Documentation comments on each type for code completion hints

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create HookProvider enum with cases claude, gemini, codex and rawValue String matching CLI names
1. Step 2: Add HookProvider computed properties for displayName, configFileName, and supportsBlocking
1. Step 3: Create ClaudeHookEventType enum with all 12 Claude Code events as cases with String raw values
1. Step 4: Add ClaudeHookEventType computed property canBlock returning true for UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest
1. Step 5: Add ClaudeHookEventType computed property matcherType returning SessionStartMatcher, ToolMatcher, or nil
1. Step 6: Create GeminiHookEventType enum with all 11 Gemini CLI events as cases with String raw values
1. Step 7: Add GeminiHookEventType computed property canBlock returning true for BeforeTool, BeforeAgent, BeforeModel, BeforeToolSelection
1. Step 8: Add GeminiHookEventType computed property matcherType for tool and session matchers
1. Step 9: Create CodexHookEventType enum with 2 notify events: agentTurnComplete, approvalRequested
1. Step 10: Add CodexHookEventType computed property canBlock always returning false
1. Step 11: Create HookEventCapability struct with canBlock, matchers, description, and provider fields
1. Step 12: Create SessionStartMatcher enum with cases startup, resume, clear, compact for session lifecycle events
1. Step 13: Create ToolMatcher struct with pattern String for glob-style tool name matching
1. Step 14: Create HookToolNameMapping struct with from, to provider fields and tool name dictionaries
1. Step 15: Add static HookToolNameMapping.claudeToGemini and HookToolNameMapping.geminiToClaude instances
1. Step 16: Create HookEventRegistry struct with static methods to get all events for a provider
1. Step 17: Add HookEventRegistry.capabilities(for event, provider) returning HookEventCapability
1. Step 18: Add Codable, Hashable, Sendable conformances to all public types
1. Step 19: Add documentation comments with event descriptions and matcher examples
1. Step 20: Write unit tests verifying event counts, blocking flags, and matcher associations

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookEventTypes.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookSchema.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookToolNameMapping.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookEventRegistry.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test --filter HookSchemaTests
swift test --filter HookEventRegistryTests
```

#### Data Model Changes
- Add HookProvider enum: claude, gemini, codex with String rawValue
- Add ClaudeHookEventType enum with 12 cases matching Claude Code hook events
- Add GeminiHookEventType enum with 11 cases matching Gemini CLI hook events
- Add CodexHookEventType enum with 2 cases for notify events
- Add HookEventCapability struct: canBlock Bool, matchers [String], description String
- Add SessionStartMatcher enum: startup, resume, clear, compact
- Add ToolMatcher struct: pattern String for glob matching
- Add HookToolNameMapping struct: mapping dictionaries between providers

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- HookProvider.allCases -> [HookProvider] via CaseIterable
- ClaudeHookEventType.allCases -> [ClaudeHookEventType] via CaseIterable
- GeminiHookEventType.allCases -> [GeminiHookEventType] via CaseIterable
- CodexHookEventType.allCases -> [CodexHookEventType] via CaseIterable
- HookEventRegistry.events(for provider: HookProvider) -> [any HookEventType]
- HookEventRegistry.capability(for event: any HookEventType) -> HookEventCapability
- HookToolNameMapping.translate(toolName: String, from: HookProvider, to: HookProvider) -> String?

**Event Contracts:**
- No runtime events emitted; these are compile-time type definitions
- Types are used by HookRunner to validate hook configurations
- Types are used by HooksBuilderView to populate event picker dropdown

#### UI States
- N/A - this atom defines data types only, no UI components
- Types will be consumed by HooksBuilderView event type picker in H005-UIPROVIDER atom

#### UI Interactions
- N/A - no direct UI interactions in this atom
- Event type enums will populate picker options in hook builder UI

#### Edge Cases
- Unknown event type string from config file: return nil from init?(rawValue:) and handle gracefully
- Provider does not support blocking: canBlock always returns false for all events
- Tool matcher pattern is empty: treat as match-all pattern
- Codex provider selected: show only 2 notify events, indicate no blocking support
- Event name case sensitivity: rawValue must match CLI expectations exactly

#### Failure Modes
- JSON decoding fails for unknown event: Codable init throws, wrap in try/catch
- Event enum exhaustive switch incomplete: compiler error catches at build time
- Tool name mapping missing entry: return nil and use original name as fallback
- Memory allocation for static registries: negligible, all types are value types

#### Rollback Plan
Delete HookSchema.swift, HookToolNameMapping.swift, and HookEventRegistry.swift. Remove HookProvider enum if only used by this atom. Hook builder falls back to hardcoded event strings without type safety. Existing hook configurations remain valid JSON but lose compile-time validation.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test HookProvider.allCases contains exactly claude, gemini, codex
- Test ClaudeHookEventType.allCases count equals 12
- Test GeminiHookEventType.allCases count equals 11
- Test CodexHookEventType.allCases count equals 2
- Test ClaudeHookEventType.preToolUse.canBlock returns true
- Test ClaudeHookEventType.postToolUse.canBlock returns false
- Test GeminiHookEventType.beforeTool.canBlock returns true
- Test CodexHookEventType.agentTurnComplete.canBlock returns false
- Test SessionStartMatcher.allCases contains startup, resume, clear, compact
- Test HookToolNameMapping.translate Bash to run_shell_command for claude to gemini
- Test HookToolNameMapping.translate returns nil for unknown tool names
- Test HookEventCapability Codable round-trip preserves all fields
- Test all event type enums are Sendable compilable

**Integration:**
- Test HookEventRegistry.events returns correct count per provider
- Test HookEventRegistry.capability returns non-nil for all known events
- Test tool name mapping is bijective: translate A to B then B to A returns A
- Test event types work with JSON encoder/decoder for config persistence

**Ui:**
- N/A - no UI in this atom, deferred to H005-UIPROVIDER

**Perf:**
- Test static registry access is O(1) dictionary lookup
- Test enum initialization from rawValue is O(1)
- Test CaseIterable allCases has no runtime allocation per call

**Security:**
- Test event rawValue strings do not allow injection
- Test tool matcher patterns are validated before use
- Test Codable does not deserialize arbitrary code

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| hook_schema_lookup_count | counter | count | N/A - observational | Track how often event capabilities are looked up for optimization |
| tool_name_translation_count | counter | count | N/A - observational | Track cross-provider tool name translations to identify common patterns |

#### Telemetry Events
- `hook_schema_event_lookup: fires when HookEventRegistry.capability called, includes provider and event name`
- `hook_tool_mapping_used: fires when tool name translation performed, includes from/to providers`

#### Acceptance Tests
- Given HookProvider.claude, when I access allCases, then I get array with exactly claude, gemini, codex
- Given ClaudeHookEventType enum, when I count allCases, then count equals 12
- Given ClaudeHookEventType.preToolUse, when I check canBlock, then it returns true
- Given ClaudeHookEventType.sessionStart, when I check matcherType, then it returns SessionStartMatcher type
- Given HookToolNameMapping, when I translate Bash from claude to gemini, then I get run_shell_command
- Given CodexHookEventType, when I check canBlock for any event, then all return false

#### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] HookProvider enum has exactly 3 cases: claude, gemini, codex
- [ ] ClaudeHookEventType enum has exactly 12 cases matching Claude Code documentation
- [ ] GeminiHookEventType enum has exactly 11 cases matching Gemini CLI documentation
- [ ] CodexHookEventType enum has exactly 2 cases for notify events

- [ ] Tool name mapping covers all 6 core tools: Bash/shell, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob
- [ ] All types are Codable, Hashable, and Sendable

#### Definition of Done

- [ ] canBlock computed property returns correct value for all events per provider docs

- [ ] All types compile with Sendable conformance for actor isolation
- [ ] Unit tests verify event counts and blocking capabilities

**Requires:** Tests, Telemetry, Error Handling, Rollback Plan

#### Completion
**Completed When:** HookSchema.swift compiles with all event type enums, HookEventRegistry returns correct capabilities for all events, HookToolNameMapping translates tool names bidirectionally, and all unit tests pass verifying event counts and blocking flags.
