**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/GanttBar.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/HookTimeline/HookTimelineEvent.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/HookTimeline/HookTimelineStatus.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/GanttBar.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build
swift test --filter GanttBarTests
open Blaze.xcodeproj
```

#### Data Model Changes
- No data model changes - GanttBar is a view component that consumes existing HookTimelineEvent model

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- GanttBar.init(event: HookTimelineEvent, totalDuration: TimeInterval, availableWidth: CGFloat, isSelected: Bool, onSelect: @escaping (UUID) -> Void, onHover: @escaping (Bool) -> Void)
- GanttBar.body: some View (SwiftUI View protocol requirement)

**Event Contracts:**
- onSelect callback invoked with UUID when bar is tapped
- onHover callback invoked with Bool when hover state changes

#### UI States
- Default state: solid color bar with category color, no border, full opacity
- Hover state: same as default (hover triggers tooltip via callback, not visual change on bar itself)
- Selected state: default appearance plus 2pt accent color border stroke
- Running state: pulsing opacity animation between 0.6 and 1.0
- Failed state: red tint overlay at 30% opacity plus default appearance
- Cancelled state: reduced opacity at 50% plus strikethrough effect on label

#### UI Interactions
- Tap on bar triggers onSelect callback with event UUID for selection handling
- Mouse hover triggers onHover(true) callback on enter, onHover(false) on exit
- VoiceOver activation triggers onSelect callback same as tap

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: event.duration is nil (running event with no end time) - use 0 for calculation, resulting in minimum width bar
- Edge case 2: totalDuration is 0 (single instant event) - guard against division by zero, return minimum width
- Edge case 3: availableWidth is less than minimum 20 points - clamp to availableWidth even if below minimum
- Edge case 4: event.name is empty string - display no label text, bar remains visible
- Edge case 5: event.name exceeds bar width significantly - truncate with ellipsis, show full name in tooltip
- Edge case 6: Status changes from running to completed while animation active - cancel animation, set opacity to 1.0
- Edge case 7: Multiple rapid status changes - debounce animation state changes to prevent flicker
- Edge case 8: Very long duration event (hours) - bar fills entire available width, label may overflow

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: Animation fails to start due to SwiftUI state timing - use onAppear with slight delay (0.1s) as workaround
- FM2: Category color returns nil - provide fallback Color.gray in bar fill
- FM3: Status icon name invalid - SF Symbols returns placeholder, acceptable degraded state
- FM4: onSelect callback throws - wrap in Task to prevent view crash

### E005-F007-S001-T007-A001 — A001: HookTooltip View Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1 days

> **Epic:** E005: Enhanced Hooks & Automation
> **Feature:** F007: Hook Gantt Visualization
> **Story:** S001: Timeline Event Foundation
> **Task:** T007: Implement Hook Tooltip Component

#### Problem Statement
When users view the Gantt timeline, they can see hook execution bars with colors indicating status, but they lack detailed context about what each hook actually did. Users need to hover over a bar to see: what hook ran, how long it took, what input it received, what output it produced, which environment variables it accessed, and why it failed (if applicable). Without tooltips, users must navigate away from the Gantt view to inspect individual hook details, breaking their flow and reducing the utility of the visualization.

#### Description
Implement the HookTooltip SwiftUI view component that renders a floating popover-style tooltip when hovering over GanttBar or GanttRow elements. The tooltip displays: hook name with icon, execution status with color indicator, start time formatted as HH:mm:ss.SSS, duration in human-readable format (e.g., 142ms, 1.2s), hook type badge (command/prompt), input JSON preview (first 200 chars), output/result preview (first 200 chars), environment variables accessed, and error message with stack trace preview for failed hooks. Uses NSPopover on macOS for native tooltip behavior with smooth fade animations.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- HookTooltip SwiftUI view struct with configurable content based on HookTimelineEvent data
- Tooltip positioning logic to appear near mouse cursor without clipping screen edges
- Section-based layout: Header (name, status), Timing (start, duration), Type badge, I/O preview, Environment, Errors
- Animated fade-in/fade-out transitions (200ms ease-out)
- Keyboard accessibility: tooltip content readable by VoiceOver when bar is focused
- Truncation of long input/output with ellipsis and expand affordance
- Error section only visible when status is failed, showing error message and truncated stack trace
- Maximum tooltip width of 320pt to prevent overwhelming UI
- Dark mode support inheriting from system appearance

**Out of Scope:**
- Click-to-pin tooltip behavior (future enhancement for detailed inspection)
- Tooltip content editing or hook re-execution from tooltip
- Deep linking from tooltip to full hook detail view (covered in separate navigation atom)
- Custom tooltip themes beyond system light/dark appearance
- Tooltip for session-level or turn-level events (only tool/file/git level hooks show full tooltip)
- Internationalization of tooltip labels (English only in v1)
- Markdown rendering in input/output preview (plain text only)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: HookTooltip shall accept a HookTimelineEvent and optional HookExecution as input data sources
1. FR2: HookTooltip header section shall display hook name in bold 13pt font with status icon (checkmark/x/spinner) and colored status label (green=completed, red=failed, blue=running, gray=pending)
1. FR3: HookTooltip timing section shall display start time formatted as HH:mm:ss.SSS and duration in human-readable format (ms for <1s, s with 1 decimal for <60s, m:ss for >=60s)
1. FR4: HookTooltip type section shall display hook type badge (Command or Prompt) with appropriate icon (terminal or brain SF Symbol)
1. FR5: HookTooltip input section shall display JSON preview of hook input truncated to 200 characters with monospace font and syntax highlighting for keys
1. FR6: HookTooltip output section shall display hook output/result truncated to 200 characters, or 'No output' placeholder if empty
1. FR7: HookTooltip environment section shall list environment variables accessed by the hook (e.g., CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, HOME) if available from HookExecution metadata
1. FR8: HookTooltip error section shall only appear when status is failed, displaying error message and first 3 lines of stack trace
1. FR9: HookTooltip shall fade in over 200ms with ease-out timing when appearing
1. FR10: HookTooltip shall fade out over 150ms when dismissing
1. FR11: HookTooltip shall position itself near the mouse cursor with arrow pointing to source GanttBar
1. FR12: HookTooltip shall reposition to avoid clipping screen edges (flip arrow direction if needed)

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Tooltip shall appear within 150ms of hover event to feel responsive
- NFR2: Tooltip rendering shall not cause frame drops (maintain 60fps during animation)
- NFR3: Memory usage per tooltip instance shall not exceed 5KB excluding cached images
- NFR4: Tooltip shall support dynamic type sizes for accessibility (respecting system font size preference)
- NFR5: Tooltip content shall be readable by VoiceOver in logical order: name, status, timing, type, input, output, errors

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create new file HookTooltip.swift in Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/ directory
1. Step 2: Define HookTooltipContent struct to encapsulate all displayable data extracted from HookTimelineEvent and HookExecution
1. Step 3: Create HookTooltipContentBuilder that extracts and formats data: truncates strings, formats dates, determines visibility of sections
1. Step 4: Define HookTooltip view struct with @State for animation, @Environment for colorScheme
1. Step 5: Implement header section with HStack containing status icon (SF Symbol), name text (bold), and status label (colored)
1. Step 6: Implement timing section with VStack containing start time label and duration label with clock icon
1. Step 7: Implement type badge section using Capsule background with hook type text and icon
1. Step 8: Implement input preview section with Text view using monospace font, lineLimit(5), and truncation
1. Step 9: Implement output preview section with similar styling to input, or placeholder text if empty
1. Step 10: Implement environment section with ForEach over environment variable names in gray monospace
1. Step 11: Implement error section with conditional visibility based on status, showing error message in red and stack trace preview in monospace
1. Step 12: Wrap all sections in VStack with 12pt spacing and padding(12)
1. Step 13: Create HookTooltipPopover wrapper that manages NSPopover lifecycle and positioning
1. Step 14: Implement showTooltip(for:at:) method that creates and presents NSPopover at specified screen location
1. Step 15: Implement hideTooltip() method that closes NSPopover with fade animation
1. Step 16: Add onHover modifier integration point for GanttBar and GanttRow to trigger tooltip show/hide
1. Step 17: Implement edge detection logic to flip tooltip arrow direction when near screen boundaries
1. Step 18: Add VoiceOver accessibility labels to all sections using accessibilityLabel modifier
1. Step 19: Write unit tests for HookTooltipContentBuilder formatting logic
1. Step 20: Write UI tests verifying tooltip appears on hover and contains expected content

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/HookTooltip.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/GanttBar.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/GanttRow.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/HookTooltip.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
mkdir -p Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks
swift build
swift test --filter HookTooltipTests
xcodebuild test -scheme Blaze -destination 'platform=macOS'
```

#### Data Model Changes
- New struct HookTooltipContent with properties: name (String), statusIcon (String), statusLabel (String), statusColor (Color), startTime (String), duration (String), hookType (String), hookTypeIcon (String), inputPreview (String?), outputPreview (String?), environmentVariables ([String]), errorMessage (String?), stackTracePreview (String?)
- No changes to existing data models; HookTooltipContent is derived/computed from HookTimelineEvent and HookExecution

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- HookTooltip.init(event: HookTimelineEvent, execution: HookExecution?) - primary initializer
- HookTooltipContentBuilder.build(from event: HookTimelineEvent, execution: HookExecution?) -> HookTooltipContent - factory method
- HookTooltipPopover.shared: HookTooltipPopover - singleton accessor for tooltip manager
- HookTooltipPopover.show(content: HookTooltipContent, at: CGPoint, relativeTo: NSView) - present tooltip
- HookTooltipPopover.hide() - dismiss current tooltip

**Event Contracts:**
- TooltipShown: Emitted when tooltip becomes visible, payload: { eventId: UUID, hookName: String }
- TooltipDismissed: Emitted when tooltip is hidden, payload: { eventId: UUID, dwellTime: TimeInterval }

#### UI States
- Hidden: Default state, no tooltip visible, waiting for hover event
- Appearing: Fade-in animation in progress (200ms), tooltip content rendered but opacity animating from 0 to 1
- Visible: Fully opaque, positioned near source element, content displayed
- Disappearing: Fade-out animation in progress (150ms), opacity animating from 1 to 0, then transitions to Hidden

#### UI Interactions
- Hover over GanttBar: After 100ms dwell time, trigger TooltipShown event and transition to Appearing state
- Mouse leave GanttBar: Immediately trigger TooltipDismissed event and transition to Disappearing state
- Scroll Gantt view while tooltip visible: Reposition tooltip to track source element, or dismiss if element scrolls out of view
- Focus GanttBar via keyboard: Show tooltip and announce content via VoiceOver
- Press Escape while tooltip visible: Dismiss tooltip immediately

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: HookExecution is nil (only HookTimelineEvent available) - show basic info (name, status, timing) without I/O preview sections
- Edge case 2: Input JSON is empty string or null - show 'No input data' placeholder
- Edge case 3: Output JSON exceeds 200 characters - truncate and append ' [truncated]' suffix
- Edge case 4: Hook is still running (no endTime) - show 'Running' status with spinner icon, duration shows elapsed time
- Edge case 5: Error message exceeds 500 characters - truncate error message at 500 chars with ellipsis
- Edge case 6: Stack trace has more than 3 lines - show first 3 lines with '+ N more lines' suffix
- Edge case 7: Mouse moves rapidly between multiple GanttBars - dismiss previous tooltip immediately before showing new one (no overlap)
- Edge case 8: GanttBar near right edge of screen - flip tooltip to appear on left side with arrow pointing right
- Edge case 9: GanttBar near bottom edge of screen - flip tooltip to appear above with arrow pointing down
- Edge case 10: System in dark mode - tooltip background uses dark popover appearance, text uses light colors
- Edge case 11: Environment variables array is empty - hide environment section entirely rather than showing empty list
- Edge case 12: Hook type is unknown/future type - display type as-is without icon, fallback to generic tag icon

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: NSPopover fails to create (rare AppKit issue) - log error and silently fail, user sees no tooltip but app continues functioning
- FM2: HookExecution data is corrupted or has invalid JSON - catch decoding error, show tooltip with available data and 'Data unavailable' in I/O sections
- FM3: Mouse position tracking fails - use fallback position centered on GanttBar bounds rather than mouse cursor
- FM4: Animation frame drops due to heavy concurrent processing - skip animation and show tooltip immediately at full opacity
- FM5: VoiceOver not running but accessibility labels still computed - no impact, labels ignored when VoiceOver inactive
- FM6: Tooltip content builder throws unexpected error - wrap in do-catch, return minimal tooltip with name and status only

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/HookTooltip.swift. Remove onHover modifier calls from GanttBar.swift and GanttRow.swift that reference HookTooltipPopover. Gantt visualization continues to work without tooltips - users see bars but no hover details. No data migration required. No other features affected.

#### Test Plan
**Unit:**
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder formats startTime correctly as HH:mm:ss.SSS
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder formats duration <1s as milliseconds (e.g., '142ms')
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder formats duration 1-60s as seconds with decimal (e.g., '1.2s')
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder formats duration >=60s as m:ss (e.g., '2:15')
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder truncates input at 200 characters
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder truncates output at 200 characters
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder returns nil inputPreview for empty input
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder returns 'No output' for nil output
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder extracts correct status icon for each HookTimelineStatus
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder extracts correct status color for each status
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder includes error section only for failed status
- Test HookTooltipContentBuilder truncates stack trace to 3 lines

**Integration:**
- Test HookTooltip renders correctly with full HookExecution data
- Test HookTooltip renders correctly with nil HookExecution (minimal data)
- Test HookTooltipPopover.show positions tooltip near provided CGPoint
- Test HookTooltipPopover.hide dismisses currently visible tooltip
- Test tooltip repositions when GanttBar position changes (scroll integration)

**Ui:**
- Test tooltip appears within 200ms of hover on GanttBar in UI test
- Test tooltip dismisses when mouse leaves GanttBar
- Test tooltip displays correct hook name matching source GanttBar
- Test tooltip displays correct duration matching HookTimelineEvent
- Test tooltip error section visible only for failed hooks
- Test tooltip keyboard accessibility: focus bar with Tab, tooltip content announced by VoiceOver simulator

**Perf:**
- Test tooltip show/hide cycle completes within 300ms total (appear + dismiss)
- Test rendering 100 tooltips sequentially does not cause memory growth (proper cleanup)
- Test tooltip animation maintains 60fps (no frame drops during fade)

**Security:**
- Test tooltip does not expose sensitive environment variable values (only names shown)
- Test input preview does not render potentially malicious HTML/script content (plain text only)

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| tooltip_dwell_time_ms | histogram | milliseconds | Track how long users view tooltips to understand engagement | Buckets: 0-500ms, 500-1000ms, 1-3s, 3-10s, >10s |
| tooltip_show_latency_ms | timer | milliseconds | Should be <150ms for responsive feel, alert if p95 >200ms | Measures time from hover event to tooltip visible |
| tooltip_error_section_views | counter | count | Track how often users hover over failed hooks | High count may indicate frequent hook failures needing attention |

#### Telemetry Events
- `hook_tooltip_shown: Fired when tooltip becomes visible, properties: { hook_name: string, hook_type: string, event_id: string }`

### E005-F008-S001-T001-A001 — A001: CodexAppServerAdapter Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 2 days

> **Epic:** E005: Enhanced Hooks & Automation
> **Feature:** F008: Codex App-Server Integration
> **Story:** S001: App-Server Communication Foundation
> **Task:** T001: Implement App-Server Adapter

#### Problem Statement
Codex CLI can run in app-server mode which provides a persistent daemon process with JSON-RPC interface. This offers advantages over direct CLI spawning: persistent sessions, better event streaming, and reduced process overhead. However, Blaze currently has no adapter to communicate with this mode. We need a robust JSON-RPC client adapter that can connect to the app-server, send requests, receive responses, and handle the bidirectional notification stream for real-time updates.

#### Description
Implement CodexAppServerAdapter actor conforming to EngineAdapter protocol with JSON-RPC 2.0 client capabilities over HTTP transport, including request ID generation, response correlation, notification stream handling, and comprehensive error types for connection failures, timeouts, and protocol errors.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- CodexAppServerAdapter actor definition conforming to EngineAdapter protocol
- JSON-RPC 2.0 request message structure (id, method, params)
- JSON-RPC 2.0 response message structure (id, result, error)
- JSON-RPC 2.0 notification message structure (method, params, no id)
- HTTP transport layer using URLSession for request/response
- Server-Sent Events (SSE) transport for notification stream
- Request ID generation using atomic counter or UUID
- Response correlation mapping pending requests to completions
- Connection state management (disconnected, connecting, connected, error)
- Error types for connection refused, timeout, invalid response, RPC error
- Async/await API surface for all RPC calls
- AsyncSequence for notification events

**Out of Scope:**
- App-server process lifecycle management (covered in X002-MANAGER)
- Event stream parsing and normalization (covered in X003-EVENTS)
- Session persistence and state management (covered in X004-SESSION)
- Port discovery and configuration (covered in X005-CONFIG)
- Authentication and authorization mechanisms
- WebSocket transport (app-server uses HTTP + SSE)
- Reconnection logic with backoff (managed by lifecycle manager)
- Request batching or pipelining

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: CodexAppServerAdapter shall conform to EngineAdapter protocol with async methods for submit, cancel, and event stream
1. FR2: Adapter shall implement JSON-RPC 2.0 request format with id (String), jsonrpc (literal 2.0), method (String), params (Encodable?)
1. FR3: Adapter shall parse JSON-RPC 2.0 response format with id, result (Decodable), or error (code, message, data)
1. FR4: Adapter shall maintain a dictionary mapping request IDs to CheckedContinuation for response correlation
1. FR5: Adapter shall generate unique request IDs using UUID().uuidString for each outgoing request
1. FR6: Adapter shall provide connect() async throws method to establish HTTP connection and verify server availability
1. FR7: Adapter shall provide disconnect() method to close connections and cancel pending requests
1. FR8: Adapter shall expose connectionState: ConnectionState published property for UI binding
1. FR9: Adapter shall provide call<T: Decodable>(method: String, params: Encodable?) async throws -> T for generic RPC calls
1. FR10: Adapter shall provide notifications: AsyncStream<JSONRPCNotification> property for incoming notifications
1. FR11: Adapter shall timeout requests after configurable duration (default 30 seconds) with TimeoutError
1. FR12: Adapter shall propagate JSON-RPC error responses as CodexRPCError with code, message, and optional data

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Request round-trip latency shall be under 100ms for local requests (excluding server processing)
- NFR2: Adapter shall support at least 10 concurrent pending requests without degradation
- NFR3: Memory footprint of adapter instance shall not exceed 1MB excluding response buffers
- NFR4: Notification stream shall deliver events within 50ms of server emission
- NFR5: Connection establishment shall complete within 5 seconds or fail with timeout
- NFR6: Adapter shall gracefully handle server disconnect without crashing

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create new file CodexAppServerAdapter.swift in Blaze/Sources/Engine/ directory
1. Step 2: Define ConnectionState enum with cases: disconnected, connecting, connected, error(Error)
1. Step 3: Define JSONRPCRequest struct with id (String), jsonrpc (String = 2.0), method (String), params (AnyCodable?)
1. Step 4: Define JSONRPCResponse<T: Decodable> struct with id (String), result (T?), error (JSONRPCError?)
1. Step 5: Define JSONRPCError struct with code (Int), message (String), data (AnyCodable?)
1. Step 6: Define JSONRPCNotification struct with method (String), params (AnyCodable?)
1. Step 7: Define CodexRPCError enum with cases: connectionFailed(Error), timeout, invalidResponse(String), rpcError(JSONRPCError), serverDisconnected
1. Step 8: Declare CodexAppServerAdapter actor with @Published connectionState property
1. Step 9: Add stored properties: baseURL (URL), session (URLSession), pendingRequests ([String: CheckedContinuation<Data, Error>]), notificationContinuation (AsyncStream<JSONRPCNotification>.Continuation?)
1. Step 10: Implement init(host: String, port: Int) initializer with URL construction and URLSession configuration
1. Step 11: Implement connect() async throws that performs health check request to /health endpoint
1. Step 12: Implement disconnect() that cancels all pending requests and closes notification stream
1. Step 13: Implement private sendRequest<P: Encodable, R: Decodable>(method: String, params: P?) async throws -> R
1. Step 14: Implement request timeout using withTimeout or Task.sleep + cancellation check
1. Step 15: Implement startNotificationStream() that opens SSE connection to /events endpoint
1. Step 16: Implement private parseSSELine(_ line: String) -> JSONRPCNotification? for SSE parsing
1. Step 17: Implement call<T: Decodable>(method: String, params: Encodable?) async throws -> T public API
1. Step 18: Implement EngineAdapter protocol methods delegating to call() with appropriate method names
1. Step 19: Add comprehensive documentation comments for all public types and methods
1. Step 20: Write unit tests with mock URLProtocol for HTTP responses

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerAdapter.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Engine/EngineAdapter.swift`

#### Data Model Changes

- New enum ConnectionState with cases: disconnected, connecting, connected, error(Error)
- New struct JSONRPCRequest with properties: id (String), jsonrpc (String), method (String), params (AnyCodable?)
- New struct JSONRPCResponse<T> with properties: id (String), result (T?), error (JSONRPCError?)
- New struct JSONRPCError with properties: code (Int), message (String), data (AnyCodable?)
- New struct JSONRPCNotification with properties: method (String), params (AnyCodable?)
- New enum CodexRPCError with cases: connectionFailed, timeout, invalidResponse, rpcError, serverDisconnected

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CodexAppServerAdapter.init(host: String, port: Int) - creates adapter configured to connect to app-server at host:port
- CodexAppServerAdapter.connect() async throws - establishes connection and verifies server health
- CodexAppServerAdapter.disconnect() - closes all connections and cancels pending requests
- CodexAppServerAdapter.call<T: Decodable>(method: String, params: Encodable?) async throws -> T - sends RPC request and awaits response
- CodexAppServerAdapter.connectionState: ConnectionState - current connection state for UI binding
- CodexAppServerAdapter.notifications: AsyncStream<JSONRPCNotification> - stream of server notifications
- EngineAdapter.submit(prompt: String, context: SessionContext) async throws -> AsyncStream<NormalizedEvent>
- EngineAdapter.cancel() async - cancels current operation

**Event Contracts:**
- JSONRPCNotification emitted when server pushes notification via SSE stream
- ConnectionStateChanged event when connectionState property changes (via @Published)
- Each notification contains method (String) and params (AnyCodable?) matching server notification format

#### UI Interactions

- User taps Disconnect button triggering disconnect() call and state transition to disconnected
- Automatic retry prompt shown when connection fails with Retry button
- Error alert displayed when RPC call fails with error message and dismiss button

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: Server not running when connect() called - throws connectionFailed with ECONNREFUSED underlying error
- Edge case 2: Server crashes mid-request - pending continuation resumed with serverDisconnected error
- Edge case 3: Response received for unknown request ID - logged as warning, response discarded
- Edge case 4: Malformed JSON in response body - throws invalidResponse with parsing error details
- Edge case 5: Server returns JSON-RPC error response - throws rpcError with code and message
- Edge case 6: Request cancelled by Task cancellation - continuation cancelled, request removed from pending
- Edge case 7: Multiple rapid connect() calls - only first proceeds, subsequent await first completion
- Edge case 8: SSE stream interrupted - notification continuation finishes, triggers reconnect via manager
- Edge case 9: Very large response body (over 10MB) - handled by URLSession memory limits, may fail
- Edge case 10: Server returns success response with null result - decoded as nil, valid for void methods

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: ECONNREFUSED on connect - display Connection refused error with suggestion to start app-server
- FM2: Request timeout after 30 seconds - display timeout error, allow retry
- FM3: JSON decode failure - display Invalid response from server with raw response in logs
- FM4: RPC error code -32600 (Invalid Request) - display Server rejected request, check parameters
- FM5: RPC error code -32601 (Method not found) - display Method not supported by app-server version
- FM6: RPC error code -32603 (Internal error) - display Server internal error, check server logs
- FM7: SSL/TLS error (if HTTPS attempted) - should not occur on localhost, fallback to HTTP
- FM8: Memory pressure during large response - URLSession handles, may receive didReceiveMemoryWarning

### E005-F008-S001-T004-A001 — A001: CodexAppServerSession Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 2.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Remote Extension Registry
> **Feature:** F008: Codex App-Server Integration
> **Story:** S001: App-Server Communication Foundation
> **Task:** T004: Implement App-Server Session Persistence

#### Problem Statement
When Blaze uses Codex in app-server mode, session state lives in two places: the long-running app-server daemon process and the Blaze harness. Unlike headless CLI mode where each invocation is stateless, app-server maintains conversation context across multiple requests. This creates synchronization challenges: what happens if Blaze crashes and restarts? What if the app-server crashes? What if both restart? We need a session persistence layer that keeps Blaze state synchronized with app-server state, enables crash recovery, and provides a unified view of session history regardless of where the authoritative state lives.

#### Description
Implement CodexAppServerSession actor in Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerSession.swift providing session state management for persistent Codex app-server mode. The actor handles session ID generation and tracking, conversation history buffering with token counting, context window management with sliding window and summarization triggers, checkpoint creation to SQLite for crash recovery, state reconciliation between Blaze and app-server on reconnect, session metadata storage (creation time, last activity, token usage), and integration with SessionStore for unified session view across all engine types.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- CodexAppServerSession actor conforming to EngineSession protocol for engine-agnostic session handling
- Session ID generation using UUID for new sessions and retrieval of existing IDs from app-server
- Conversation history buffer storing last N messages with role, content, and timestamp
- Token counting for context window management using tiktoken-compatible algorithm
- Context window sliding with configurable max tokens and summarization trigger threshold
- Checkpoint creation on configurable intervals and before risky operations
- Checkpoint storage in SQLite via SessionStore with session_id, checkpoint_data, created_at columns
- Crash recovery loading latest checkpoint on session resume and reconciling with app-server state
- State reconciliation protocol comparing Blaze checkpoint with app-server reported history
- Session metadata tracking: session_id, created_at, last_activity_at, total_tokens_used, message_count
- Integration with SessionStore for CRUD operations on session records
- Delegate protocol for session state change notifications to UI layer
- Serialization of session state to JSON for checkpoint data
- Deserialization and validation of checkpoint data on recovery
- Handling of app-server session ID mismatch (app-server restarted with different session)
- Graceful handling of checkpoint corruption with fallback to fresh session

**Out of Scope:**
- JSON-RPC communication with app-server (handled by X001-ADAPTER)
- App-server process lifecycle (handled by X002-MANAGER)
- Event stream parsing (handled by X003-EVENTS)
- Configuration of ports and auth (handled by X005-CONFIG)
- Actual LLM inference or token generation (done by Codex app-server)
- Session UI display (handled by SessionListView and related UI atoms)
- Multi-session management across different projects (handled by SessionStore)
- Session export or sharing functionality (future feature)
- End-to-end encryption of session data at rest (security enhancement)
- Cloud sync of session state (future feature)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-01: CodexAppServerSession.init(sessionId:adapter:store:) creates session with given ID or generates new UUID if nil
1. FR-02: session.appendMessage(role:content:) adds message to history buffer and triggers checkpoint if threshold reached
1. FR-03: session.getHistory() returns ordered list of messages with role, content, and timestamp
1. FR-04: session.getHistoryForContext(maxTokens:) returns messages fitting within token budget with oldest trimmed first
1. FR-05: session.createCheckpoint() serializes current state to JSON and stores via SessionStore
1. FR-06: session.loadCheckpoint(sessionId:) deserializes checkpoint data and initializes session state
1. FR-07: session.reconcileWithServer() queries app-server for current state and resolves discrepancies
1. FR-08: session.getMetadata() returns SessionMetadata struct with id, created, lastActivity, tokens, messageCount
1. FR-09: session.updateLastActivity() refreshes last_activity_at timestamp and persists metadata
1. FR-10: session.estimateTokens(text:) returns approximate token count using fast estimation algorithm
1. FR-11: session.getTotalTokensUsed() returns cumulative tokens across all messages in session
1. FR-12: session.clear() removes all messages and resets state while preserving session ID
1. FR-13: session.close() creates final checkpoint and releases any held resources
1. FR-14: Session automatically creates checkpoint when message count crosses checkpoint interval threshold
1. FR-15: Session logs warning when token usage approaches context limit and triggers summarization delegate callback

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-01: Checkpoint creation latency must be under 500ms for sessions with 1000 messages
- NFR-02: Token estimation must complete under 10ms for 10K character strings
- NFR-03: Session recovery from checkpoint must complete under 2 seconds
- NFR-04: Memory footprint of session state must not exceed 50MB for 10K message history
- NFR-05: Session must handle 100 concurrent appendMessage calls without deadlock or data loss
- NFR-06: Checkpoint data must be recoverable if app terminated mid-write (atomic write)

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 01: Create Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerSession.swift with file header and imports (Foundation, OSLog)

1. Step 07: Define CodexAppServerSessionError enum with cases: checkpointCorrupted, checkpointNotFound, reconciliationFailed, tokenLimitExceeded, serializationFailed

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 01: Session created but no messages added - checkpoint contains empty history array but valid metadata
- Edge case 02: Checkpoint file corrupted or truncated - log error, notify delegate, start fresh session with warning
- Edge case 03: App-server session ID differs from checkpoint - server restarted, log warning, continue with Blaze history as source of truth
- Edge case 04: App-server has more messages than Blaze - messages sent via direct CLI, attempt to fetch and merge
- Edge case 05: Blaze has more messages than app-server - messages lost in server restart, Blaze history is authoritative
- Edge case 06: Extremely long message exceeding token estimate buffer - clamp to reasonable estimate, log warning
- Edge case 07: Checkpoint version newer than code supports - reject with clear error, suggest app update
- Edge case 08: Checkpoint version older than current - run migration chain to update format
- Edge case 09: Concurrent checkpoint writes from rapid message appends - serialize writes via actor isolation
- Edge case 10: SessionStore database locked by another process - retry with backoff, fail after 5 attempts
- Edge case 11: Disk full during checkpoint write - catch error, notify user, continue without checkpoint
- Edge case 12: Session metadata dates in future due to clock skew - normalize to current time if future
- Edge case 13: Token count estimation overflow for huge messages - use Int64 internally, cap display values
- Edge case 14: Zero-length message content - allow but skip token counting, log debug message
- Edge case 15: Unicode normalization affecting token count - use NFC normalized form for consistency

#### Failure Modes
- FM-01: Checkpoint write failure due to disk error - continue session in memory, retry checkpoint on next interval, warn user of unsaved state
- FM-02: Checkpoint read failure on recovery - start fresh session, log detailed error, offer to view corrupted data
- FM-03: Reconciliation timeout (app-server unresponsive) - continue with local state, retry reconciliation on next message
- FM-04: Token estimation wildly inaccurate - may hit actual limit unexpectedly, rely on server error response as fallback
- FM-05: Database schema mismatch after update - migration should handle, but fail clearly if migration missing
- FM-06: Memory pressure during large session load - session actor is lazy loaded, checkpoint data streamed if needed
- FM-07: Delegate callback throws - catch and log, do not propagate to session actor to prevent state corruption
- FM-08: Actor reentrancy during checkpoint - prevented by actor isolation, but test explicitly for this case

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerSession.swift and Tests/Engine/CodexAppServerSessionTests.swift. Remove SessionStore.saveCheckpoint and loadCheckpoint methods. Drop checkpoints table via migration v9 with DROP TABLE IF EXISTS checkpoints. Remove imports and references from adapter and manager files. User session data in checkpoints table is lost but can be manually exported before rollback if needed. Core session functionality via SessionStore sessions table is unaffected.

### E005-F008-S001-T005-A001 — A001: CodexAppServerConfig Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1 days

> **Epic:** E005: Enhanced Hooks & Automation
> **Feature:** F008: Codex App-Server Integration
> **Story:** S001: App-Server Communication Foundation
> **Task:** T005: Implement App-Server Configuration

#### Problem Statement
The Codex app-server daemon requires multiple configuration parameters to launch correctly: port number, authentication tokens, environment variables, timeout values, and startup flags. Without centralized configuration management, these settings would be scattered across the codebase, making it difficult to maintain consistency, validate inputs, persist user preferences, and provide a unified settings UI. A dedicated configuration struct ensures type safety, validation, persistence, and clean API boundaries between the manager, adapter, and UI layers.

#### Description
Implement CodexAppServerConfig struct in Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerConfig.swift providing strongly-typed configuration for the Codex app-server daemon including port range allocation, authentication token retrieval, startup command arguments, timeout values for connection and health checks, environment variable injection, TLS settings for secure connections, and persistence via UserDefaults with Codable serialization. Configuration validates port ranges, provides sensible defaults, and exposes SwiftUI-bindable properties for the settings UI.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- CodexAppServerConfig struct with Codable and Sendable conformance
- Port configuration with range validation (1024-65535) and default port (9100)
- Port range specification for automatic port allocation fallback (default 9100-9199)
- Authentication mode enum: none, apiKey, oauth with associated configuration
- API key retrieval from macOS Keychain via Security framework
- Startup arguments array for additional codex app-server command flags
- Connection timeout configuration with default 30 seconds and range validation (1-300s)
- Health check interval configuration with default 5 seconds and range validation (1-60s)
- Health check timeout configuration with default 2 seconds and range validation (1-30s)
- Startup timeout configuration with default 30 seconds and range validation (5-120s)
- Shutdown grace period configuration with default 5 seconds and range validation (1-30s)
- Maximum restart attempts configuration with default 3 and range validation (0-10)
- Restart backoff base configuration with default 1 second and range validation (0.5-10s)
- Environment variables dictionary for process injection
- TLS enabled flag with default false for localhost connections
- TLS certificate path configuration for custom certificates
- Log level configuration enum: debug, info, warning, error with default info
- Auto-start on app launch boolean with default false
- Host configuration with default localhost and validation
- JSON output mode flag with default true
- UserDefaults persistence with suite name for app group sharing
- ConfigurationError enum for validation failures
- Factory method for default configuration
- Factory method for loading from UserDefaults
- Save method for persisting to UserDefaults
- Validation method returning array of ConfigurationError
- Reset to defaults method
- SwiftUI Binding helpers for settings UI integration
- Equatable and Hashable conformance for change detection
- Documentation comments for all public members

**Out of Scope:**
- Actual Keychain read/write implementation details (uses KeychainService abstraction)
- Process spawning logic (handled by X002-MANAGER)
- JSON-RPC communication (handled by X001-ADAPTER)
- Event parsing (handled by X003-EVENTS)
- Session state management (handled by X004-SESSION)
- Settings UI views (handled by separate settings view atoms)
- OAuth flow implementation (placeholder for future work)
- Remote configuration sync (local only for MVP)
- Configuration migration between versions (handle in future atom)
- Configuration encryption at rest (UserDefaults is sufficient for non-sensitive data)
- Multi-profile configuration (single profile for MVP)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-01: CodexAppServerConfig shall define port property with Int type, default 9100, validated in range 1024-65535
1. FR-02: Config shall define portRangeStart and portRangeEnd for fallback port allocation, defaults 9100-9199
1. FR-03: Config shall define authMode enum with cases none, apiKey, oauth and associated metadata

1. FR-07: Config shall define healthCheckTimeoutSeconds with Double type, default 2, range 1-30
1. FR-08: Config shall define startupTimeoutSeconds with Double type, default 30, range 5-120
1. FR-09: Config shall define shutdownGracePeriodSeconds with Double type, default 5, range 1-30

#### Data Model Changes
- New enum AuthenticationMode with cases: none, apiKey(service: String, account: String), oauth(clientId: String, scopes: [String])
- New enum LogLevel with cases: debug, info, warning, error
- New enum ConfigurationError with cases: invalidPort(Int), invalidPortRange(start: Int, end: Int), invalidTimeout(field: String, value: Double, min: Double, max: Double), emptyHost, invalidHostname(String), tlsCertificateNotFound(String), restrictedEnvironmentVariable(String)
- New struct CodexAppServerConfig with properties: port (Int), portRangeStart (Int), portRangeEnd (Int), authMode (AuthenticationMode), connectionTimeoutSeconds (Double), healthCheckIntervalSeconds (Double), healthCheckTimeoutSeconds (Double), startupTimeoutSeconds (Double), shutdownGracePeriodSeconds (Double), maxRestartAttempts (Int), restartBackoffBaseSeconds (Double), environmentVariables ([String: String]), tlsEnabled (Bool), tlsCertificatePath (String?), logLevel (LogLevel), autoStartOnLaunch (Bool), host (String), jsonOutputMode (Bool)

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CodexAppServerConfig.init(port:portRangeStart:portRangeEnd:authMode:connectionTimeoutSeconds:healthCheckIntervalSeconds:healthCheckTimeoutSeconds:startupTimeoutSeconds:shutdownGracePeriodSeconds:maxRestartAttempts:restartBackoffBaseSeconds:environmentVariables:tlsEnabled:tlsCertificatePath:logLevel:autoStartOnLaunch:host:jsonOutputMode:) - memberwise initializer with defaults
- CodexAppServerConfig.validate() -> [ConfigurationError] - returns array of all validation errors, empty if valid
- CodexAppServerConfig.save(to: UserDefaults) throws - persists configuration to UserDefaults
- CodexAppServerConfig.load(from: UserDefaults) -> CodexAppServerConfig? - loads configuration or nil if not found
- CodexAppServerConfig.makeDefault() -> CodexAppServerConfig - factory for default configuration
- CodexAppServerConfig.apiKeyFromKeychain() throws -> String? - retrieves API key from Keychain
- CodexAppServerConfig.commandLineArguments: [String] - computed CLI arguments for process spawn
- CodexAppServerConfig.baseURL: URL - computed base URL for HTTP requests
- CodexAppServerConfig.healthEndpointURL: URL - computed URL for health check endpoint
- CodexAppServerConfig.with(port: Int) -> CodexAppServerConfig - copy with modified port
- CodexAppServerConfig.with(host: String) -> CodexAppServerConfig - copy with modified host

**Event Contracts:**
- Configuration changes do not emit events directly - consumers observe via SwiftUI bindings or explicit comparison
- Settings UI publishes ConfigurationDidChange notification when user saves changes
- Manager listens for configuration changes and restarts app-server if running

#### UI States
- N/A - configuration struct has no direct UI; UI states handled by settings view atoms

#### UI Interactions
- N/A - configuration struct has no direct UI; UI interactions handled by settings view atoms

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 01: Port 0 specified - validate() returns invalidPort(0) since 0 means any available port which conflicts with explicit configuration
- Edge case 02: Port 80 specified (privileged) - validate() returns invalidPort(80) since ports below 1024 require root
- Edge case 03: portRangeStart greater than portRangeEnd - validate() returns invalidPortRange with swapped values
- Edge case 04: portRangeStart equals portRangeEnd - valid, means single port with no fallback
- Edge case 05: Empty host string - validate() returns emptyHost error
- Edge case 06: Host with invalid characters (spaces, special chars) - validate() returns invalidHostname with offending host
- Edge case 07: Host as IP address (127.0.0.1) - valid, hostname regex allows IP format
- Edge case 08: tlsEnabled true but tlsCertificatePath nil - valid, uses system default certificates
- Edge case 09: tlsEnabled true with nonexistent certificate path - validate() returns tlsCertificateNotFound
- Edge case 10: Environment variable with key PATH - validate() returns restrictedEnvironmentVariable(PATH)
- Edge case 11: Environment variable with key HOME - validate() returns restrictedEnvironmentVariable(HOME)
- Edge case 12: Environment variable with key DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH - validate() returns restrictedEnvironmentVariable to prevent injection
- Edge case 13: Negative timeout value - validate() returns invalidTimeout with negative value
- Edge case 14: Zero timeout value - validate() returns invalidTimeout since zero means no timeout which is dangerous
- Edge case 15: Extremely large timeout (over max) - validate() returns invalidTimeout with clamping suggestion
- Edge case 16: maxRestartAttempts of 0 - valid, means no auto-restart
- Edge case 17: UserDefaults contains malformed data - load() returns nil, caller uses defaults
- Edge case 18: Keychain access denied by user - apiKeyFromKeychain() throws KeychainError.accessDenied
- Edge case 19: Keychain item not found - apiKeyFromKeychain() returns nil (not an error)
- Edge case 20: Configuration saved with old schema version - load() handles via Codable migration or returns nil

#### Failure Modes
- FM-01: Validation errors on save - UI displays all errors, save blocked until resolved
- FM-02: UserDefaults write failure - throws error with underlying NSError, UI shows retry option
- FM-03: UserDefaults read failure (corruption) - returns nil, caller uses defaults with warning log
- FM-04: Keychain access timeout - throws timeout error, UI shows manual API key entry option
- FM-05: Keychain access denied - throws access denied error, UI shows system preferences link
- FM-06: TLS certificate file not readable - throws file permission error, UI shows path picker

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerConfig.swift and remove any imports from other files. UserDefaults data under key codex.appserver.config can be removed via defaults delete com.blaze.app codex.appserver.config command. No other persistent state affected.

### E005-F009-S001-T002-A001 — A001: HookMatchers Implementation

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Enhanced Hooks & Automation
> **Feature:** F009: Hook Infrastructure Building Blocks
> **Story:** S001: Core Hook Data Types and Matching
> **Task:** T002: Implement Pattern Matching System

#### Problem Statement
Hooks need a flexible pattern matching system to determine when they should fire. A hook targeting Write operations should not fire for Read operations. A hook for session startup should not fire on resume. Currently there is no pattern matching infrastructure. We need a comprehensive matcher system that supports exact tool name matching, pipe-delimited multiple tool matching, wildcard matching for all tools, and regex matching for complex patterns like MCP tool namespaces. Additionally, event-specific matchers for SessionStart and PreCompact events require dedicated enum types with semantic meaning.

#### Description
Implement complete pattern matching infrastructure in HookMatchers.swift including HookMatcher struct with automatic type detection, MatcherType enum with four matching strategies (exact, multiple, wildcard, regex), SessionStartMatcher enum for session lifecycle events, PreCompactMatcher enum for compaction triggers, and MatcherSuggestions helper providing context-aware pattern recommendations.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- HookMatcher struct with pattern string and detected MatcherType
- MatcherType enum with exact, multiple, wildcard, and regex cases
- MatcherType.detect(from:) static method for automatic pattern type detection
- HookMatcher.matches(_:) method to test if a tool name matches the pattern
- SessionStartMatcher enum with startup, resume, clear, and compact cases
- PreCompactMatcher enum with manual and auto cases
- MatcherSuggestions struct with static toolPatterns array
- MatcherSuggestions.suggestions(for:) method returning context-aware patterns
- Codable conformance for all types for JSON serialization
- Sendable conformance for all types for Swift Concurrency safety
- Hashable conformance for HookMatcher for use in Sets and Dictionary keys
- DisplayName and icon properties on MatcherType for UI presentation

**Out of Scope:**
- Hook execution logic (covered in separate hook runner atoms)
- Hook configuration UI (covered in HooksBuilder atoms)
- Hook persistence to settings.json (covered in HookStorage atoms)
- Complex multi-condition matching (AND/OR logic between matchers)
- Matcher performance optimization or caching
- Regular expression validation or syntax highlighting
- Custom matcher types beyond the four defined patterns
- Localization of matcher descriptions or UI copy

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: HookMatcher shall store pattern as String property accessible for UI display
1. FR2: HookMatcher shall store type as MatcherType property computed on initialization
1. FR3: HookMatcher.init(pattern:) shall call MatcherType.detect(from:) to set type automatically
1. FR4: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true for exact match when type is .exact and pattern equals input
1. FR5: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true for multiple match when type is .multiple and any pipe-delimited option equals input
1. FR6: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true unconditionally when type is .wildcard
1. FR7: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true when type is .regex and pattern matches input via NSRegularExpression
1. FR8: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return false for .regex when pattern is invalid rather than throwing
1. FR9: MatcherType.detect(from:) shall return .wildcard for pattern exactly equal to asterisk
1. FR10: MatcherType.detect(from:) shall return .multiple for pattern containing pipe character
1. FR11: MatcherType.detect(from:) shall return .regex for pattern containing .*, [, or backslash characters

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: Empty pattern string passed to HookMatcher.init - detected as exact, matches only empty string (unusual but valid)
- Edge case 2: Pattern with only pipe character | - detected as multiple, splits to empty strings, matches empty tool name
- Edge case 3: Pattern asterisk in middle like Read*Write - detected as regex due to *, not wildcard
- Edge case 4: Invalid regex pattern like [unclosed - matches() returns false, does not throw
- Edge case 5: Pattern with escaped pipe like Read\|Write - detected as regex due to backslash, matches literal Read|Write
- Edge case 6: Tool name with special regex characters like mcp__fs__read - matched correctly by exact pattern
- Edge case 7: Extremely long pattern (1000+ characters) - may cause regex compilation slowdown, but functions correctly
- Edge case 8: Unicode characters in pattern or tool name - handled by NSRegularExpression, matches correctly
- Edge case 9: Case sensitivity - matching is case-sensitive, Write does not match write
- Edge case 10: Pattern with newlines or whitespace - preserved in pattern, matched literally

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: Regex pattern causes catastrophic backtracking - mitigated by NSRegularExpression timeout; matches() may return false after timeout
- FM2: Pattern contains characters invalid for JSON encoding - Codable encoding fails; caller must validate input
- FM3: MatcherType.detect misclassifies pattern with accidental regex chars - user gets unexpected matches; document detection rules
- FM4: SessionStartMatcher raw value changes between versions - JSON deserialization fails for saved configs; maintain backward compatibility

### E005-F009-S001-T006-A001 — A001: HookTestRunner Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1 days

> **Epic:** E005: Session Creation UX + Onboarding + Multi-CLI
> **Feature:** F009: Advanced Hooks Builder
> **Story:** S001: Hook Builder Core Components
> **Task:** T006: Implement Hook Test Runner

#### Problem Statement
Hook developers need a way to test their hooks before deploying them to production. Currently, testing requires manually crafting JSON input, running scripts in terminal, and parsing output by hand. This is error-prone and slow. A built-in test runner that accepts structured input, executes hooks in isolation, captures all output streams, parses results as HookOutput, and provides clear pass/fail feedback will dramatically improve the hook development experience and reduce broken hook deployments.

#### Description
Implement HookTestRunner actor with testCommandHook method that spawns hook scripts with JSON-encoded HookInput via stdin, captures stdout/stderr, handles timeouts, parses output as HookOutput, and returns TestResult struct containing success status, raw output, exit code, execution duration, parsed output, and error collection. Also implement generateTestCommand helper for CLI debugging.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- HookTestRunner actor definition with actor isolation for thread-safe test execution
- TestResult struct with success (Bool), output (String), exitCode (Int), duration (TimeInterval), parsedOutput (HookOutput?), and errors ([String])
- testCommandHook method accepting command (String), input (HookInput), and timeout (TimeInterval) parameters
- Inline script handling by writing command to temporary file with executable permissions
- External script path resolution with $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT variable substitution
- JSON encoding of HookInput for stdin pipe to hook script
- Process spawning via /bin/bash -c with stdin pipe and stdout/stderr capture
- Timeout handling using DispatchSemaphore with configurable duration defaulting to 60 seconds
- HookOutput JSON parsing from stdout with graceful fallback on parse failure
- Error collection including stderr content and JSON parse failures
- generateTestCommand method returning copy-pasteable shell command for manual debugging
- Cleanup of temporary script files in defer block

**Out of Scope:**
- Prompt hook testing (uses LLM, different execution model, covered in separate atom)
- Agent hook testing (requires agent lifecycle, covered in separate atom)
- UI for test runner (covered in B012-BUILDERPANEL atom)
- Persistent test history or test case management
- Mock filesystem or sandboxed execution environment
- Parallel test execution or test batching
- Code coverage or performance profiling of hooks
- Network isolation during test execution

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: HookTestRunner shall be declared as a public actor to ensure thread-safe test execution
1. FR2: TestResult shall be a Sendable struct containing success (Bool), output (String), exitCode (Int), duration (TimeInterval), parsedOutput (HookOutput?), and errors ([String])
1. FR3: testCommandHook shall accept command (String), input (HookInput), and optional timeout (TimeInterval defaulting to 60) parameters
1. FR4: testCommandHook shall detect inline scripts (not starting with / or $) and write them to temporary files with 0o755 permissions
1. FR5: testCommandHook shall substitute $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR with FileManager.default.currentDirectoryPath in script paths
1. FR6: testCommandHook shall substitute $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with currentDirectoryPath + /.claude in script paths
1. FR7: testCommandHook shall encode HookInput as JSON using JSONEncoder for stdin pipe
1. FR8: testCommandHook shall spawn /bin/bash -c with echo piping JSON to script via stdin
1. FR9: testCommandHook shall escape single quotes in JSON input using '\'' replacement pattern
1. FR10: testCommandHook shall capture stdout and stderr via separate Pipe instances
1. FR11: testCommandHook shall implement timeout using DispatchSemaphore with .wait(timeout:) returning .timedOut on expiration
1. FR12: testCommandHook shall terminate process and return failure TestResult when timeout is exceeded
1. FR13: testCommandHook shall parse stdout as HookOutput using JSONDecoder when output is non-empty
1. FR14: testCommandHook shall append parse errors to errors array when JSON decoding fails
1. FR15: testCommandHook shall append stderr content to errors array when stderr is non-empty
1. FR16: testCommandHook shall calculate success as exitCode == 0 AND errors.isEmpty
1. FR17: testCommandHook shall calculate duration using Date().timeIntervalSince(startTime)
1. FR18: testCommandHook shall clean up temporary script files in defer block using FileManager.removeItem
1. FR19: generateTestCommand shall accept scriptPath (String) and input (HookInput) parameters
1. FR20: generateTestCommand shall return shell command string with properly escaped JSON and script path

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: Test execution overhead (excluding script runtime) shall be under 50ms
- NFR2: Memory usage during test shall not exceed 10MB excluding script output buffers
- NFR3: Timeout precision shall be within 100ms of specified timeout value
- NFR4: Actor isolation shall prevent data races when running concurrent tests
- NFR5: Temporary file cleanup shall occur in all code paths including error and timeout cases
- NFR6: JSON encoding/decoding shall handle all HookInput and HookOutput field types without data loss

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create new file HookTestRunner.swift in Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/ directory
1. Step 2: Add Foundation import at top of file
1. Step 3: Define public actor HookTestRunner with no stored properties (stateless service)
1. Step 4: Define TestResult struct inside actor with public access and Sendable conformance
1. Step 5: Add TestResult properties: success (Bool), output (String), exitCode (Int), duration (TimeInterval), parsedOutput (HookOutput?), errors ([String])
1. Step 6: Implement testCommandHook method signature with command, input, timeout parameters
1. Step 7: Record startTime using Date() at method entry
1. Step 8: Implement script path resolution: check if command starts with / or $ to determine inline vs external
1. Step 9: For inline scripts: create temp file path using temporaryDirectory + UUID, write command, set permissions 0o755
1. Step 10: For external scripts: replace $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with resolved paths
1. Step 11: Add defer block to delete temp file if cleanup flag is true
1. Step 12: Encode HookInput to JSON using JSONEncoder, convert to String with UTF-8
1. Step 13: Create Process instance with executableURL = /bin/bash
1. Step 14: Set process arguments to [-c, echo 'JSON' | scriptPath] with escaped single quotes
1. Step 15: Create outputPipe and errorPipe as Pipe instances, assign to standardOutput and standardError
1. Step 16: Call process.run() wrapped in try to handle launch failures
1. Step 17: Create DispatchSemaphore with value 0 for timeout coordination
1. Step 18: Dispatch async block that calls process.waitUntilExit() then signals semaphore
1. Step 19: Wait on semaphore with timeout, check for .timedOut result
1. Step 20: On timeout: call process.terminate(), return failure TestResult with timeout error message
1. Step 21: Read outputData and errorData from pipes using readDataToEndOfFile()
1. Step 22: Convert outputData to String with UTF-8 encoding, default to empty string
1. Step 23: Convert errorData to String with UTF-8 encoding, default to empty string
1. Step 24: Get exitCode from process.terminationStatus as Int
1. Step 25: Calculate duration using Date().timeIntervalSince(startTime)
1. Step 26: Initialize empty errors array and nil parsedOutput
1. Step 27: If output is non-empty after trimming, attempt JSONDecoder.decode as HookOutput
1. Step 28: On decode failure, append parse error message to errors array with localizedDescription
1. Step 29: If errorOutput is non-empty, append stderr: prefix + content to errors array
1. Step 30: Construct and return TestResult with all collected values
1. Step 31: Implement generateTestCommand method with scriptPath and input parameters
1. Step 32: Encode input using JSONEncoder with sortedKeys for deterministic output
1. Step 33: Construct shell command string with echo, escaped JSON, pipe, and bash scriptPath
1. Step 34: Return formatted command string suitable for copy-paste to terminal
1. Step 35: Add documentation comments to all public types and methods

#### Data Model Changes
- New actor HookTestRunner: Stateless service actor for executing hook tests in isolation
- New struct TestResult: Sendable value type containing success (Bool), output (String), exitCode (Int), duration (TimeInterval), parsedOutput (HookOutput?), errors ([String])
- No database changes: Test runner is ephemeral with no persistence requirements
- No model migrations: New types only, no modifications to existing types

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- HookTestRunner.testCommandHook(command: String, input: HookInput, timeout: TimeInterval = 60) async throws -> TestResult - Executes command hook with provided input and returns structured test result
- HookTestRunner.generateTestCommand(scriptPath: String, input: HookInput) throws -> String - Returns shell command for manual debugging in terminal
- TestResult.success: Bool - True if exitCode is 0 and no errors occurred
- TestResult.output: String - Raw stdout content from hook execution
- TestResult.exitCode: Int - Process termination status (0 = success)
- TestResult.duration: TimeInterval - Execution time in seconds
- TestResult.parsedOutput: HookOutput? - Decoded hook output if valid JSON returned
- TestResult.errors: [String] - Collection of error messages including stderr and parse failures

**Event Contracts:**
- No custom events emitted: Test runner is a synchronous service with result returned directly
- HookOutput parsed from stdout follows existing HookOutput contract with result field (continue/block/error) and optional message field
- Actor isolation ensures no concurrent state mutations requiring event coordination

#### UI States
- Test idle state: Run Test button enabled, no results displayed
- Test running state: Run Test button disabled, progress spinner visible, Abort button available
- Test success state: Green checkmark icon, exit code 0 displayed, duration shown, parsed output in expandable section
- Test failure state: Red X icon, non-zero exit code displayed, errors listed in red text
- Test timeout state: Yellow warning icon, timeout message displayed, process terminated message shown
- Parse warning state: Orange warning badge on output section indicating JSON parse failure with raw output still visible

#### UI Interactions
- User clicks Run Test button triggering testCommandHook call with current hook config and sample input
- User clicks Abort button during test execution triggering Task cancellation and process termination
- User expands Output section to view raw stdout content from hook execution
- User expands Errors section to view stderr content and parse failures
- User clicks Copy Command button triggering generateTestCommand and copying result to clipboard
- User adjusts timeout slider to modify test timeout duration before execution

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: Command string is empty - should throw or return error immediately without spawning process
- Edge case 2: Script path contains spaces - must be quoted properly in bash -c argument
- Edge case 3: HookInput contains single quotes - must escape as '\'' to prevent shell injection
- Edge case 4: Hook script does not exist - process will fail with file not found, captured in stderr
- Edge case 5: Hook script is not executable - permission denied error captured in stderr
- Edge case 6: Hook outputs invalid JSON - parse fails gracefully, raw output still available in result
- Edge case 7: Hook outputs valid JSON but wrong schema - decode fails, error message includes decoding details
- Edge case 8: Hook outputs nothing (empty stdout) - parsedOutput is nil, not an error condition
- Edge case 9: Hook writes to stderr but exits 0 - success is false because errors array is non-empty
- Edge case 10: Hook hangs indefinitely - timeout fires, process terminated, timeout error returned
- Edge case 11: Hook exits immediately with non-zero code - failure captured with stderr content
- Edge case 12: Temporary file creation fails - throw error from write operation, no cleanup needed
- Edge case 13: Multiple concurrent tests - actor isolation ensures each test has independent state
- Edge case 14: Process spawn fails - try/catch around process.run() handles launch errors
- Edge case 15: Very large stdout output (megabytes) - memory handled by Data, may hit practical limits

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: Script not found error - Display: Hook script not found at path. Check: script path and $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR resolution
- FM2: Permission denied error - Display: Cannot execute hook script. Suggestion: Run chmod +x on the script file
- FM3: Timeout exceeded - Display: Hook execution timed out after N seconds. Suggestion: Increase timeout or optimize hook
- FM4: JSON parse failure - Display: Hook output is not valid JSON. Show raw output for debugging
- FM5: Process spawn failure - Display: Failed to start hook process. Check system resources and bash availability
- FM6: Temporary file write failure - Display: Cannot create temporary script file. Check disk space and permissions
- FM7: UTF-8 encoding failure - Display: Hook output contains invalid characters. Check script encoding
- FM8: Script crashes or segfaults - Display: Hook process terminated abnormally (signal N). Check script for bugs

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/HookTestRunner.swift file. Remove any imports or references to HookTestRunner from other files (likely HookBuilderPanel.swift or similar). The test runner is a standalone service with no persistence or external dependencies. No database migrations to revert. No user data affected as test results are ephemeral and never persisted.

| hook_test_count | counter | tests | Track total hook test executions for usage analytics | Incremented each time testCommandHook is called regardless of outcome |
| hook_test_duration | histogram | milliseconds | Measure test execution time distribution, target p50 under 500ms for typical hooks | Recorded from method entry to result return, bucketed at 100,500,1000,5000,30000ms |
| hook_test_success_rate | gauge | percentage | Track pass rate of hook tests, expect high rate for deployed hooks | Calculated as successes/total over sliding window |
| hook_test_timeout_rate | gauge | percentage | Track timeout rate, target under 5% indicating reasonable timeout defaults | Calculated as timeouts/total over sliding window |

#### Telemetry Events
- `hook_test_started: Emitted when testCommandHook begins with hook_type=command`
- `hook_test_completed: Emitted when testCommandHook finishes with success (bool), duration_ms (int), exit_code (int)`
- `hook_test_timeout: Emitted when test exceeds timeout with timeout_seconds (int)`
- `hook_test_parse_failed: Emitted when JSON parsing fails with error_type (string)`

#### Acceptance Tests
- AT1: Given a hook script that echoes input, when testCommandHook is called with sample HookInput, then TestResult contains the echoed JSON in output field
- AT2: Given a hook script that exits with code 1, when testCommandHook is called, then TestResult.success is false and exitCode is 1
- AT3: Given a hook script that outputs valid HookOutput JSON, when testCommandHook is called, then TestResult.parsedOutput contains decoded HookOutput
- AT4: Given a hook script that outputs invalid JSON, when testCommandHook is called, then TestResult.parsedOutput is nil and errors contains parse failure message
- AT5: Given a hook script that blocks for 2 seconds, when testCommandHook is called with timeout=1, then TestResult contains timeout error message
- AT6: Given generateTestCommand called with script path and input, when returned command is run in terminal, then output matches testCommandHook result

#### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] HookTestRunner actor is defined in Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/HookTestRunner.swift
- [ ] TestResult struct contains all required fields: success, output, exitCode, duration, parsedOutput, errors
- [ ] testCommandHook method handles both inline scripts and external script paths
- [ ] testCommandHook properly substitutes $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in paths
- [ ] testCommandHook escapes single quotes in JSON input to prevent shell injection
- [ ] testCommandHook implements timeout using DispatchSemaphore and terminates process on expiration
- [ ] testCommandHook parses stdout as HookOutput when valid JSON is returned
- [ ] testCommandHook captures stderr content in errors array
- [ ] Temporary script files are cleaned up in all code paths via defer block
- [ ] generateTestCommand returns valid shell command for copy-paste debugging
- [ ] All unit tests pass with minimum 90% code coverage on HookTestRunner

#### Definition of Done
- [ ] HookTestRunner.swift exists at Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/HookTestRunner.swift
- [ ] Actor contains testCommandHook and generateTestCommand public methods
- [ ] TestResult struct is defined with all required properties and Sendable conformance
- [ ] Script path variable substitution handles $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT
- [ ] Timeout mechanism terminates hung processes and returns appropriate error
- [ ] JSON parsing of HookOutput succeeds for valid output and fails gracefully for invalid
- [ ] Temp file cleanup occurs in defer block for inline scripts
- [ ] All unit tests pass covering happy path, error cases, and edge cases
- [ ] Code compiles without warnings on Swift 5.9 with macOS 13.0+ deployment target

**Requires:** Tests, Telemetry, Error Handling, Rollback Plan

#### Completion
**Completed When:** HookTestRunner.swift is fully implemented with testCommandHook method that can execute command hooks with sample input, capture all output streams, handle timeouts, parse HookOutput JSON, and return comprehensive TestResult. Unit tests cover success, failure, timeout, and parse error scenarios. Integration test demonstrates real hook script execution with stdin/stdout piping.

**Evidence:** Screenshot of Xcode showing HookTestRunnerTests passing with green checkmarks. Console output showing successful test of real hook script with JSON input and parsed output. Code review approval confirming actor isolation, timeout handling, and cleanup logic are correct.

#### Source References
- docs/new-features-v2.md section F009 B006-TESTING
- Claude Code hooks documentation for hook protocol reference

#### Open Questions
- Should testCommandHook support environment variable injection for custom test environments?
- Should TestResult include memory usage or CPU time metrics for performance debugging?
- Should there be a dry-run mode that validates script path without execution?
- Should generateTestCommand support outputting to a temp file for very long JSON inputs?

#### Notes
The test runner is a critical developer experience improvement. By providing immediate feedback on hook behavior with structured output, developers can iterate faster and deploy with confidence. The generateTestCommand helper enables debugging in terminal when the UI-based tester is insufficient. Consider adding support for test fixtures or saved test cases in a future atom.
