#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- TutorialStepContainer.init(target: TutorialTarget, title: String, body: String, showPrevious: Bool, nextLabel: String, onPrevious: () -> Void, onNext: () -> Void) - container view builder
- TutorialStepCopy.step1Title: String - returns 'Start a Session'
- TutorialStepCopy.step1Body: String - returns description of session creation
- TutorialStepCopy.step2Title: String - returns 'Worktree Navigator'
- TutorialStepCopy.step2Body: String - returns description of worktree sidebar
- TutorialStepCopy.step3Title: String - returns 'File Explorer'
- TutorialStepCopy.step3Body: String - returns description of file tree
- TutorialStepCopy.step4Title: String - returns 'Live Terminal'
- TutorialStepCopy.step4Body: String - returns description of terminal panel
- TutorialStepCopy.step5Title: String - returns 'Conversation Flow'
- TutorialStepCopy.step5Body: String - returns description of chat area
- TutorialStepCopy.step6Title: String - returns 'Prompt Composer'
- TutorialStepCopy.step6Body: String - returns description of chat input
- TutorialStepCopy.step7Title: String - returns 'Activity Panel'
- TutorialStepCopy.step7Body: String - returns description of right sidebar tabs
- CalloutPosition.calculateOptimal(targetRect: CGRect, containerBounds: CGRect) -> CalloutPosition - returns best placement
- TutorialStep1View.init(viewModel: TutorialViewModel) -> some View
- TutorialStep2View.init(viewModel: TutorialViewModel) -> some View
- TutorialStep3View.init(viewModel: TutorialViewModel) -> some View
- TutorialStep4View.init(viewModel: TutorialViewModel) -> some View
- TutorialStep5View.init(viewModel: TutorialViewModel) -> some View
- TutorialStep6View.init(viewModel: TutorialViewModel) -> some View
- TutorialStep7View.init(viewModel: TutorialViewModel) -> some View

**Event Contracts:**
- tutorial_step_viewed: Emitted when step becomes visible with { step_number: Int, step_name: String, target: String }
- tutorial_step_navigation: Emitted when Previous/Next clicked with { from_step: Int, to_step: Int, direction: 'previous' | 'next' | 'finish' }
- tutorial_step_dwell_time: Emitted when leaving a step with { step_number: Int, dwell_seconds: Double }
- tutorial_callout_expanded: Emitted if callout has expandable details and user expands (future) with { step_number: Int }

#### UI States
- Step 1 active state: Spotlight over New Session button, callout visible, Previous hidden, Next shows 'Next'
- Step 2-6 active states: Spotlight over respective target, callout visible, Previous visible, Next shows 'Next'
- Step 7 active state: Spotlight over Right Sidebar, callout visible, Previous visible, Next shows 'Finish'
- Transition state: Previous spotlight fading out, new spotlight fading in, callout crossfading
- Keyboard focused state: Current navigation button has focus ring indicator
- VoiceOver active state: Callout text announced, navigation buttons labeled with actions

#### UI Interactions
- User clicks Next button: Spotlight moves to next target area, step counter increments, callout updates
- User clicks Previous button: Spotlight moves to previous target area, step counter decrements, callout updates
- User clicks Finish button (step 7): Tutorial overlay dismisses, main app fully visible
- User presses Right Arrow key: Same as clicking Next button
- User presses Left Arrow key: Same as clicking Previous button (no-op on step 1)
- User presses Escape key: Tutorial dismisses early with confirmation prompt (if implemented) or immediate dismiss
- User presses Tab key: Focus moves between Previous and Next buttons
- User resizes window: Spotlight position updates dynamically to follow target anchor
- VoiceOver user navigates: Step title and body announced, button actions described

#### Edge Cases
- User resizes window so target area moves off-screen: Spotlight and callout reposition or show fallback message
- User opens Settings sheet while tutorial active: Tutorial pauses, resumes when sheet closes (or dismisses tutorial)
- User changes theme while tutorial active: Callout colors update dynamically to match new theme
- User with very large Dynamic Type: Callout expands to accommodate text, may need scroll if extremely large
- User on small screen (MacBook Air): Callouts may need to use compact layout to fit
- User rapidly clicks Next: Navigation is debounced, only one step advance per 250ms
- User at step 7 clicks Previous then immediately Next: Both navigate correctly without race conditions
- Target UI area is hidden (e.g., sidebar collapsed): Show callout with message to expand sidebar first or skip step
- VoiceOver user navigates out of tutorial overlay: Focus trap keeps focus within tutorial until dismissed

#### Failure Modes
- Preference key returns zero rect for target: Show fallback spotlight at center screen with warning, log error
- TutorialViewModel currentStep is nil or invalid: Default to step 1, log state corruption warning
- Callout text fails to load from copy struct: Show placeholder text, log missing copy error
- Animation spring timing causes jank on older hardware: Fall back to linear animation if frame drops detected
- Memory pressure during tutorial: Views are lightweight, no special handling needed but log if views recreated frequently
- SwiftUI view diffing causes flicker: Ensure step views have stable identity to prevent unnecessary recreation

#### Rollback Plan
Remove TutorialStep1-7View files and TutorialStepContainer. Update TutorialOverlayView to show generic placeholder content. Tutorial infrastructure from O009 remains functional but shows static content instead of step-by-step tour. No persistence changes to reverse.

### E005-F003-S003-T001-A001 — BlazeApp Onboarding Integration

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 1.0 days

> **Epic:** Onboarding Experience
> **Feature:** First-Run Onboarding Flow
> **Story:** App Integration and Lifecycle Wiring
> **Task:** Wire Onboarding and Tutorial into BlazeApp Entry Point

#### Problem Statement
The onboarding infrastructure (OnboardingRootView, OnboardingViewModel) and tutorial system (TutorialOverlayView, TutorialViewModel) exist as isolated modules. They must be wired into the main app entry point (BlazeApp.swift) to trigger automatically on first launch, resume if interrupted, show tutorial on demand, and welcome returning users by name. Without this integration, users would see the main app immediately without setup guidance.

#### Description
Add @AppStorage bindings for hasCompletedOnboarding and userName, @State properties for showOnboarding, showTutorial, and showWelcomeBack, fullScreenCover modifier for OnboardingRootView, overlay modifier for TutorialOverlayView, onAppear logic to determine which flow to trigger, and environment object injection for OnboardingViewModel and TutorialViewModel.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Add @AppStorage property wrapper for hasCompletedOnboarding Bool in BlazeApp
- Add @AppStorage property wrapper for userName String in BlazeApp
- Add @State private var showOnboarding Bool initialized from hasCompletedOnboarding negation
- Add @State private var showTutorial Bool initialized to false
- Add @State private var showWelcomeBack Bool initialized to false
- Add @StateObject or @State for OnboardingViewModel instance
- Add @StateObject or @State for TutorialViewModel instance
- Add .fullScreenCover(isPresented: $showOnboarding) modifier presenting OnboardingRootView
- Add .overlay modifier conditionally rendering TutorialOverlayView when showTutorial is true
- Add .onAppear modifier with conditional logic for first-time vs returning user detection
- Add .environmentObject injection for OnboardingViewModel to OnboardingRootView
- Add .environmentObject injection for TutorialViewModel to TutorialOverlayView
- Add welcome-back toast view component with fade-in animation
- Add userName interpolation in welcome-back message
- Add dismiss handler for onboarding completion that sets showOnboarding to false
- Add binding from OnboardingRootView completion to trigger optional tutorial flow
- Add global keyboard shortcut (Cmd+Shift+T) to toggle tutorial overlay from anywhere
- Update ContentView to support tutorial anchor points via preference keys

**Out of Scope:**
- OnboardingRootView implementation - completed in E005-F003-S001-T001
- OnboardingViewModel implementation - completed in E005-F003-S001-T001
- Individual onboarding screen implementations - completed in O002-O008 atoms
- TutorialOverlayView implementation - completed in O009-TUTORIAL-INFRA atom
- TutorialViewModel implementation - completed in O009-TUTORIAL-INFRA atom
- Individual tutorial step implementations - completed in O010-O016 atoms
- Animation polish for onboarding transitions - handled in O018-POLISH atom
- Localization of welcome-back strings - deferred to L10N epic
- Deep linking to specific onboarding steps - not in scope for initial release

#### Functional Requirements
1. BlazeApp body creates WindowGroup containing ContentView as root
1. ContentView has .fullScreenCover modifier with isPresented bound to showOnboarding
1. showOnboarding initializes to true if hasCompletedOnboarding is false
1. showOnboarding initializes to false if hasCompletedOnboarding is true
1. fullScreenCover presents OnboardingRootView with OnboardingViewModel as environmentObject
1. fullScreenCover uses interactiveDismissDisabled(true) to prevent accidental dismissal
1. OnboardingRootView completion callback sets showOnboarding to false
1. OnboardingRootView completion callback optionally sets showTutorial to true if user selected tutorial
1. ContentView has .overlay modifier that conditionally renders TutorialOverlayView when showTutorial is true
1. TutorialOverlayView receives TutorialViewModel as environmentObject
1. TutorialOverlayView completion callback sets showTutorial to false
1. ContentView has .onAppear modifier that runs first-launch detection logic
1. onAppear sets showOnboarding to true if hasCompletedOnboarding is false
1. onAppear sets showWelcomeBack to true if hasCompletedOnboarding is true AND userName is non-empty
1. Welcome-back overlay displays toast with 'Welcome back, {userName}!' message
1. Welcome-back toast uses slide-down animation with 0.3s ease-out timing
1. Welcome-back toast auto-dismisses after 3 seconds via DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter
1. Global keyboard shortcut Cmd+Shift+T toggles showTutorial from any app state
1. Cmd+Shift+T does nothing if onboarding is currently showing
1. Tutorial can be re-triggered any time after onboarding completion via keyboard shortcut or Settings menu

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- App launch to first meaningful paint under 500ms for returning users
- App launch to onboarding display under 300ms for first-time users
- Memory overhead of integration code under 500 bytes
- No retain cycles introduced by @State/@StateObject/@EnvironmentObject bindings
- All transitions respect accessibilityReduceMotion preference
- VoiceOver announces 'Onboarding' when fullScreenCover appears
- VoiceOver announces 'Welcome back' when toast appears

#### Implementation Steps
1. Open Blaze/Sources/App/BlazeApp.swift for editing
1. Add import statement for Onboarding module if not already present
1. Add import statement for Tutorial module if not already present
1. Add @AppStorage(hasCompletedOnboarding) var hasCompletedOnboarding = false property
1. Add @AppStorage(userName) var userName = String.empty property
1. Add @State private var showOnboarding = false property
1. Add @State private var showTutorial = false property
1. Add @State private var showWelcomeBack = false property
1. Add @StateObject private var onboardingViewModel = OnboardingViewModel() property
1. Add @StateObject private var tutorialViewModel = TutorialViewModel() property
1. Locate WindowGroup body and ContentView instantiation
1. Add .fullScreenCover(isPresented: $showOnboarding) modifier to ContentView
1. Inside fullScreenCover closure, return OnboardingRootView()
1. Add .environmentObject(onboardingViewModel) modifier to OnboardingRootView
1. Add .interactiveDismissDisabled(true) modifier to fullScreenCover content
1. Add .onDisappear handler to fullScreenCover that checks if tutorial should start
1. Add .overlay modifier to ContentView after fullScreenCover
1. Inside overlay, add conditional if showTutorial { TutorialOverlayView() }
1. Add .environmentObject(tutorialViewModel) modifier to TutorialOverlayView
1. Add .onAppear modifier to ContentView at end of modifier chain
1. In onAppear closure, add if !hasCompletedOnboarding { showOnboarding = true }
1. In onAppear closure, add else if !userName.isEmpty { showWelcomeBack = true }

#### Data Model Changes

- WelcomeBackToast is a pure view component with no data model

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- BlazeApp.hasCompletedOnboarding: Bool (read from AppStorage, triggers onboarding)
- BlazeApp.userName: String (read from AppStorage, used in welcome-back)
- BlazeApp.showOnboarding: Bool (controls fullScreenCover presentation)
- BlazeApp.showTutorial: Bool (controls tutorial overlay visibility)
- BlazeApp.showWelcomeBack: Bool (controls welcome-back toast visibility)
- WelcomeBackToast.init(userName: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>) - toast component
- OnboardingRootView.onComplete: ((startTutorial: Bool) -> Void)? - completion callback
- TutorialOverlayView.onComplete: (() -> Void)? - dismissal callback

**Event Contracts:**
- app_launched: Emitted on BlazeApp body evaluation with { is_first_launch: Bool, has_completed_onboarding: Bool }
- onboarding_presented: Emitted when showOnboarding becomes true with { trigger: 'first_launch' | 'manual' }
- onboarding_dismissed: Emitted when showOnboarding becomes false with { start_tutorial: Bool }
- tutorial_presented: Emitted when showTutorial becomes true with { trigger: 'post_onboarding' | 'keyboard_shortcut' | 'settings_menu' }
- tutorial_dismissed: Emitted when showTutorial becomes false with { completed: Bool, last_step: Int }
- welcome_back_shown: Emitted when showWelcomeBack becomes true with { user_name: String }
- welcome_back_dismissed: Emitted when showWelcomeBack becomes false with { dismiss_type: 'auto' | 'tap' }

#### UI States
- Initial launch (first-time): ContentView renders, immediately covered by OnboardingRootView fullScreenCover
- Initial launch (returning user with name): ContentView renders, WelcomeBackToast slides down from top
- Initial launch (returning user without name): ContentView renders normally, no toast
- Onboarding active: fullScreenCover visible, ContentView behind but not interactive
- Onboarding completing: fullScreenCover animates away, ContentView becomes interactive
- Tutorial active: ContentView visible with TutorialOverlayView overlay, spotlight on target area
- Tutorial inactive: ContentView fully interactive, no overlay
- Welcome-back visible: Toast overlay at top of screen, ContentView fully interactive below
- Welcome-back dismissing: Toast slides up and fades out over 0.3s

#### UI Interactions
- User launches app (first time): OnboardingRootView appears automatically as fullScreenCover
- User completes onboarding without tutorial: fullScreenCover dismisses, ContentView shown
- User completes onboarding with tutorial: fullScreenCover dismisses, TutorialOverlayView appears
- User presses Cmd+Shift+T: Tutorial overlay toggles on/off (if not in onboarding)
- User launches app (returning with name): Welcome-back toast appears, auto-dismisses after 3s
- User taps welcome-back toast: Toast dismisses immediately
- User swipes down on onboarding: Nothing happens (interactiveDismissDisabled)
- User clicks outside tutorial spotlight: Tutorial advances or dismisses based on TutorialViewModel

#### Edge Cases
- User force-quits during onboarding: hasCompletedOnboarding remains false, onboarding shows again on next launch
- User completes onboarding then deletes preferences: hasCompletedOnboarding resets, onboarding shows again
- User has userName but hasCompletedOnboarding is false (corrupted state): Onboarding takes precedence, no welcome-back
- User rapidly toggles Cmd+Shift+T: showTutorial toggles each time, no race condition due to SwiftUI binding
- User triggers tutorial while welcome-back toast is visible: Both can coexist, toast dismisses normally
- Window loses focus during onboarding: fullScreenCover remains visible, no interaction issues
- System enters low-power mode during onboarding: Animations may be reduced, functionality preserved
- VoiceOver user in onboarding: fullScreenCover announces as modal, escape does not dismiss
- User has empty userName after onboarding (skipped profile): No welcome-back toast on subsequent launches

#### Failure Modes
- OnboardingRootView fails to load (import error): App crashes on launch - caught by build-time check
- TutorialOverlayView fails to load (import error): Tutorial button does nothing - caught by build-time check
- AppStorage read fails (corrupted plist): Defaults to false/empty, triggers onboarding
- @StateObject initialization fails (memory): App crashes - extremely rare, no mitigation
- fullScreenCover animation hangs: UI appears frozen - covered by SwiftUI framework stability
- Timer for welcome-back dismiss leaks: Toast never auto-dismisses - use weak self in closure
- Environment object not injected: Child views crash on access - caught by testing

#### Rollback Plan
Revert BlazeApp.swift to remove fullScreenCover and overlay modifiers. Delete WelcomeBackToast.swift. ContentView returns to direct rendering without conditional flows. Users who have not completed onboarding will see main app directly. AppStorage keys remain but are ignored. No data migration needed.

### E005-F005-S001-T005-A001 — InstallationProgressView UI Component

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1 days

> **Epic:** Onboarding Experience
> **Feature:** CLI Detection and Installation
> **Story:** CLI Installation Flow
> **Task:** Implement Installation Progress View

#### Problem Statement
During CLI installation which can take 30-120 seconds depending on network speed and package size, users need visual feedback to understand installation progress, see what step is currently executing, monitor for errors, and have the ability to cancel a stalled or unwanted installation. Without this view, users would see a blank or spinning state with no indication of progress or ability to intervene.

#### Description
Implement a SwiftUI view that renders real-time CLI installation progress including: current step indicator with checkmarks for completed steps, animated progress bar for current operation, streaming terminal output preview, elapsed time counter, cancel button with confirmation, error state display with retry option, and success completion state with celebration animation.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- InstallationProgressView SwiftUI struct accepting InstallProgress binding and cancel callback
- Progress step list showing all installation phases with visual state indicators (pending, active, completed, failed)
- Animated progress bar for current active step with indeterminate mode for unknown duration operations
- Terminal output preview showing last 10 lines of stdout/stderr from installation process
- Elapsed time display with live updating timer showing MM:SS format
- Cancel button that triggers confirmation alert before stopping installation
- Error state view showing error message, failed step, and retry button
- Success state view with checkmark animation and 'Continue' button
- Accessibility labels for VoiceOver announcing progress changes and step completion
- Keyboard shortcut Cmd+. to trigger cancel confirmation

**Out of Scope:**
- Actual process spawning and management - handled by CLIInstallationService (C002-SERVICE)
- Installation state machine logic - handled by CLIInstallationState (C003-STATE)
- CLI detection logic - handled by CLIInstallationService
- Parent view orchestration - handled by OnboardingCLISetupView (C004-VIEW)
- Network error handling and retries - handled by CLIInstallationService
- Dependency resolution (checking Node.js, Python presence) - handled by CLIInstallationService
- Installation queue management for multiple CLIs - handled by CLISetupViewModel

#### Functional Requirements
1. InstallationProgressView accepts InstallProgress Binding and onCancel closure as init parameters
1. View displays vertical list of installation steps derived from InstallProgress.steps array
1. Each step row shows: SF Symbol icon (circle for pending, arrow.circlepath for active, checkmark.circle.fill for completed, xmark.circle.fill for failed), step name text, and optional duration for completed steps
1. Currently active step row has highlighted background color and animated icon rotation
1. Progress bar below step list shows InstallProgress.progress value (0.0 to 1.0) or indeterminate animation if progress is nil
1. Terminal output section displays last 10 lines from InstallProgress.outputLines in monospace font with dark background
1. Elapsed time label updates every second showing format 'Elapsed: MM:SS'
1. Cancel button is always visible and enabled during active installation
1. Cancel button click shows confirmation alert with 'Cancel Installation' and 'Continue' options
1. Confirming cancel triggers onCancel closure callback
1. Error state replaces progress view when InstallProgress.error is non-nil
1. Error state shows error icon, error message, failed step name, and Retry button
1. Retry button click clears error and restarts installation via onRetry callback
1. Success state shows when InstallProgress.isComplete is true with no errors
1. Success state displays checkmark with scale animation, 'Installation Complete' message, and Continue button
1. Continue button triggers onComplete callback to advance wizard

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- Progress bar animation uses spring timing with duration 0.3s for smooth updates
- Step list updates trigger implicit animation with duration 0.25s
- Timer updates at 1Hz frequency to show elapsed seconds
- Terminal output scroll position auto-scrolls to bottom on new lines
- Memory usage stays under 2MB even with 1000+ output lines (only last 10 displayed)
- VoiceOver announces step changes with 0.5s debounce to prevent rapid-fire announcements

#### Implementation Steps
1. Create Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Views/InstallationProgressView.swift file
1. Define InstallProgressStep struct with id, name, status enum (pending, active, completed, failed), duration optional
1. Define InstallProgress ObservableObject with steps array, currentStepIndex, progress Double optional, outputLines array, elapsedSeconds Int, error optional, isComplete Bool
1. Create InstallationProgressView struct with @Binding progress and callback closures
1. Implement stepRowView helper that renders single step with icon and text
1. Add conditional icon rendering based on step.status with rotation animation for active
1. Implement stepsListView using ForEach over progress.steps with stepRowView
1. Add ProgressView with progress.progress value or indeterminate style
1. Create terminalOutputView with ScrollView, monospace Text, dark background
1. Implement timerView with Text binding to progress.elapsedSeconds formatted as MM:SS
1. Add Timer publisher that updates elapsedSeconds every 1 second
1. Create cancelButton with Button and destructive role
1. Implement cancelConfirmationAlert modifier with .alert binding to showCancelConfirmation state
1. Create errorStateView with VStack containing error icon, message, step name, Retry button
1. Implement successStateView with checkmark icon, scale animation, message, Continue button
1. Compose main body with conditional rendering: errorStateView if error, successStateView if complete, else progressContentView
1. Add keyboard shortcut .cancelAction to cancel button
1. Add accessibility labels to all interactive elements
1. Add accessibility announcements for step status changes using AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
1. Write unit tests for progress state rendering
1. Write UI tests for cancel flow and error recovery

**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Views/InstallationProgressView.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Models/InstallProgress.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Views/OnboardingCLISetupView.swift`
- `BlazeTests/InstallationProgressViewTests.swift`

**New Files:**


#### Data Model Changes
- Extend InstallProgress struct (from C003-STATE) to include outputLines: [String] array for terminal output
- Add isComplete computed property to InstallProgress that returns true when all steps are completed status
- Add formattedElapsedTime computed property returning MM:SS string from elapsedSeconds

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- InstallationProgressView.init(progress: Binding<InstallProgress>, onCancel: @escaping () -> Void, onRetry: @escaping () -> Void, onComplete: @escaping () -> Void)
- InstallProgress.steps: [InstallProgressStep] - ordered array of installation steps
- InstallProgress.currentStepIndex: Int - index of currently active step
- InstallProgress.progress: Double? - 0.0 to 1.0 for current step, nil for indeterminate
- InstallProgress.outputLines: [String] - terminal output lines (last N kept)
- InstallProgress.elapsedSeconds: Int - seconds since installation started
- InstallProgress.error: CLIInstallError? - error if installation failed
- InstallProgress.isComplete: Bool - true when all steps completed successfully
- InstallProgressStep.id: String - unique identifier for step
- InstallProgressStep.name: String - display name for step
- InstallProgressStep.status: StepStatus - pending, active, completed, or failed
- InstallProgressStep.duration: TimeInterval? - seconds taken for completed steps
- StepStatus enum: pending, active, completed, failed

**Event Contracts:**
- installation_progress_viewed: Emitted when InstallationProgressView appears with { cli_type: String, total_steps: Int }
- installation_step_started: Emitted when step status changes to active with { cli_type: String, step_name: String, step_index: Int }
- installation_step_completed: Emitted when step status changes to completed with { cli_type: String, step_name: String, duration_seconds: Double }
- installation_cancel_requested: Emitted when cancel button clicked (before confirmation) with { cli_type: String, elapsed_seconds: Int, current_step: String }
- installation_cancel_confirmed: Emitted when cancel confirmed with { cli_type: String, elapsed_seconds: Int, current_step: String }
- installation_cancel_dismissed: Emitted when cancel dismissed with { cli_type: String }
- installation_error_displayed: Emitted when error state shown with { cli_type: String, error_type: String, error_message: String, failed_step: String }
- installation_retry_clicked: Emitted when retry button clicked with { cli_type: String, error_type: String }
- installation_completed: Emitted when success state shown with { cli_type: String, total_duration_seconds: Int, steps_count: Int }

#### UI States
- Initial loading state: progress.steps empty, indeterminate spinner, 'Preparing installation' text
- Active installation state: steps list visible with current step highlighted, progress bar animating, terminal output streaming, timer counting
- Step transition state: previous step shows checkmark with fade, current step highlights with spring animation
- Indeterminate progress state: progress bar in indeterminate mode when progress value is nil
- Determinate progress state: progress bar shows actual percentage when progress value is 0.0-1.0
- Cancel confirmation state: alert overlay with 'Cancel Installation?' title and two buttons
- Error state: error icon prominent, error message in red, failed step indicated, Retry button primary action
- Success state: large checkmark with scale-in animation, 'Installation Complete' text, Continue button
- Cancelled state: 'Installation Cancelled' message with option to retry or skip

#### UI Interactions
- User views progress: steps list and progress bar update in real-time as installation proceeds
- User scrolls terminal output: manual scroll overrides auto-scroll, releases to resume auto-scroll
- User clicks Cancel: shows confirmation alert, does not stop installation yet
- User confirms Cancel: triggers onCancel callback, parent stops installation process
- User dismisses Cancel: alert closes, installation continues uninterrupted
- User clicks Retry after error: triggers onRetry callback, error state clears, installation restarts
- User clicks Continue after success: triggers onComplete callback, wizard advances to next screen
- User presses Cmd+Period: equivalent to clicking Cancel button
- VoiceOver user navigates: announces current step, progress percentage, elapsed time

#### Edge Cases
- Installation completes faster than 1 second: timer shows 00:00, success state appears immediately
- Progress jumps from 10% to 90%: animation interpolates smoothly without jarring jump
- Terminal output has 10000+ lines: only last 10 displayed, no memory growth, scroll position maintained
- Installation fails on first step: error state shows with step index 0, all steps show as pending except first
- User cancels during final step: installation may complete before cancel processed, show appropriate state
- Network disconnects mid-install: error state shows network error, retry button available
- User rapidly clicks Cancel then dismisses: confirmation state handles rapid toggle without crash
- View appears with already-completed progress: success state shown immediately without animation
- View appears with already-failed progress: error state shown immediately
- ElapsedSeconds overflows display: after 99:59, show 99:59+ instead of wrapping

#### Failure Modes
- Timer publisher not cancelled on view disappear: use .onDisappear to cancel timer subscription
- Memory leak from output line accumulation: implement circular buffer with max 100 lines stored, 10 displayed
- Animation stutter during rapid updates: batch progress updates with 100ms debounce
- VoiceOver announcement spam: debounce announcements at 500ms minimum interval
- Cancel callback not called: ensure onCancel is non-optional and always invoked on confirm
- Progress binding update on background thread: force MainActor for all binding updates
- Error state not shown: ensure error != nil check happens after progress update

#### Rollback Plan
Remove InstallationProgressView.swift from Xcode project, remove import from OnboardingCLISetupView.swift, replace with simple ProgressView() spinner. No data model changes to reverse. Test files can be deleted.

## Phase 7: Multi-CLI Hooks

### E005-F004-S001-T005-A001 — Provider Selector Segmented Control Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** Multi-CLI Hook Management
> **Feature:** Hook Provider Abstraction
> **Story:** Provider Selector UI
> **Task:** Implement Provider Selector View

#### Problem Statement
The Hooks Builder currently assumes Claude Code as the only target provider. With multi-CLI support, users need to select which provider they are configuring hooks for. Different providers support different hook events (Claude has 12, Gemini has 11, Codex has its own set). Without a provider selector, users cannot create provider-specific hook configurations or understand which events are available for their target CLI.

#### Description
Implement a segmented picker control at the top of the Hooks Builder interface that allows switching between Claude Code (12 events), Gemini (11 events), and Codex (disabled with tooltip). The selector must update the hook canvas to show only events valid for the selected provider and persist the selection across sessions.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- ProviderSelectorView SwiftUI component with Picker using SegmentedPickerStyle
- HookProvider enum with cases for claudeCode, gemini, and codex
- Provider display names: 'Claude Code', 'Gemini', 'Codex'
- Provider availability status: claudeCode (enabled), gemini (enabled), codex (disabled)
- Tooltip for disabled Codex option explaining 'Codex hook integration coming soon'
- Event count badges showing available event count per provider
- Selection binding to parent HooksBuilderViewModel.selectedProvider property
- Persistence of selected provider via AppStorage
- Visual indicator of currently selected provider with accent color
- Keyboard accessibility with arrow key navigation between segments
- Provider-specific icon display (SF Symbols: sparkles for Claude, wand.and.stars for Gemini, terminal for Codex)
- Animated transition when switching providers
- Callback to parent view when provider selection changes

**Out of Scope:**
- Provider-specific event filtering logic in HooksBuilderViewModel - handled by H002-EVENTMAP
- Provider-specific tool name mapping - handled by H007-MIGRATE
- Export to provider-specific config paths - handled by H008-EXPORT
- Session-aware hook context injection - handled by H009-CONTEXT
- Detection of installed CLIs to auto-select default provider - handled by C001-TYPES
- Full HooksBuilderView integration - separate integration task
- Provider authentication status checking - out of scope for MVP

#### Functional Requirements
1. HookProvider enum defines three cases: claudeCode, gemini, codex with String raw values
1. HookProvider.displayName computed property returns localized display string for each provider
1. HookProvider.isEnabled computed property returns true for claudeCode and gemini, false for codex
1. HookProvider.eventCount computed property returns 12 for claudeCode, 11 for gemini, 0 for codex
1. HookProvider.iconName computed property returns SF Symbol name for each provider
1. HookProvider.disabledReason computed property returns nil for enabled providers, explanation string for disabled ones
1. ProviderSelectorView accepts @Binding var selectedProvider: HookProvider parameter
1. ProviderSelectorView renders three-segment Picker with provider display names
1. Selecting claudeCode segment sets selectedProvider to .claudeCode and triggers onChange callback
1. Selecting gemini segment sets selectedProvider to .gemini and triggers onChange callback
1. Codex segment is disabled and selecting it has no effect on selectedProvider
1. Hovering over Codex segment displays tooltip with disabledReason text
1. Event count badge displays as parenthetical suffix: 'Claude Code (12)'
1. Selected segment uses app accent color for highlight
1. Unselected segments use secondary label color
1. Disabled segment uses quaternary label color with 50% opacity
1. Arrow left/right keyboard navigation cycles through enabled segments only
1. AppStorage key 'hooks_selectedProvider' persists raw value of selectedProvider
1. On view appear, selectedProvider initializes from AppStorage or defaults to .claudeCode
1. Provider change animates with easeInOut timing over 200ms

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- Segment selection responds within 16ms for 60fps feedback
- Tooltip appears within 500ms of hover (standard macOS delay)
- Memory footprint of ProviderSelectorView under 512 bytes
- No retain cycles from @Binding or closure captures
- VoiceOver announces provider name, event count, and enabled/disabled status
- Picker supports reduced motion preference by disabling animation

#### Implementation Steps
1. Create Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/Models/HookProvider.swift if not exists
1. Define HookProvider enum with String raw value conformance: case claudeCode = 'claude', gemini = 'gemini', codex = 'codex'
1. Add CaseIterable conformance to HookProvider for iteration
1. Implement displayName computed property with switch returning 'Claude Code', 'Gemini', 'Codex'
1. Implement isEnabled computed property with switch returning true, true, false
1. Implement eventCount computed property with switch returning 12, 11, 0
1. Implement iconName computed property returning 'sparkles', 'wand.and.stars', 'terminal'
1. Implement disabledReason computed property returning nil, nil, 'Codex hook integration coming soon'
1. Create Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/ProviderSelectorView.swift
1. Define ProviderSelectorView struct conforming to View
1. Add @Binding var selectedProvider: HookProvider parameter
1. Add @AppStorage('hooks_selectedProvider') private var storedProvider: String = 'claude'
1. Add @State private var isHoveringDisabled: Bool = false for tooltip tracking
1. Add @Environment accessibilityReduceMotion private var reduceMotion for animation control
1. Implement body with VStack containing Picker
1. Configure Picker with SegmentedPickerStyle()
1. Implement ForEach over HookProvider.allCases for segment content
1. Render segment label with HStack containing Image systemName provider.iconName and Text provider.displayName and Text showing event count in parentheses
1. Apply .disabled(!provider.isEnabled) modifier to codex segment tag
1. Apply .help(provider.disabledReason ?? '') modifier for tooltip on disabled segment
1. Add .onChange(of: selectedProvider) handler to persist to storedProvider
1. Add .onChange(of: selectedProvider) handler to call parent callback if provided
1. Add .onAppear to initialize selectedProvider from storedProvider
1. Apply .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: selectedProvider)
1. Add .accessibilityLabel for each segment including enabled status
1. Create unit test file BlazeTests/Settings/ProviderSelectorViewTests.swift
1. Write tests for HookProvider computed properties
1. Write tests for ProviderSelectorView selection behavior

**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/Models/HookProvider.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/ProviderSelectorView.swift`
- `Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/HooksBuilderView.swift`

#### Data Model Changes
- Add HookProvider enum with String raw value in Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/Models/HookProvider.swift
- HookProvider cases: claudeCode (raw: 'claude'), gemini (raw: 'gemini'), codex (raw: 'codex')
- Add AppStorage key 'hooks_selectedProvider' storing String raw value of HookProvider
- Default value for hooks_selectedProvider is 'claude' (claudeCode)

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- HookProvider.displayName: String - returns human-readable provider name
- HookProvider.isEnabled: Bool - returns whether provider can be selected
- HookProvider.eventCount: Int - returns number of supported hook events
- HookProvider.iconName: String - returns SF Symbol name for provider icon
- HookProvider.disabledReason: String? - returns nil if enabled, explanation if disabled
- ProviderSelectorView.init(selectedProvider: Binding<HookProvider>, onChange: ((HookProvider) -> Void)?) - initializer with binding and optional callback
- ProviderSelectorView.body: some View - renders segmented picker control

**Event Contracts:**
- hooks_provider_selected: Emitted when user selects a different provider with { provider: String, previous_provider: String, event_count: Int }
- hooks_provider_disabled_tapped: Emitted when user attempts to select disabled provider with { provider: String, reason: String }

#### UI States
- Default state: claudeCode segment selected, highlighted with accent color, gemini and codex segments in secondary color
- Gemini selected state: gemini segment highlighted with accent color, others in secondary color
- Codex hover state: codex segment shows tooltip 'Codex hook integration coming soon'
- Disabled visual state: codex segment at 50% opacity with quaternary label color
- Keyboard focus state: focused segment has focus ring indicator
- Loading state: N/A - no async operations in this component

#### UI Interactions
- User clicks Claude Code segment: selectedProvider becomes .claudeCode, segment highlights, onChange fires
- User clicks Gemini segment: selectedProvider becomes .gemini, segment highlights, onChange fires
- User clicks Codex segment: no state change, no selection, tooltip appears after hover delay
- User presses left arrow with focus on Gemini: focus moves to Claude Code, selection changes
- User presses right arrow with focus on Claude Code: focus moves to Gemini, selection changes
- User presses right arrow with focus on Gemini: focus skips disabled Codex, wraps to Claude Code or stops
- User hovers over Codex segment: tooltip appears after 500ms delay
- User moves mouse away from Codex: tooltip dismisses
- VoiceOver user navigates to Codex segment: announces 'Codex, 0 events, disabled, Codex hook integration coming soon'

#### Edge Cases
- AppStorage contains invalid provider string: default to claudeCode, log warning
- AppStorage unavailable (sandbox restriction): use in-memory state only, log warning
- All providers disabled (hypothetical): show informational message instead of empty picker
- Provider enum gains new case in future: CaseIterable handles automatically, verify UI layout
- User rapidly clicks between segments: debounce onChange callback at 100ms
- System appearance changes (dark/light mode): colors update automatically via semantic colors
- Window resized very narrow: segment labels truncate with ellipsis, tooltips still work
- VoiceOver enabled mid-interaction: picker remains accessible, focus not disrupted

#### Failure Modes
- AppStorage write fails: continue with in-memory state, retry on next selection
- Picker fails to render segment: SwiftUI fallback displays plain text
- Icon SF Symbol not found: system shows question mark placeholder, log warning
- Binding update fails: parent view state inconsistent, log error and reset to default
- Animation causes frame drop on slow Mac: reduce motion detected, animation disabled
- Tooltip API unavailable on older macOS: help modifier gracefully degrades to no-op

#### Rollback Plan
Remove ProviderSelectorView from HooksBuilderView, delete ProviderSelectorView.swift and HookProvider.swift, remove AppStorage key usage. Hooks Builder defaults to Claude Code only behavior. No data migration needed as AppStorage key is isolated.

### E005-F003-S002-T001-A001 — E005-F003-S002-T001-A001: Tutorial Overlay Infrastructure Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 2 days

> **Epic:** E005: Onboarding and Tutorial System
> **Feature:** E005-F003: Interactive Tutorial System
> **Story:** E005-F003-S002: Tutorial Overlay Infrastructure
> **Task:** E005-F003-S002-T001: Implement Tutorial Overlay Core Components

#### Problem Statement
New users launching Blaze for the first time have no guided introduction to the application's features. The three-pane layout with sessions, chat, and sidebar contains numerous interactive elements that are not self-discoverable. Without a tutorial system, users may miss key features like worktree management, hook configuration, and timeline visualization.

#### Description
Implement the complete tutorial overlay infrastructure consisting of seven tutorial targets (New Session, Worktree Sidebar, File Tree, Terminal Panel, Chat Area, Chat Input, Right Sidebar), a view model for state management, overlay view for rendering, backdrop for dimming, callout for tooltips, and preference key for anchor positioning.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- TutorialTarget enum defining 7 anchored regions: newSession, worktreeSidebar, fileTree, terminalPanel, chatArea, chatInput, rightSidebar
- TutorialViewModel ObservableObject managing currentStep, isActive, progress calculations, and step navigation
- TutorialOverlayView SwiftUI view composing backdrop and callout based on current target
- TutorialBackdrop view rendering semi-transparent overlay with spotlight cutout using GeometryReader
- TutorialCallout view displaying tooltip with title, description, step indicator, and navigation buttons
- TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey for collecting anchor bounds from tutorial-enabled views
- TutorialAnchorModifier view modifier for marking views as tutorial targets

**Out of Scope:**
- Individual tutorial step content and copy (separate atoms O010-O016)
- App-level integration into BlazeApp.swift (separate atom O017-INTEGRATE)
- Animation polish and accessibility motion settings (separate atom O018-POLISH)
- Persistence of tutorial completion state to UserDefaults
- Tutorial analytics and telemetry events
- Skip tutorial functionality and confirmation dialog

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-001: TutorialTarget enum defines exactly 7 cases: newSession, worktreeSidebar, fileTree, terminalPanel, chatArea, chatInput, rightSidebar
1. FR-002: Each TutorialTarget provides a computed title property returning a localized string
1. FR-003: Each TutorialTarget provides a computed description property returning tutorial copy
1. FR-004: TutorialViewModel publishes currentStep as Int starting at 0
1. FR-005: TutorialViewModel publishes isActive as Bool controlling overlay visibility
1. FR-006: TutorialViewModel provides nextStep() method incrementing currentStep with bounds checking
1. FR-007: TutorialViewModel provides previousStep() method decrementing currentStep with bounds checking
1. FR-008: TutorialViewModel provides skipTutorial() method setting isActive to false
1. FR-009: TutorialViewModel provides currentTarget computed property mapping step index to TutorialTarget
1. FR-010: TutorialOverlayView renders TutorialBackdrop when isActive is true
1. FR-011: TutorialOverlayView renders TutorialCallout positioned relative to current target anchor
1. FR-012: TutorialBackdrop renders a full-window Color.black.opacity(0.6) layer
1. FR-013: TutorialBackdrop cuts out a spotlight rectangle at the target anchor bounds with 8pt padding
1. FR-014: TutorialCallout displays target title in 16pt semibold font
1. FR-015: TutorialCallout displays target description in 14pt regular font with 60% opacity
1. FR-016: TutorialCallout displays step indicator as 'Step N of 7' text
1. FR-017: TutorialCallout provides Previous button disabled on first step
1. FR-018: TutorialCallout provides Next button with 'Finish' label on last step
1. FR-019: TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey collects CGRect values keyed by TutorialTarget
1. FR-020: tutorialAnchor(for:) view modifier applies preference key to any SwiftUI view

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-001: Tutorial overlay must render at 60fps without frame drops during step transitions
- NFR-002: Memory footprint of tutorial system must not exceed 5MB when active
- NFR-003: Tutorial components must be fully accessible via VoiceOver with proper labels
- NFR-004: Callout text must maintain WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against backdrop
- NFR-005: Tutorial must handle window resize events within 16ms without visual glitches

#### Implementation Steps

1. Step 9: Create TutorialOverlayView in TutorialOverlayView.swift composing backdrop and callout

#### Data Model Changes
- TutorialTarget enum: newSession, worktreeSidebar, fileTree, terminalPanel, chatArea, chatInput, rightSidebar
- TutorialAnchorPreferenceKey.Value: [TutorialTarget: CGRect] dictionary mapping targets to frame bounds
- TutorialViewModel.State: currentStep (Int), isActive (Bool), anchors ([TutorialTarget: CGRect])

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- TutorialViewModel.nextStep() -> Void: Increments currentStep if currentStep < 6, otherwise sets isActive to false
- TutorialViewModel.previousStep() -> Void: Decrements currentStep if currentStep > 0
- TutorialViewModel.skipTutorial() -> Void: Sets isActive to false immediately
- TutorialViewModel.startTutorial() -> Void: Sets currentStep to 0 and isActive to true
- TutorialViewModel.currentTarget: TutorialTarget? computed property returning TutorialTarget.allCases[currentStep] or nil
- tutorialAnchor(for: TutorialTarget) -> some ViewModifier: Returns modifier that reports bounds via preference key

**Event Contracts:**
- TutorialStepChanged: Published when currentStep changes, payload includes previousStep and newStep integers
- TutorialCompleted: Published when user reaches final step and taps Finish button
- TutorialSkipped: Published when user taps Skip button at any step
- TutorialStarted: Published when startTutorial() is called

#### UI States
- Inactive: Tutorial overlay not visible, TutorialViewModel.isActive is false
- Active Step N: Overlay visible with spotlight on target N, callout showing step N content
- Transitioning: Brief state during step animation, spotlight and callout animating to new positions
- Completing: Final step with Finish button visible, about to dismiss

#### UI Interactions
- Tap Next button: Advances to next tutorial step or completes tutorial on final step
- Tap Previous button: Returns to previous tutorial step, disabled on first step
- Tap Skip button: Dismisses tutorial immediately without completing
- Tap outside callout: No action, tutorial remains active until explicitly dismissed
- Window resize: Anchors recalculate, spotlight and callout reposition accordingly

#### Edge Cases
- EC-001: Window resized smaller than callout minimum width (280pt) - callout should scroll or truncate gracefully
- EC-002: Tutorial target view not in hierarchy (e.g., sidebar collapsed) - skip that step or show centered callout with instruction to expand
- EC-003: Multiple windows open - tutorial should only appear in frontmost window
- EC-004: App enters background during tutorial - pause tutorial state, resume on foreground
- EC-005: User rapidly taps Next multiple times - debounce navigation to prevent step skipping
- EC-006: Accessibility large text enabled - callout must expand to accommodate larger fonts
- EC-007: Right-to-left language layout - callout positioning must flip appropriately

#### Failure Modes
- FM-001: Preference key returns empty dictionary - fallback to centered overlay without spotlight
- FM-002: TutorialViewModel not injected into environment - fatal error with descriptive message in debug, silent skip in release
- FM-003: Anchor bounds return zero rect - treat as missing target, show generic positioning
- FM-004: Animation interrupted by state change - cancel in-flight animations cleanly
- FM-005: Memory pressure during tutorial - tutorial system should be first to release resources

#### Rollback Plan
To rollback tutorial infrastructure: 1) Delete Blaze/Sources/Tutorial/ directory entirely, 2) Remove any tutorialAnchor modifiers from ContentView and child views, 3) Remove TutorialViewModel @EnvironmentObject from BlazeApp, 4) Remove TutorialOverlayView overlay from ContentView. No data migrations required as tutorial state is ephemeral.

**Unit:**
- TutorialViewModelTests.testInitialState: Verify currentStep is 0 and isActive is false on init
- TutorialViewModelTests.testNextStep: Verify currentStep increments from 0 to 1
- TutorialViewModelTests.testNextStepAtEnd: Verify currentStep stays at 6 and isActive becomes false
- TutorialViewModelTests.testPreviousStep: Verify currentStep decrements from 3 to 2
- TutorialViewModelTests.testPreviousStepAtStart: Verify currentStep stays at 0
- TutorialViewModelTests.testSkipTutorial: Verify isActive becomes false regardless of currentStep
- TutorialViewModelTests.testCurrentTarget: Verify currentTarget returns correct TutorialTarget for each step
- TutorialTargetTests.testAllCasesCount: Verify TutorialTarget.allCases.count equals 7
- TutorialTargetTests.testTitleNotEmpty: Verify each target has non-empty title string
- TutorialTargetTests.testDescriptionNotEmpty: Verify each target has non-empty description string

**Integration:**
- TutorialPreferenceKeyTests.testAnchorCollection: Verify preference key collects bounds from multiple views
- TutorialOverlayIntegrationTests.testBackdropRendersWhenActive: Verify backdrop appears when isActive is true
- TutorialOverlayIntegrationTests.testCalloutPositioning: Verify callout positions near anchor bounds

**Ui:**
- TutorialUITests.testNextButtonAdvancesStep: Launch app, start tutorial, tap Next, verify step indicator shows 'Step 2 of 7'
- TutorialUITests.testPreviousButtonReturnsStep: From step 3, tap Previous, verify step indicator shows 'Step 2 of 7'
- TutorialUITests.testFinishButtonDismisses: Navigate to step 7, tap Finish, verify overlay disappears
- TutorialUITests.testSkipButtonDismisses: From any step, tap Skip, verify overlay disappears

**Perf:**
- TutorialPerfTests.testOverlayRenderPerformance: Measure rendering time for tutorial overlay, target under 16ms
- TutorialPerfTests.testStepTransitionPerformance: Measure time to transition between steps, target under 100ms

**Security:**
- No security tests required - pure UI component

#### Metrics
| Name | Type | Unit | Target | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|-------|
| tutorial_completion_rate | gauge | percentage | Greater than 60% of users who start tutorial should complete it | Track ratio of tutorial.completed to tutorial.started events |

| tutorial_overlay_render_time | timer | milliseconds | Under 16ms for 60fps rendering | Measure using Instruments Time Profiler on overlay draw |

#### Telemetry Events

- `tutorial.step_viewed: Fired on each step, properties: {step_index, target_name, timestamp}`
- `tutorial.completed: Fired when user finishes all steps, properties: {total_duration_ms, timestamp}`

### E005-F004-S001-T001-A001 — H001-PROVIDER: HookProvider Enum Implementation

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Multi-CLI Hook Architecture
> **Feature:** E005-F004: HookProvider Enum and Provider Abstraction
> **Story:** E005-F004-S001: Implement HookProvider enum for multi-CLI hook support
> **Task:** E005-F004-S001-T001: Create HookProvider enum with provider properties

#### Problem Statement
The current hooks implementation is Claude-specific with hardcoded paths and event types. To support Gemini CLI and OpenAI Codex CLI, we need a provider abstraction that encapsulates: (1) whether the provider supports hooks at all, (2) the config directory name for that provider, (3) the settings filename convention, and (4) the available hook events for each provider. Without this abstraction, adding new providers would require scattered conditionals throughout the codebase.

#### Description
Create the foundational HookProvider enum in Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift that defines provider cases and their associated configuration. This enum serves as the single source of truth for provider-specific hook capabilities and paths throughout the application.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Define HookProvider enum with claude, gemini, codex cases
- Implement supportsHooks computed property returning Bool based on provider capability
- Implement configDirectoryName computed property returning provider-specific directory string
- Implement settingsFilename computed property returning settings.json constant
- Implement events computed property returning array of HookEventDefinition for each provider
- Add Codable conformance for serialization in settings
- Add CaseIterable conformance for UI iteration
- Add RawValue String conformance for display and logging

**Out of Scope:**
- HookEventDefinition types themselves (covered by H002-SCHEMA atom)
- ClaudeHookEvents.all and GeminiHookEvents.all constants (covered by H002-SCHEMA atom)
- MultiProviderHooksService actor (covered by H003-SERVICE atom)
- HookRunner provider parameter modification (covered by H004-RUNNER atom)
- UI components for provider selection (covered by H005-UIPROVIDER atom)
- Hook description field implementation (covered by H006-DESCRIPTION atom)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-001: HookProvider enum SHALL define exactly three cases: claude, gemini, codex
1. FR-002: supportsHooks property SHALL return true for claude and gemini, false for codex
1. FR-003: configDirectoryName property SHALL return .claude for claude case, .gemini for gemini case, .codex for codex case
1. FR-004: settingsFilename property SHALL return settings.json for all cases
1. FR-005: events property SHALL return ClaudeHookEvents.all for claude case
1. FR-006: events property SHALL return GeminiHookEvents.all for gemini case
1. FR-007: events property SHALL return empty array for codex case
1. FR-008: Enum SHALL conform to Codable protocol for JSON serialization
1. FR-009: Enum SHALL conform to CaseIterable protocol for iteration
1. FR-010: Enum raw value type SHALL be String for human-readable serialization

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-001: Enum instantiation and property access SHALL complete in under 1 microsecond
- NFR-002: Memory footprint of HookProvider instance SHALL be 8 bytes or less (single String pointer)
- NFR-003: Code SHALL compile without warnings on Swift 5.9+
- NFR-004: File SHALL have 100% documentation coverage with DocC comments

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create new file Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift with standard header comment
1. Step 2: Add import Foundation statement
1. Step 3: Define enum HookProvider: String, Codable, CaseIterable with cases claude, gemini, codex
1. Step 4: Implement supportsHooks computed property with switch statement returning appropriate Bool
1. Step 5: Implement configDirectoryName computed property with switch statement returning directory strings
1. Step 6: Implement settingsFilename computed property returning settings.json constant
1. Step 7: Implement events computed property with switch statement returning appropriate HookEventDefinition arrays
1. Step 8: Add DocC documentation comments for enum and all public properties
1. Step 9: Add MARK comments for code organization
1. Step 10: Verify file compiles without errors or warnings

#### Files
**Files Touched:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift`

**New Files:**
- `Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift`

#### Commands
```bash
swift build --target Blaze 2>&1 | head -50
swift test --filter HookProviderTests
swiftlint lint Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift
```

#### Data Model Changes
- New enum type HookProvider added to Core/Hooks module
- HookProvider.RawValue is String type
- HookProvider conforms to Codable, CaseIterable protocols

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- HookProvider.claude.rawValue returns claude string
- HookProvider.gemini.rawValue returns gemini string
- HookProvider.codex.rawValue returns codex string
- HookProvider.allCases returns array of all three cases in declaration order

**Event Contracts:**
- No events emitted by this atom (enum is passive data type)
- Events property returns HookEventDefinition array but does not emit events itself

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: Decoding unknown provider string from JSON should fail gracefully with DecodingError
- Edge case 2: Future provider addition should only require adding new case and implementing computed properties
- Edge case 3: Empty events array for codex should be handled by callers without crashing
- Edge case 4: Config directory names must not contain path separators or special characters
- Edge case 5: Raw value string must match case name exactly for predictable serialization

#### Failure Modes
- FM-001: If ClaudeHookEvents or GeminiHookEvents types are not defined, compilation fails with undefined symbol error - Mitigation: Ensure H002-SCHEMA atom is completed first or use forward declaration
- FM-002: If events property returns nil instead of empty array, callers may crash on force unwrap - Mitigation: Return empty array explicitly for unsupported providers
- FM-003: If raw value string differs from case name, JSON round-trip may produce unexpected results - Mitigation: Use implicit raw values (no explicit assignment)

Delete Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift file. Remove any imports of HookProvider from dependent files. Revert to hardcoded Claude-only paths in existing code. No data migration required as this is a new type with no persistent storage.

- Test HookProvider.allCases enumeration completes in under 10 microseconds

**Security:**

- Test raw values cannot be manipulated to inject arbitrary strings

### E005-F005-S001-T001-A001 — C001-TYPES: CLI Type Definitions

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Onboarding and CLI Management
> **Feature:** E005-F005: CLI Detection and Installation
> **Story:** E005-F005-S001: Implement CLI type definitions and installation infrastructure
> **Task:** E005-F005-S001-T001: Create CLITypes.swift with CLI type definitions

#### Problem Statement
The onboarding flow needs to detect which agentic coding CLIs are installed and offer to install missing ones. Currently there is no unified model for CLI tools - we need a type-safe enum that captures: (1) the executable name for shell detection, (2) version flag for checking installation, (3) human-readable display name and description, (4) whether the tool is recommended for new users, (5) runtime dependencies like Node.js or Python, and (6) the appropriate install command (npm, pip, brew, etc.). Without this model, detection and installation logic would be scattered and inconsistent across the codebase.

#### Description
Create CLITypes.swift containing the CLIType enum with eight cases (claude, codex, gemini, aider, cursor, cody, opencode, amp) and comprehensive computed properties for each. Also define DependencyType enum for runtime prerequisites and InstallCommand enum for installation method variants. This atom is the foundation of the CLI installation service - all detection, installation, and UI components depend on these type definitions.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Define CLIType enum with cases for claude, codex, gemini, aider, cursor, cody, opencode, amp
- Implement displayName computed property returning human-readable name for each CLI
- Implement executable computed property returning the shell command name for each CLI
- Implement versionFlag computed property returning the flag to check version (typically --version)
- Implement description computed property returning one-sentence explanation of each CLI
- Implement isRecommended computed property returning Bool indicating if CLI is recommended for beginners
- Implement dependencies computed property returning array of DependencyType values
- Implement installCommand computed property returning InstallCommand enum case with install parameters
- Define DependencyType enum with cases for nodejs, python, rust runtime prerequisites
- Define InstallCommand enum with associated values for npm, pip, brew, cask, and shell installation methods
- Add Codable conformance to CLIType for persistence in settings
- Add CaseIterable conformance to CLIType for UI iteration
- Add Hashable conformance to CLIType for use as Dictionary keys and in Sets
- Add RawValue String conformance to CLIType for serialization

**Out of Scope:**
- CLIInstallationService actor implementation (covered by C002-SERVICE atom)
- CLISetupState state machine (covered by C003-STATE atom)
- OnboardingCLISetupView UI component (covered by C004-VIEW atom)
- InstallationProgressView component (covered by C005-PROGRESS atom)
- CLISetupViewModel orchestration (covered by C006-VIEWMODEL atom)
- Actual shell execution of detection or installation commands
- Network operations for downloading CLI tools
- Error handling for failed installations (handled by service layer)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-001: CLIType enum SHALL define exactly eight cases: claude, codex, gemini, aider, cursor, cody, opencode, amp
1. FR-002: displayName property SHALL return human-readable strings: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider, Cursor, Cody, OpenCode, Amp
1. FR-003: executable property SHALL return binary names: claude, codex, gemini, aider, cursor, cody, opencode, amp
1. FR-004: versionFlag property SHALL return --version for all CLIs
1. FR-005: description property SHALL return one-sentence description for each CLI tool
1. FR-006: isRecommended property SHALL return true for claude and gemini, false for others
1. FR-007: dependencies property SHALL return appropriate DependencyType array: claude and codex require nodejs, aider requires python, others return empty array
1. FR-008: installCommand property SHALL return appropriate InstallCommand case with correct package names
1. FR-009: DependencyType enum SHALL define cases for nodejs, python, rust
1. FR-010: InstallCommand enum SHALL define cases with associated values: npm(package: String), pip(package: String), brew(formula: String), cask(name: String), shell(script: String)
1. FR-011: CLIType SHALL conform to Codable for JSON serialization
1. FR-012: CLIType SHALL conform to CaseIterable for ForEach iteration
1. FR-013: CLIType SHALL conform to Hashable for Dictionary key usage
1. FR-014: DependencyType SHALL conform to Codable and Hashable
1. FR-015: InstallCommand SHALL conform to Codable

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-001: Enum property access SHALL complete in under 1 microsecond
- NFR-002: Memory footprint of CLIType instance SHALL be minimal (8 bytes for enum tag)
- NFR-003: Code SHALL compile without warnings on Swift 5.9 and Swift 6.0
- NFR-004: File SHALL have DocC documentation for all public types and properties
- NFR-005: Code SHALL follow Swift API Design Guidelines for naming

- CLIType.claude.executable returns claude string
- CLIType.claude.versionFlag returns --version string
- CLIType.claude.description returns descriptive string about Claude Code CLI
- CLIType.claude.isRecommended returns true

- CLIType.claude.installCommand returns .npm(package: @anthropic-ai/claude-code)

**Event Contracts:**

#### UI States

#### UI Interactions
- N/A - Model layer types have no UI interactions

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: CLI executable name may differ on some systems (e.g., claude vs claude-code) - executable property returns canonical name
- Edge case 2: Install command packages may change versions - use package name without version specifier
- Edge case 3: Some tools have multiple installation methods - installCommand returns the primary recommended method
- Edge case 4: Decoding unknown CLIType string from JSON should throw DecodingError.dataCorrupted
- Edge case 5: InstallCommand associated value strings may contain special characters - ensure proper encoding
- Edge case 6: Empty dependencies array is valid for tools with no runtime prerequisites
- Edge case 7: Future CLI tools may require additional DependencyType cases - enum is extensible
- Edge case 8: shell(script:) case may contain multi-line scripts - String should preserve newlines

#### Failure Modes
- FM-001: If executable name is wrong, detection will fail silently - Mitigation: Verify executable names against current CLI documentation before release
- FM-002: If install command package name is incorrect, installation will fail - Mitigation: Test installation commands on clean macOS system
- FM-003: If InstallCommand Codable implementation has bugs, settings persistence fails - Mitigation: Comprehensive unit tests for encode/decode round-trip
- FM-004: If DependencyType is missing a case, certain CLIs cannot express their requirements - Mitigation: Review all CLI documentation for prerequisites
- FM-005: If versionFlag is wrong for a CLI, version detection returns error - Mitigation: All major CLIs use --version, verify before adding new ones

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Models/CLITypes.swift file. Remove any imports of CLIType, DependencyType, or InstallCommand from dependent files (should be none if this is the first atom). No data migration required as this is a new type with no persistent storage yet.

### E005-F005-S001-T002-A001 — C002-SERVICE: CLIInstallationService Actor Implementation

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Onboarding and CLI Integration
> **Feature:** E005-F005: CLI Detection and Installation
> **Story:** E005-F005-S001: Implement CLI detection and installation infrastructure
> **Task:** E005-F005-S001-T002: Create CLIInstallationService actor

#### Problem Statement
Blaze needs to detect and install multiple agentic coding CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, etc.) during onboarding. Each CLI has different detection methods (checking PATH, version commands), dependencies (Node.js, Python, Rust), and installation mechanisms (npm, pip, brew, shell scripts). Without a centralized service actor, this logic would be scattered across view models and views, making it untestable, non-thread-safe, and difficult to maintain. The service must handle concurrent detection of multiple CLIs, sequential installation with progress tracking, cancellation support, and graceful error recovery.

#### Description
Create the CLIInstallationService actor in Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Services/CLIInstallationService.swift that orchestrates CLI detection and installation. This actor is the core business logic layer for the CLI setup feature, coordinating between CLIType definitions, shell command execution, and progress reporting.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- Define CLIInstallationService actor with MainActor isolation for UI-safe state updates
- Implement detectAllCLIs() async method that scans PATH for all known CLI executables
- Implement detectCLI(type:) async method for single CLI detection with version extraction
- Implement checkDependencies(for:) async method that verifies required dependencies
- Implement installCLI(type:) async throws method that executes installation command
- Implement installMultipleCLIs(types:) async throws method for batch installation with progress
- Implement cancelInstallation() method to abort in-progress installations
- Define CLIDetectionResult struct with isInstalled, version, path fields
- Define CLIInstallError enum with detailed error cases
- Implement progress reporting via AsyncStream or Combine publisher
- Add dependency injection for shell command executor (testability)
- Implement detectUserShell() method to identify current shell (bash, zsh, fish)
- Implement updateShellPATH(for:shell:) method to append CLI paths to shell config
- Support bash (~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile), zsh (~/.zshrc), and fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish)
- Use shell-appropriate syntax: export PATH for bash/zsh, set -gx PATH for fish
- Implement searchHomebrewPackages(query:) async method to search for packages
- Implement installHomebrewPackage(name:withDependencies:) async method for full automation

**Out of Scope:**
- CLIType enum definition (covered by C001-TYPES atom)
- CLISetupState state machine (covered by C003-STATE atom)
- UI views for CLI setup (covered by C004-VIEW atom)
- Installation progress view (covered by C005-PROGRESS atom)
- ViewModel orchestration (covered by C006-VIEWMODEL atom)
- Homebrew installation if not present (manual prerequisite)
- Automatic dependency installation (user must install Node.js etc. manually)
- Shell configurations other than bash, zsh, fish (e.g., tcsh, csh)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-001: CLIInstallationService SHALL be declared as an actor with @MainActor isolation
1. FR-002: detectAllCLIs() SHALL return array of CLIDetectionResult for all CLIType.allCases
1. FR-003: detectCLI(type:) SHALL execute which command to find CLI path
1. FR-004: detectCLI(type:) SHALL execute version flag command to extract version string
1. FR-005: detectCLI(type:) SHALL return CLIDetectionResult with isInstalled, version, path fields
1. FR-006: checkDependencies(for:) SHALL verify each dependency in CLIType.dependencies array
1. FR-007: checkDependencies(for:) SHALL return array of missing DependencyType
1. FR-008: installCLI(type:) SHALL execute CLIType.installCommand via shell
1. FR-009: installCLI(type:) SHALL throw CLIInstallError on failure with underlying error
1. FR-010: installCLI(type:) SHALL verify installation success by re-detecting CLI
1. FR-011: installMultipleCLIs(types:) SHALL install CLIs sequentially to avoid conflicts
1. FR-012: installMultipleCLIs(types:) SHALL emit progress events via progressStream
1. FR-013: installMultipleCLIs(types:) SHALL continue on individual failure and aggregate errors
1. FR-014: cancelInstallation() SHALL set cancellation flag checked by install methods
1. FR-015: Service SHALL inject ShellExecutor protocol for testability
1. FR-016: detectUserShell() SHALL return ShellType enum (bash, zsh, fish, unknown)
1. FR-017: updateShellPATH(for:shell:) SHALL backup config file before modification
1. FR-018: updateShellPATH(for:shell:) SHALL use idempotent PATH additions (check before adding)
1. FR-019: searchHomebrewPackages(query:) SHALL return matching formulae and casks
1. FR-020: installHomebrewPackage(name:withDependencies:) SHALL install package and all dependencies

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-001: Single CLI detection SHALL complete in under 500ms
- NFR-002: Full detection scan of all CLIs SHALL complete in under 3 seconds
- NFR-003: Installation progress events SHALL emit at least every 5 seconds
- NFR-004: Service SHALL release resources on deinit (no retain cycles)
- NFR-005: Memory usage during installation SHALL not exceed 50MB
- NFR-006: All public methods SHALL have DocC documentation

#### Implementation Steps

#### Data Model Changes
- New actor type CLIInstallationService added to Onboarding/Services module
- New struct CLIDetectionResult with isInstalled, version, path fields
- New struct InstallProgress with cli, step, progress fields
- New struct ShellOutput with stdout, stderr, exitCode fields
- New struct InstallationReport with installed, failed, skipped arrays
- New enum CLIInstallError with notFound, dependencyMissing, installFailed, cancelled, timeout, permissionDenied cases
- New enum InstallStep with preparing, downloading, installing, verifying, complete, failed cases
- New protocol ShellExecutor for dependency injection
- New enum ShellType with cases: bash, zsh, fish, unknown
- New struct HomebrewPackage with name, version, description, dependencies fields

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CLIInstallationService.detectAllCLIs() async -> [CLIDetectionResult] - Scans for all known CLIs
- CLIInstallationService.detectCLI(type: CLIType) async -> CLIDetectionResult - Detects single CLI
- CLIInstallationService.checkDependencies(for: CLIType) async -> [DependencyType] - Returns missing deps
- CLIInstallationService.installCLI(type: CLIType) async throws - Installs single CLI
- CLIInstallationService.installMultipleCLIs(types: [CLIType]) async throws -> InstallationReport - Batch install
- CLIInstallationService.cancelInstallation() - Sets cancellation flag
- CLIInstallationService.progressPublisher: AnyPublisher<InstallProgress, Never> - Progress stream
- CLIInstallationService.detectUserShell() -> ShellType - Detects user's default shell
- CLIInstallationService.updateShellPATH(for: CLIType, shell: ShellType) async throws - Updates shell config
- CLIInstallationService.searchHomebrewPackages(query: String) async -> [HomebrewPackage] - Search packages
- CLIInstallationService.installHomebrewPackage(name: String, withDependencies: Bool) async throws - Install package

**Event Contracts:**
- InstallProgress event emitted on progressPublisher when installation step changes
- InstallProgress.step transitions: preparing -> downloading -> installing -> verifying -> complete/failed
- Progress events include cli field identifying which CLI is being installed
- Progress events include progress field (0.0 to 1.0) for determinate progress bars

#### Edge Cases
- Edge case 1: CLI executable exists but version command fails - return isInstalled=true with version=nil
- Edge case 2: CLI partially installed (executable exists but broken) - detect as installed, installation will overwrite
- Edge case 3: Network timeout during npm/pip install - throw CLIInstallError.timeout with 5-minute threshold
- Edge case 4: User cancels during download phase - check isCancelled flag and throw .cancelled
- Edge case 5: Permission denied during global npm install - throw CLIInstallError.permissionDenied
- Edge case 6: Homebrew not installed for brew formula - throw CLIInstallError.dependencyMissing(.homebrew)
- Edge case 7: Multiple CLIs with shared dependency (Node.js) - check dependency once and cache result
- Edge case 8: PATH does not include Homebrew paths - search common Homebrew locations directly
- Edge case 9: Version string in unexpected format - capture raw string, do not parse
- Edge case 10: Empty types array passed to installMultipleCLIs - return empty report immediately

#### Failure Modes
- FM-001: Process.run() throws if executable not found - Mitigation: Catch and convert to CLIInstallError.notFound
- FM-002: Shell command hangs indefinitely - Mitigation: Use Task.sleep with timeout and terminate process
- FM-003: Race condition on isCancelled flag - Mitigation: Actor isolation ensures serial access
- FM-004: Memory leak from Process not terminated - Mitigation: Always call terminate() in defer block
- FM-005: progressSubject subscriber not cleaned up - Mitigation: Use AnyPublisher wrapper, no strong refs
- FM-006: CLIType.installCommand returns .shell with malicious script - Mitigation: Only execute known commands from CLIType enum

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Services/CLIInstallationService.swift file. Remove imports from dependent files (CLISetupViewModel). Revert to manual CLI setup instructions in onboarding. Installed CLIs remain on system (no uninstall). No data migration required as service has no persistent storage.
