### E005-F006-S002-T003-A001 — Agents Selection View Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Remote Extension Registry
> **Feature:** F006: Registry Selection UI
> **Story:** Registry Item Selection Views
> **Task:** Implement AgentsSelectionView.swift

#### Problem Statement
During onboarding, users need to discover and select agents that automate common workflows. Without a dedicated agents selection view with use-case filtering, users would face an overwhelming unfiltered list, making it difficult to find agents relevant to their needs (e.g., a user focused on debugging wants to see debugging agents prominently, not wade through planning agents).

#### Description
Implement AgentsSelectionView in Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/AgentsSelectionView.swift as a SwiftUI view displaying available agents from the registry in a filterable grid layout. The view features a horizontal chip bar for use-case filtering (All, Planning, Debugging, Security, Research, Workflow), a search bar for text filtering by name/description, a LazyVGrid of AgentCard components showing agent name/description/required-skills/CLI-compatibility, checkbox-based multi-selection persisted to OnboardingViewModel.selectedAgents, and empty state handling when no agents match filters. View observes RegistryCoordinator for agent data and OnboardingViewModel for selection state.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- AgentsSelectionView struct conforming to View protocol
- Horizontal FilterChipBar component for use-case filtering with All/Planning/Debugging/Security/Research/Workflow chips
- SearchBar component for text-based filtering by agent name and description
- LazyVGrid layout with adaptive columns for responsive agent card display
- AgentCard component showing agent name, description, required skills, CLI compatibility badges, and selection checkbox
- UseCase enum defining Planning, Debugging, Security, Research, Workflow categories with displayName and SF Symbol icon
- Computed filteredAgents property applying both use-case and search filters
- Binding to OnboardingViewModel.selectedAgents for persisting selection state
- Binding to RegistryCoordinator.agents for accessing available agents
- Empty state view when no agents match current filters
- Loading state view while registry is fetching agents
- Error state view when registry fetch fails with retry button

**Out of Scope:**
- Agent installation logic (handled by RegistryInstaller in R004)
- Registry network fetching (handled by RegistryFetcher in R002)
- Agent detail modal or expanded view (future enhancement)
- Agent dependency resolution (handled by RegistryCoordinator in R005)
- Drag-and-drop reordering of selected agents
- Agent configuration or customization UI
- Agent version selection (always installs latest)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-01: View displays horizontal chip bar with use-case filters (All, Planning, Debugging, Security, Research, Workflow) at top
1. FR-02: Selecting a use-case chip filters displayed agents to only those matching that use case
1. FR-03: All chip shows all agents regardless of use case
1. FR-04: Search bar below chip bar filters agents by name and description substring match
1. FR-05: Search and use-case filters combine (AND logic) - agents must match both to display
1. FR-06: LazyVGrid displays AgentCard for each filtered agent with adaptive 3-column layout
1. FR-07: AgentCard displays agent name as title, description as subtitle, required skills as tag pills, CLI compatibility as badges
1. FR-08: AgentCard includes checkbox that toggles selection in OnboardingViewModel.selectedAgents
1. FR-09: Checkbox state reflects current selection - checked if agent.id in selectedAgents
1. FR-10: Tapping anywhere on AgentCard toggles selection (not just checkbox)
1. FR-11: Empty state view displays when filteredAgents is empty with message and clear-filters button
1. FR-12: Loading state view displays spinner and message while RegistryCoordinator.isLoading is true
1. FR-13: Error state view displays when RegistryCoordinator.error is non-nil with error message and retry button
1. FR-14: Selected agents count badge displays in navigation bar or header showing N selected

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-01: View renders initial agent grid in under 100ms with 50 agents
- NFR-02: Search filtering updates grid in under 50ms for responsive typing
- NFR-03: Selection toggle completes in under 16ms (60fps) for smooth interaction
- NFR-04: View must be accessible with VoiceOver announcing agent names and selection state
- NFR-05: View must support keyboard navigation between agent cards
- NFR-06: Memory usage must not exceed 10MB with 100 agents loaded

#### Implementation Steps
1. Create Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/AgentsSelectionView.swift with file header and imports (SwiftUI, Foundation)
1. Define UseCase enum with cases all, planning, debugging, security, research, workflow, each with displayName String and iconName String computed properties
1. Define AgentsSelectionView struct with @EnvironmentObject var viewModel: OnboardingViewModel and @EnvironmentObject var registry: RegistryCoordinator
1. Add @State private var selectedUseCase: UseCase = .all for filter chip state
1. Add @State private var searchText: String = empty string for search bar state
1. Add @State private var debouncedSearchText: String = empty string for debounced search
1. Implement computed var filteredAgents: [AgentItem] that filters registry.agents by selectedUseCase and debouncedSearchText
1. Implement body computed property with VStack containing filterChipBar, searchBar, and agentGrid
1. Implement filterChipBar as HStack of ForEach over UseCase.allCases creating FilterChip views with selection binding
1. Implement searchBar as TextField with magnifying glass icon and clear button, bound to searchText with .onChange debouncing to debouncedSearchText
1. Implement agentGrid as ScrollView containing LazyVGrid with adaptive GridItem columns (minimum 280pt)
1. Within LazyVGrid ForEach over filteredAgents creating AgentCard views with selection binding
1. Implement AgentCard as VStack with agent.name Text, agent.description Text, requiredSkills HStack of tag pills, forCli HStack of CLI badges, and selection checkbox
1. Implement checkbox as Image(systemName:) toggling between checkmark.circle.fill and circle based on viewModel.selectedAgents.contains(agent.id)
1. Add onTapGesture to AgentCard that toggles selection via viewModel.toggleAgentSelection(agent)
1. Implement emptyStateView as VStack with magnifying glass icon, no agents found message, and Clear Filters button
1. Implement loadingStateView as VStack with ProgressView spinner and Loading agents message
1. Implement errorStateView as VStack with exclamation mark icon, error message, and Retry button calling registry.fetchAgents()
1. Add .onAppear modifier to trigger registry.fetchAgentsIfNeeded()
1. Add .onChange(of: searchText) with 300ms debounce using Task.sleep updating debouncedSearchText
1. Add .animation(.easeInOut, value: filteredAgents) for smooth grid updates
1. Add accessibility labels to all interactive elements
1. Create FilterChip subview component with label, isSelected binding, and consistent styling
1. Create AgentCard subview component encapsulating card layout and selection logic
1. Add selectedCount computed property returning viewModel.selectedAgents.count
1. Add header Text showing Selected agents count when count greater than zero

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- AgentsSelectionView.init() - initializes view with environment objects
- UseCase.displayName: String - returns human-readable use case name
- UseCase.iconName: String - returns SF Symbol name for use case
- UseCase.allCases: [UseCase] - returns all use cases including .all
- AgentCard.init(agent: AgentItem, isSelected: Binding<Bool>) - initializes card with agent data and selection binding
- FilterChip.init(label: String, icon: String, isSelected: Binding<Bool>) - initializes filter chip
- OnboardingViewModel.toggleAgentSelection(_ agent: AgentItem) - toggles agent in selectedAgents set
- RegistryCoordinator.agents: [AgentItem] - published array of available agents
- RegistryCoordinator.isLoading: Bool - published loading state
- RegistryCoordinator.error: Error? - published error state
- RegistryCoordinator.fetchAgentsIfNeeded() - fetches agents if cache expired

**Event Contracts:**
- onboarding.agents.filter_changed - emitted when use case filter changes with new filter value
- onboarding.agents.search_changed - emitted when search text changes with debounced query
- onboarding.agents.selection_changed - emitted when agent selection toggles with agent id and new state
- onboarding.agents.view_appeared - emitted when AgentsSelectionView appears
- onboarding.agents.retry_tapped - emitted when error retry button tapped

#### UI States
- Loading: ProgressView spinner with Loading agents text centered in view
- Empty (no agents): Magnifying glass icon with No agents found message and Clear Filters button
- Empty (no match): Filter icon with No agents match your filters message and Clear Filters button
- Error: Exclamation mark icon with error message and Retry button
- Content: Grid of AgentCard components with filter chips and search bar
- Content with selection: Same as content with checkbox filled on selected cards and selection count badge

#### UI Interactions
- Tap filter chip: Sets selectedUseCase state triggering grid filter update
- Tap search bar: Focuses text field for typing
- Type in search bar: Updates searchText state with 300ms debounce to debouncedSearchText
- Tap X in search bar: Clears searchText to empty string
- Tap agent card: Toggles selection state for that agent in OnboardingViewModel
- Tap checkbox on card: Same as tapping card - toggles selection
- Tap Clear Filters button: Resets selectedUseCase to .all and searchText to empty
- Tap Retry button: Calls registry.fetchAgents() to retry failed fetch
- Keyboard arrow keys: Navigate between agent cards in grid
- Keyboard space/enter: Toggle selection on focused agent card

#### Edge Cases
- Zero agents in registry returns empty content state not error state
- All agents filtered out shows empty match state with clear filters option
- Search text with only whitespace treated as empty search
- Agent with empty requiredSkills array shows no Requires section
- Agent with empty forCli array shows warning badge Works with: Unknown
- Agent with very long name truncates with trailing indicator after 2 lines
- Agent with very long description truncates with trailing indicator after 3 lines
- Rapid filter changes cancel pending debounce timers
- Selection persists when filters change and re-match previously selected agent
- Network error during initial load shows error state with retry
- Network error during retry shows updated error message
- Agent appears in multiple use cases when tags contain multiple values
- Search matches partial word (e.g., debug matches debugging agent)
- Case-insensitive search (DEBUG matches Debugging Agent)

#### Failure Modes
- RegistryCoordinator.agents nil or empty on appear: Show loading then empty state
- RegistryCoordinator.error set: Show error state with message and retry
- OnboardingViewModel environment object missing: Fatal error in debug, graceful fallback in release
- Search debounce Task cancelled: Silently ignore, user typed more
- Toggle selection fails Set operation: Log error, do not update UI state
- Grid layout calculation overflow: Use minimum column width fallback

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/AgentsSelectionView.swift. Remove any OnboardingViewModel.toggleAgentSelection method if added solely for this view. No user data affected as selection state is in-memory only during onboarding flow. Onboarding flow continues to work with agents step skipped or showing placeholder.

### E005-F007-S001-T004-A001 — A001: Gantt Container View Component

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 2.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Visual Hooks Builder
> **Feature:** F007: Gantt-Style Timeline Visualization
> **Story:** S001: Hook Execution Timeline
> **Task:** T004: Implement Gantt Container View

#### Problem Statement
Hook execution timing and parallelism are difficult to understand from log-based or list-based views. A Gantt-style timeline visualization provides intuitive visual representation of hook timing, duration, and concurrent execution, but requires a well-architected container to coordinate multiple synchronized UI components.

#### Description
Implement HookGanttView.swift as the main container component that wraps the Gantt chart visualization, provides view mode toggle (list/gantt), time scale selector, scroll synchronization between sidebar and timeline, and coordinates child components (GanttRow, GanttBar, HookTooltip).

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- HookGanttView container component with NavigationSplitView layout
- View mode toggle binding (list view vs Gantt timeline)
- Time scale selector (1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1min, 5min per viewport width)
- Scroll synchronization between hook sidebar and timeline viewport
- Time axis header with tick marks and labels
- Viewport state management for pan and zoom interactions
- Coordination of child components via environment and bindings
- Integration with HooksBuilderState for hook data
- Depth toggle control allowing user to select visible nesting depth (1, 2, or 3 levels)
- @AppStorage property for persisting user's preferred depth setting
- Segmented picker or stepper for depth selection with labels: 'Flat', '2 Levels', '3 Levels'

**Out of Scope:**
- Individual GanttRow rendering logic (handled by G005-ROW)
- GanttBar animation and styling (handled by G006-BAR)
- Tooltip presentation and content (handled by G007-TOOLTIP)
- Hook filtering and search (handled by separate filter component)
- Export or screenshot functionality
- Printing or PDF generation

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-001: Container shall display toggle control to switch between list view and Gantt timeline view
1. FR-002: Container shall provide time scale selector with options: 1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1min, 5min per viewport width
1. FR-003: Container shall synchronize vertical scroll position between hook name sidebar and timeline viewport
1. FR-004: Container shall render time axis header with appropriate tick marks based on selected scale
1. FR-005: Container shall manage viewport bounds state for pan gestures
1. FR-006: Container shall pass selected time scale to child GanttRow components via environment
1. FR-007: Container shall coordinate with HooksBuilderState to receive hook definition updates
1. FR-008: Container shall support keyboard navigation between hooks when in Gantt mode
1. FR-DEPTH-TOGGLE: Container SHALL include depth toggle control for 1/2/3 levels
1. FR-DEPTH-PERSIST: Selected depth SHALL persist via @AppStorage('ganttDepth')
1. FR-DEPTH-FILTER: Gantt rows SHALL filter to show only events at or above selected depth

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-001: Scroll synchronization latency shall be less than 16ms (one frame at 60fps)
- NFR-002: Time scale change shall complete visual update within 100ms
- NFR-003: Container shall support VoiceOver with meaningful labels for all controls
- NFR-004: Memory footprint shall not exceed 5MB for 100 hooks in view

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create HookGanttView.swift file with basic struct conforming to View protocol
1. Step 2: Add @EnvironmentObject property for HooksBuilderState observation
1. Step 3: Implement ViewMode enum with list and gantt cases plus toggle binding
1. Step 4: Implement TimeScale enum with cases for each supported scale (1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1min, 5min)
1. Step 5: Add @State properties for selectedTimeScale, viewportOffset, scrollOffset
1. Step 6: Build NavigationSplitView with sidebar for hook names and detail for timeline
1. Step 7: Create time axis header view with tick marks computed from TimeScale
1. Step 8: Implement ScrollViewReader coordination for synchronized scrolling between panes
1. Step 9: Add toolbar items for view mode toggle and time scale picker
1. Step 10: Create TimeScaleEnvironmentKey and inject into child views
1. Step 11: Implement MagnificationGesture for zoom-to-scale conversion
1. Step 12: Add accessibility labels and traits to all interactive elements
1. Step 13: Write unit tests for TimeScale computations and viewport math
1. Step 14: Verify VoiceOver navigation flow through all controls

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- HookGanttView.init(hooks: Binding<[HookDefinition]>) - Constructor accepting hook binding
- TimeScale.tickInterval: TimeInterval - Computed interval between tick marks
- TimeScale.labelFormat: String - Date format string for tick labels
- ViewMode.toggle() - Mutating method to flip between list and gantt

**Event Contracts:**
- onTimeScaleChange(scale: TimeScale) - Published when user selects new scale
- onViewModeChange(mode: ViewMode) - Published when user toggles view mode
- onViewportPan(offset: CGPoint) - Published during pan gesture for scroll sync
- onHookSelected(id: UUID) - Published when user clicks a hook row

#### UI States
- Empty state: No hooks configured, show placeholder with add hook CTA
- Loading state: Hooks loading from configuration, show skeleton rows
- List mode: Traditional vertical list of hook cards
- Gantt mode: Timeline visualization with synchronized scroll
- Zoomed state: User has changed time scale from default
- Error state: Configuration parse error, show inline error banner

#### UI Interactions
- Click view mode toggle to switch between list and Gantt views
- Click time scale picker to select different scale option
- Scroll vertically in sidebar to scroll timeline in sync
- Pinch gesture on timeline to zoom in/out (adjust time scale)
- Click hook row to select and show details in inspector
- Press arrow keys to navigate between hook rows
- Press Cmd+Plus/Minus to adjust time scale via keyboard
- User taps depth toggle to cycle through 1/2/3 levels
- Gantt chart updates immediately when depth changes
- Depth setting persists across app launches

#### Edge Cases
- Zero hooks: Display empty state with add hook prompt
- Single hook: Render timeline with appropriate scale for single item
- Very long hook name: Truncate with ellipsis, show full name in tooltip
- Hooks spanning multiple viewport widths: Enable horizontal scroll
- Overlapping hooks: Stack vertically with z-index based on start time
- Negative duration (clock skew): Clamp to minimum 1ms display width
- Time scale at extremes: Prevent zoom beyond 1s or 5min bounds

#### Failure Modes
- HooksBuilderState not in environment: Fatal error with descriptive message
- ScrollView coordination fails: Fall back to independent scroll without sync
- Time axis tick calculation overflow: Clamp to safe bounds
- Memory pressure during large hook list: Implement lazy loading of off-screen rows

#### Rollback Plan
Revert HookGanttView.swift and TimeScale.swift files, remove integration from HooksBuilderView.swift, restore previous list-only view. No data migration required as this is purely a view component.

#### Notes
This container is the orchestration hub for the Gantt visualization. Keep it thin by delegating row rendering to GanttRow and bar animation to GanttBar. ### E005-F008-S001-T002-A001 — App-Server Lifecycle Manager Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** medium | **Estimate:** 2 days

> **Epic:** E005: Remote Extension Registry
> **Feature:** F008: Codex App-Server Integration
> **Story:** App-Server Lifecycle Management
> **Task:** Implement CodexAppServerManager.swift

#### Problem Statement
The Blaze harness needs to communicate with Codex CLI via its app-server mode for advanced scenarios like persistent sessions and structured event streaming. Without a dedicated lifecycle manager, the app would have to manually spawn processes, track PIDs, handle crashes, and coordinate shutdown - all error-prone operations that belong in a single responsible component. The manager must handle the daemon lifecycle reliably across app launches, backgrounding, and unexpected terminations.

#### Description
Implement CodexAppServerManager actor in Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerManager.swift providing full lifecycle control for the Codex app-server daemon. The manager handles process spawning via Foundation.Process, port allocation, health check polling via HTTP GET to /health endpoint, graceful SIGTERM shutdown with SIGKILL fallback, automatic restart on crash detection, and state machine transitions (stopped, starting, running, stopping, error). Exposes async methods start(), stop(), restart(), and observable @Published state for UI binding.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- CodexAppServerManager actor with Sendable conformance for thread-safe access
- AppServerState enum with stopped, starting, running, stopping, error cases and associated error info
- start() async throws method that spawns app-server process and waits for healthy state
- stop() async method that sends SIGTERM, waits grace period, then SIGKILL if needed
- restart() async throws method that stops then starts with exponential backoff on repeated failures
- healthCheck() async throws -> HealthStatus method polling /health endpoint
- State machine validation preventing invalid transitions like starting while already running
- Process spawning using Foundation.Process with stdout/stderr pipe capture
- Port allocation finding available port in configured range 9100-9199
- Automatic restart on unexpected process termination with configurable max retries
- Observable @Published state property for SwiftUI binding
- Delegate protocol for lifecycle event callbacks to adapter layer
- Configurable timeouts for startup, health check, and shutdown operations
- Logging of all state transitions and errors for debugging

**Out of Scope:**
- JSON-RPC communication protocol (handled by X001-ADAPTER)
- Event stream parsing (handled by X003-EVENTS)
- Session state persistence (handled by X004-SESSION)
- Port and auth configuration UI (handled by X005-CONFIG)
- Codex CLI binary installation or updates (external to Blaze)
- Windows or Linux process management (macOS only)
- Sandbox permission requests for process spawning (handled at app level)
- Multi-instance app-server support (single instance per Blaze app)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-01: start() must spawn Codex app-server process with configured port and JSON output mode
1. FR-02: start() must poll /health endpoint until 200 response or timeout exceeded
1. FR-03: start() must transition state from stopped to starting to running on success
1. FR-04: start() must transition to error state with descriptive error on failure
1. FR-05: stop() must send SIGTERM to process and wait up to gracePeriod seconds
1. FR-06: stop() must send SIGKILL if process does not exit within grace period
1. FR-07: stop() must transition state from running to stopping to stopped
1. FR-08: restart() must call stop() then start() with exponential backoff on repeated failures
1. FR-09: healthCheck() must return HealthStatus with latency, version, and uptime info
1. FR-10: Manager must detect unexpected process termination and attempt auto-restart
1. FR-11: Manager must respect maxRestartAttempts limit to prevent restart loops
1. FR-12: Manager must find available port by checking socket availability in range
1. FR-13: Manager must capture process stdout/stderr for logging and event parsing
1. FR-14: Manager must notify delegate of state changes for adapter coordination
1. FR-15: Manager must clean up zombie processes on app termination via atexit handler

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-01: State transitions must complete within 100ms excluding I/O waits
- NFR-02: Health check round-trip must complete within 1 second timeout
- NFR-03: Memory footprint of manager must not exceed 1MB including buffers
- NFR-04: Must handle 1000 rapid start/stop cycles without resource leaks
- NFR-05: All async operations must be cancellable via Task cancellation
- NFR-06: Logs must use OSLog with appropriate log levels (debug, info, error)

#### Implementation Steps
1. Create Blaze/Sources/Engine/ directory if not exists
1. Create CodexAppServerManager.swift with file header and imports (Foundation, OSLog, Combine)
1. Define AppServerState enum with cases: stopped, starting, running, stopping, error(AppServerError)
1. Define AppServerError enum with cases: binaryNotFound, portUnavailable, startupTimeout, healthCheckFailed, unexpectedTermination
1. Define HealthStatus struct with isHealthy (Bool), latency (TimeInterval), version (String?), uptime (TimeInterval?)
1. Define AppServerManagerDelegate protocol with methods: didChangeState, didReceiveOutput, didTerminateUnexpectedly
1. Define CodexAppServerManager actor with private properties: process (Process?), port (Int), state (AppServerState), restartAttempts (Int)
1. Add @Published state property using CurrentValueSubject for Combine observation
1. Implement private findAvailablePort() -> Int? checking socket availability in range 9100-9199
1. Implement private spawnProcess(port: Int) throws -> Process creating Process with codex app-server arguments
1. Implement private waitForHealthy(timeout: TimeInterval) async throws polling /health until success
1. Implement public start() async throws orchestrating spawn, health wait, and state transitions
1. Implement public stop() async sending SIGTERM, waiting grace period, then SIGKILL fallback
1. Implement public restart() async throws with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s) on failures
1. Implement public healthCheck() async throws -> HealthStatus making HTTP request to /health
1. Implement private handleProcessTermination() detecting unexpected exit and triggering restart
1. Set up Process.terminationHandler to call handleProcessTermination on unexpected exit
1. Implement private transitionState(to:) with validation preventing invalid transitions
1. Add OSLog logging for all state transitions and errors
1. Implement deinit calling stop() synchronously via DispatchSemaphore for cleanup
1. Add atexit handler registration to stop daemon on app termination
1. Write unit tests using mock Process for state machine validation
1. Write integration tests spawning real process for health check verification

#### Data Model Changes
- New AppServerState enum: stopped | starting | running | stopping | error(AppServerError) for state machine
- New AppServerError enum: binaryNotFound | portUnavailable | startupTimeout | healthCheckFailed | unexpectedTermination
- New HealthStatus struct: isHealthy (Bool), latency (TimeInterval), version (String?), uptime (TimeInterval?)
- New CodexAppServerManager actor: process (Process?), port (Int), state (AppServerState), restartAttempts (Int), delegate (AppServerManagerDelegate?)

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- CodexAppServerManager.start() async throws - spawns app-server and waits for healthy
- CodexAppServerManager.stop() async - gracefully terminates app-server process
- CodexAppServerManager.restart() async throws - stops then starts with backoff
- CodexAppServerManager.healthCheck() async throws -> HealthStatus - polls /health endpoint
- CodexAppServerManager.state: AppServerState - current lifecycle state (observable)
- CodexAppServerManager.port: Int - port number app-server is running on
- AppServerManagerDelegate.didChangeState(from:to:) - lifecycle state change callback
- AppServerManagerDelegate.didReceiveOutput(line:isStderr:) - process output callback
- AppServerManagerDelegate.didTerminateUnexpectedly(exitCode:) - crash notification callback

**Event Contracts:**
- codex.appserver.state_changed - emitted on state transitions with from/to states
- codex.appserver.started - emitted when app-server reaches running state with port number
- codex.appserver.stopped - emitted when app-server reaches stopped state
- codex.appserver.health_check - emitted on health check with latency and status
- codex.appserver.restart_attempted - emitted on auto-restart with attempt number
- codex.appserver.error - emitted on error with error type and description

#### UI States
- N/A - see na_justifications

#### UI Interactions
- N/A - see na_justifications

#### Edge Cases
- Codex binary not found in PATH - throw binaryNotFound error with helpful message
- All ports in range already in use - throw portUnavailable error listing tried ports
- App-server process exits immediately on spawn - detect via terminationHandler and report
- Health endpoint returns non-200 status - retry with backoff then fail with healthCheckFailed
- Health endpoint times out repeatedly - fail with startupTimeout after configured attempts
- Process ignores SIGTERM - escalate to SIGKILL after grace period
- start() called while already starting - return existing startup Task result
- stop() called while already stopped - return immediately without error
- restart() called rapidly multiple times - coalesce into single restart operation
- App terminated via Cmd+Q - ensure daemon stopped via atexit handler
- App force quit via Activity Monitor - daemon may orphan (documented limitation)
- System sleep/wake cycle - health check may fail temporarily, use retry
- Network interface change - localhost should remain stable
- Codex CLI updates while running - existing process continues until restart
- Port freed but immediately rebound - retry port detection
- Process spawns but health never succeeds - timeout and cleanup process

#### Failure Modes
- FM-01: Binary not found - user notification with install instructions link
- FM-02: Port conflict - retry with next port in range, then fail with list of tried ports
- FM-03: Startup timeout - stop spawned process, transition to error state, log details
- FM-04: Health check failure - retry 3 times with 500ms interval, then fail
- FM-05: Unexpected termination - auto-restart up to maxRestartAttempts, then fail permanently
- FM-06: SIGTERM ignored - SIGKILL after grace period, log warning about unclean shutdown
- FM-07: Too many restart attempts - disable auto-restart, require manual intervention
- FM-08: Process spawn permission denied - fail with sandbox permission error

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerManager.swift and Tests/CodexAppServerManagerTests.swift. Remove any imports or references from other files. No user data or configuration affected since manager is stateless code. If daemon was running, it will be orphaned until manual kill or system restart.

- test_maxRestartAttempts_preventsLoop - verify restart limit enforcement

**Integration:**
- test_spawnRealProcess_reachesHealthy - spawn actual codex process and verify health
- test_stopRealProcess_exitsCleanly - verify SIGTERM handling with real process
- test_healthCheck_returnsValidStatus - verify /health endpoint parsing

**Ui:**

**Perf:**

- test_healthCheckLatency_under1second - verify health check performance

**Security:**

### E005-F008-S001-T003-A001 — App-Server Event Stream Parser Implementation

**Severity:** P2 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 1.5 days

> **Epic:** E005: Remote Extension Registry
> **Feature:** F008: Codex App-Server Integration
> **Story:** App-Server Communication Foundation
> **Task:** Implement App-Server Event Stream Parser

#### Problem Statement
The Codex app-server emits real-time events via Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream to notify clients of ongoing activity such as token generation, tool invocations, and errors. The raw SSE stream contains untyped JSON payloads with Codex-specific field names and structures that differ from our unified NormalizedEvent schema used by the UI layer. Without a dedicated parsing and normalization layer, the adapter would need to embed parsing logic, the UI would need Codex-specific handling, and error recovery would be inconsistent. We need a focused event stream parser that translates the raw SSE stream into a clean AsyncSequence of NormalizedEvents that the rest of the application can consume uniformly.

#### Description
Implement CodexAppServerEvents actor in Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerEvents.swift providing comprehensive SSE stream parsing for the Codex app-server notification channel. The module receives raw SSE data lines from the adapter layer, parses event type and data fields per SSE specification, deserializes JSON payloads into strongly-typed Codex event structs, maps Codex-specific event types to the shared NormalizedEvent enum for UI consumption, handles malformed events gracefully with logging, manages event buffering during reconnection, and exposes an AsyncSequence-based API for downstream consumers. Supports all Codex app-server event types including prompt_started, token_generated, tool_call_started, tool_call_completed, error_occurred, and session_ended.

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- CodexAppServerEvents actor with Sendable conformance for thread-safe SSE processing
- SSE line parser following Server-Sent Events W3C specification (event, data, id, retry fields)
- Multi-line data field accumulation for events spanning multiple data: lines
- Event type dispatch based on event: field value with fallback to message type
- CodexEventPayload enum with associated types for each Codex-specific event structure
- CodexPromptStartedPayload struct with prompt_id, model, timestamp fields
- CodexTokenGeneratedPayload struct with token, prompt_id, is_final fields
- CodexToolCallStartedPayload struct with tool_name, tool_id, arguments fields
- CodexToolCallCompletedPayload struct with tool_id, result, duration_ms, is_error fields
- CodexErrorOccurredPayload struct with error_code, error_message, recoverable fields
- CodexSessionEndedPayload struct with reason, total_tokens, total_duration_ms fields
- NormalizedEvent mapping layer converting Codex payloads to AssistantDelta, ToolCallStarted, ToolCallCompleted, ErrorEvent, SessionEnded variants
- AsyncStream-based eventStream property for downstream consumption
- Event buffering during reconnection with configurable buffer size limit
- Last event ID tracking for reconnection resume support per SSE spec
- Malformed event handling with warning logs and skip-and-continue behavior
- Stream lifecycle callbacks for connected, disconnected, reconnecting states
- Event timestamp normalization from Codex epoch format to Swift Date
- Backpressure handling when consumer is slower than producer

**Out of Scope:**
- HTTP connection management for SSE endpoint (handled by X001-ADAPTER)
- App-server lifecycle management (handled by X002-MANAGER)
- Session state persistence (handled by X004-SESSION)
- App-server configuration (handled by X005-CONFIG)
- Retry and reconnection logic (handled by adapter layer)
- Event persistence to database (handled by SessionStore)
- UI rendering of events (handled by view layer)
- Authentication token handling (handled by adapter)
- WebSocket fallback transport (app-server uses SSE only)

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR-01: CodexAppServerEvents actor shall accept raw SSE data lines via feed(line:) async method
1. FR-02: Parser shall accumulate data: field lines until empty line signals event completion
1. FR-03: Parser shall extract event type from event: field, defaulting to message if absent
1. FR-04: Parser shall extract event ID from id: field and store as lastEventId for reconnection
1. FR-05: Parser shall ignore comment lines starting with colon character
1. FR-06: Parser shall deserialize accumulated data as JSON into CodexEventPayload enum variant
1. FR-07: Parser shall dispatch to appropriate payload struct based on event type string
1. FR-08: Parser shall convert CodexPromptStartedPayload to NormalizedEvent.promptStarted with mapped fields
1. FR-09: Parser shall convert CodexTokenGeneratedPayload to NormalizedEvent.assistantDelta with token as content
1. FR-10: Parser shall convert CodexToolCallStartedPayload to NormalizedEvent.toolCallStarted with tool info
1. FR-11: Parser shall convert CodexToolCallCompletedPayload to NormalizedEvent.toolCallCompleted with result
1. FR-12: Parser shall convert CodexErrorOccurredPayload to NormalizedEvent.error with error details
1. FR-13: Parser shall convert CodexSessionEndedPayload to NormalizedEvent.sessionEnded with summary
1. FR-14: Parser shall yield normalized events via eventStream AsyncStream property
1. FR-15: Parser shall buffer events during reconnection up to maxBufferSize limit (default 1000 events)
1. FR-16: Parser shall drop oldest events when buffer exceeds limit with warning log
1. FR-17: Parser shall provide lastEventId property for reconnection resume header
1. FR-18: Parser shall emit streamState changes (connected, disconnected, reconnecting) via stateStream
1. FR-19: Parser shall handle malformed JSON by logging warning and skipping event
1. FR-20: Parser shall normalize Codex epoch timestamps to Swift Date using Date(timeIntervalSince1970:)

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-01: Event parsing latency from feed() call to eventStream yield must be under 5ms
- NFR-02: Parser must handle 1000 events per second sustained throughput without dropping
- NFR-03: Memory footprint of parser excluding buffer must not exceed 100KB
- NFR-04: Buffer memory with 1000 events must not exceed 10MB
- NFR-05: Parser must be resilient to malformed input without crashing
- NFR-06: All async operations must support Task cancellation within 100ms

- CodexAppServerEvents.stateStream: AsyncStream<StreamState> - stream of state changes for monitoring
- CodexAppServerEvents.lastEventId: String? - last received event ID for reconnection header
- CodexAppServerEvents.setStreamState(_ state: StreamState) - updates connection state for buffer management
- CodexAppServerEvents.reset() - clears all internal state for fresh start
- CodexAppServerEvents.bufferCount: Int - current number of buffered events during reconnection

**Event Contracts:**
- NormalizedEvent.promptStarted - emitted when Codex begins processing a prompt with prompt_id and model
- NormalizedEvent.assistantDelta - emitted for each token with content string and is_final flag
- NormalizedEvent.toolCallStarted - emitted when Codex invokes a tool with tool_name and arguments
- NormalizedEvent.toolCallCompleted - emitted when tool execution finishes with result and duration
- NormalizedEvent.error - emitted on Codex error with code, message, and recoverable flag
- NormalizedEvent.sessionEnded - emitted when Codex session terminates with reason and stats
- StreamState.connected - emitted when SSE connection established and events flowing
- StreamState.disconnected - emitted when SSE connection lost
- StreamState.reconnecting - emitted when attempting to reconnect with buffering active
- StreamState.error(Error) - emitted on unrecoverable stream error

#### Edge Cases
- EC-01: Empty data field in SSE event - skip event with debug log, do not yield
- EC-02: Missing event type field - default to message type per SSE spec
- EC-03: Malformed JSON in data field - log warning with first 200 chars of data, skip event
- EC-04: Unknown event type string - parse as unknown(String) variant, normalize to generic event
- EC-05: Event ID with special characters - store as-is for reconnection header
- EC-06: Retry field present - log but ignore (retry logic in adapter layer)
- EC-07: Very large data field over 1MB - attempt parse, may fail with memory error, skip
- EC-08: Data split across multiple data: lines - accumulate correctly with newlines preserved
- EC-09: Rapid event burst over 1000/sec - apply backpressure via AsyncStream buffer
- EC-10: Consumer slower than producer - AsyncStream buffers, may drop if buffer limit policy set
- EC-11: Stream interrupted mid-event - discard incomplete pending data on reset
- EC-12: Empty line before any data - ignore, do not emit empty event
- EC-13: Comment lines interspersed - skip comment lines, continue accumulation
- EC-14: Timestamp in future - clamp to current time with warning
- EC-15: Timestamp is zero - use current time as fallback with warning
- EC-16: Tool arguments contain nested JSON - AnyCodable preserves structure correctly

#### Failure Modes
- FM-01: JSON decode failure - log warning with event type and error, skip event, continue processing
- FM-02: Unknown event type - normalize to generic NormalizedEvent.unknown variant, log info
- FM-03: Buffer overflow during extended reconnection - drop oldest events, log warning with count dropped
- FM-04: Continuation already finished - check before yield, log error if attempting to yield to finished stream
- FM-05: Actor reentrancy during rapid feed() calls - actor isolation prevents, but log if detected
- FM-06: Memory pressure from large events - rely on system memory warnings, no custom handling
- FM-07: Invalid UTF-8 in SSE line - String initializer handles, log warning if lossy conversion
- FM-08: Extremely long line without newline - URLSession line reading handles, may split

#### Rollback Plan
Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerEvents.swift and Tests/Engine/CodexAppServerEventsTests.swift. Remove imports from CodexAppServerAdapter.swift. The parser is stateless code with no persistent data, so removal is clean. Events already processed and persisted to SessionStore remain unaffected.

#### Test Plan

- test_parseLineType_eventLine_extractsType - verify event: prefix stripped and type returned

This parser is focused on correctness and robustness over performance. The SSE format is simple but has edge cases around multi-line data and comment handling. The W3C spec is the authoritative reference. Consider extracting generic SSEParser if needed for other providers. The normalization layer is critical for UI consistency across Claude, Gemini, and Codex engines.

## F009-Phase1-TypeSystem

_1 atoms in this phase_

| ID | Atom | Status | Priority | Risk |
|----|------|--------|----------|------|
| E005-F009-S001-T001-A001 | HookType enum with cases, computed properties, and template variables | planned | must | low |

### E005-F009-S001-T001-A001 — HookType enum with cases, computed properties, and template variables

**Severity:** P1 | **Status:** planned | **Risk:** low | **Estimate:** 0.5 days

> **Epic:** Advanced Hooks Builder
> **Feature:** Hook Type System Foundation
> **Story:** Implement core hook type enum and supporting structures
> **Task:** Create HookTypes.swift with HookType enum, HookDefinition struct, TemplateVariable, and HookValidationError

#### Problem Statement
The hooks builder UI needs a type-safe foundation to represent the three hook types supported by Claude Code (prompt, command, agent). Each type has different execution semantics, timeouts, and available template variables. Without this type system, the UI cannot provide accurate guidance, validation, or autocomplete for hook configuration.

#### Description
Define HookType as a String-backed Codable enum with prompt, command, and agent cases. Implement computed properties for displayName, icon (SF Symbol), description, defaultTimeout, and templateVariables. The templateVariables property returns type-specific TemplateVariable arrays documenting available substitution variables for prompt hooks ($TOOL_INPUT, $TOOL_RESULT, $USER_PROMPT, $TRANSCRIPT_PATH) and command hooks ($CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, $CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE).

#### Scope
**In Scope:**
- HookType enum with prompt, command, agent cases
- CaseIterable and Sendable conformance for SwiftUI iteration
- Computed displayName returning human-readable names
- Computed icon returning SF Symbol names for UI
- Computed description returning help text explaining each type
- Computed defaultTimeout returning seconds (30 for prompt, 60 for command, 120 for agent)
- Computed templateVariables returning type-specific TemplateVariable arrays
- TemplateVariable struct with name and description properties
- HookDefinition struct with id, type, timeout, prompt, command, agent, once properties
- HookDefinition.validate() method returning HookValidationError array
- HookValidationError enum with missingPrompt, missingCommand, missingAgent, relativePathWarning, invalidTimeout cases
- HookValidationError LocalizedError conformance with errorDescription
- HookValidationError.isWarning computed property to distinguish warnings from errors

**Out of Scope:**
- Hook event types (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.) - covered in separate atom
- Hook matcher patterns - covered in separate atom
- Hook persistence to settings.json - covered in separate atom
- Hook execution runtime - covered in separate atom
- Hook testing infrastructure - covered in separate atom

#### Functional Requirements
1. FR1: HookType.prompt case with displayName Prompt, icon brain, timeout 30s
1. FR2: HookType.command case with displayName Command, icon terminal, timeout 60s
1. FR3: HookType.agent case with displayName Agent, icon person.crop.circle, timeout 120s
1. FR4: HookType.prompt.templateVariables returns 7 variables ($TOOL_INPUT, $TOOL_INPUT.command, $TOOL_INPUT.file_path, $TOOL_INPUT.content, $TOOL_RESULT, $USER_PROMPT, $TRANSCRIPT_PATH)
1. FR5: HookType.command.templateVariables returns 4 variables ($CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, $CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE)
1. FR6: HookType.agent.templateVariables returns empty array
1. FR7: HookDefinition.validate() returns missingPrompt when prompt type lacks prompt string
1. FR8: HookDefinition.validate() returns missingCommand when command type lacks command string
1. FR9: HookDefinition.validate() returns missingAgent when agent type lacks agent string
1. FR10: HookDefinition.validate() returns relativePathWarning when command lacks $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and does not start with /
1. FR11: HookDefinition.validate() returns invalidTimeout when timeout outside 1-600 range
1. FR12: HookValidationError.relativePathWarning.isWarning returns true, all others return false

#### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR1: All types must be Sendable for thread-safe UI updates
- NFR2: Enum iteration via CaseIterable for picker population
- NFR3: Hashable conformance on HookDefinition for SwiftUI list identification
- NFR4: LocalizedError conformance for user-friendly error messages
- NFR5: Zero external dependencies - Foundation only

#### Implementation Steps
1. Step 1: Create file Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookTypes.swift with Foundation import
1. Step 2: Define HookType enum with String raw value, Codable, CaseIterable, Sendable conformance
1. Step 3: Add prompt, command, agent cases to HookType
1. Step 4: Implement displayName computed property with switch returning Prompt, Command, Agent
1. Step 5: Implement icon computed property with switch returning brain, terminal, person.crop.circle
1. Step 6: Implement description computed property with switch returning help text for each type
1. Step 7: Implement defaultTimeout computed property with switch returning 30, 60, 120
1. Step 8: Define TemplateVariable struct with Identifiable (id = name), Sendable, name and description properties
1. Step 9: Implement templateVariables computed property returning type-specific TemplateVariable arrays
1. Step 10: Define HookDefinition struct with Codable, Sendable, Identifiable, Hashable conformance
1. Step 11: Add HookDefinition properties: id (UUID), type (HookType), timeout (Int?), prompt (String?), command (String?), agent (String?), once (Bool?)
1. Step 12: Implement HookDefinition.init(type:) setting type and default timeout
1. Step 13: Implement HookDefinition.validate() method with type-specific validation logic
1. Step 14: Define HookValidationError enum with Sendable conformance and five cases
1. Step 15: Implement LocalizedError conformance with errorDescription computed property
1. Step 16: Implement isWarning computed property returning true only for relativePathWarning

#### Data Model Changes

- New HookDefinition struct with UUID id field

#### Contracts
**API Contracts:**
- HookType.rawValue maps to JSON string: prompt, command, agent
- HookDefinition JSON keys: id (UUID string), type (HookType rawValue), timeout (optional int), prompt (optional string), command (optional string), agent (optional string), once (optional bool)
- TemplateVariable.id equals TemplateVariable.name for Identifiable
- HookValidationError.errorDescription returns non-nil localized string

**Event Contracts:**

#### Edge Cases
- EC1: Empty string prompt (whitespace only) must trigger missingPrompt error
- EC2: Empty string command (whitespace only) must trigger missingCommand error
- EC3: Empty string agent (whitespace only) must trigger missingAgent error
- EC4: Command starting with / should not trigger relativePathWarning
- EC5: Command containing $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT anywhere should not trigger relativePathWarning
- EC6: Timeout of exactly 1 should be valid (boundary)
- EC7: Timeout of exactly 600 should be valid (boundary)
- EC8: Timeout of 0 should trigger invalidTimeout
- EC9: Timeout of 601 should trigger invalidTimeout
- EC10: nil timeout should be valid (uses default)
- EC11: HookDefinition with multiple validation errors returns all errors in array

#### Failure Modes
- FM1: Invalid JSON decode of HookType falls back to DecodingError.dataCorrupted
- FM2: Invalid UUID string in HookDefinition.id causes decode failure
- FM3: Unknown HookType raw value in JSON causes decode failure - no fallback case
- FM4: Memory pressure during large TemplateVariable array creation - unlikely given fixed small arrays
